FOUNDATIONAL BLACK AMERICA – PURSUING ETHNORACIAL PURITY AT THE EXPENSE OF POWER

An individual or a group pursuing their own identity can be interpreted as a sign of independence, self-awareness and maturity, suggesting they may be expanding beyond their cognitive baseline.

The self-view of the FBA (Foundational Black Americans) interest group is a normative perspective but is fashioned as binary framing. The new identity which seeks the noble goal of indigenization for American Blacks, which while factual, is foolishly pursued at the cost of fragmentation.

While I accept the premise that Black Americans are indigenous to the nation called the United States of America, I insist that the FBA movement like the BLM organization is nothing more than a grift.
Blacks once the largest minority group in the US have now been surpassed by Latin Americans whose numbers draw from a vast human pool ranging from Mexico in the Argentina in the south, where Blacks who were one third of that country’s population have been exterminated as a race. Black Americans as a matter of sheer demographics cannot compete with the rates of Latin growth.

Secondly, Latin migrants are not sympathetic to Black American causes as Blacks in Latin countries generally face discrimination and occupy the bottom tiers of the socio-economic scale.
The polarizing FBA strategy which divides Blacks based on background is asinine and idiotic. It seeks a phony ethnic and racial purity at the expense of power. And so once again, Anglophone Black Americans, who are the modern founders of democracy stand to be cheated out their legacy and heritage in the American and Americas Projects because like Moonshine, the FBA fools who divide the Anglophone Black nation are likely bought and paid to pretend they have tails and to make monkey sounds because a political party that collapse the nation’s borders have greased and promised them “reparations” once they return to power and this talk of foundational blackness is simply positioning for the time when “reparations” will begin to flow and their goal is to ensure that they and only themselves get paid while Gambol and his kin don’t get so much as a nickel for his non-native Haitian or Jamaican grandma, which brings me back to my original point that the whole thing is just a grift.

On a more serious note, regarding the makeup and origins of Black Americans I’ve added the following regarding the foundational roots.

Historical records documenting the migration of enslaved people from the Caribbean to the British mainland colonies are vast, though they vary wildly depending on the colony, the century, and the nature of the trade.
Because the movement of enslaved people within the Americas—often called the Intra-American slave trade—frequently involved individual colonial merchants, smuggling, and personal property transfers, the paper trail is distinct from the larger transatlantic trade. Historians and genealogists rely on several specific types of records to track this history:
1. Database and Shipping Registries
·
· The Trans-Atlantic and Intra-American Slave Trade Databases: Hosted on https://t.co/wjEUg2pxF3, these massive public databases aggregate centuries of shipping manifests, custom house records, and port logs. The Intra-American Database specifically tracks thousands of documented coastal voyages that brought enslaved people from Caribbean ports (like Bridgetown, Barbados, or Kingston, Jamaica) to North American ports like Charleston, Boston, New York, and Chesapeake Bay. [1, 2, 3]
· Port Custom House Books: Colonial ports required captains to declare their cargo to collect taxes. For example, British "Naval Office Shipping Lists" record the arrivals of ships from the West Indies into ports like New York and Boston, listing cargo counts of sugar, molasses, rum, and "Negroes."
·
2. Early Settler Manifests and "Headright" Grants
In the southern colonies, particularly South Carolina, enslaved people from the Caribbean were frequently brought over not by slave traders, but as the personal property of migrating plantation owners. [1, 4]
·
· Headright Records: To encourage settlement, the "Lords Proprietors" of South Carolina offered white settlers land grants based on the number of dependents and enslaved people they brought with them (e.g., 20 acres per enslaved male, 10 per female). Land patent books and warrant registries explicitly record the names of white Barbadian planters claiming acreage for the enslaved Afro-Barbadians they brought to Charles Town in the 1670s. [5, 6, 7]
· Letters and Official Dispatches: Personal logs and letters from colonial officials capture these arrivals. For instance, historical documents note that South Carolina's first governor, William Sayle, brought four Black people with him from the Caribbean in 1670. Later that year, Captain Henry Brayne documented returning from a supply run with "one lusty negro man". [4, 5, 8]
·
3. State and Local Legal Archives
Because enslaved people were legally classified as property, their forced migration is heavily documented in local civil records rather than humanitarian ones: [9]
·
· Bills of Sale and Deeds: Local county courthouses hold property deeds recording the sale of enslaved individuals who were explicitly noted as "seasoned" (meaning they had already survived the disease environment and forced labor system of the Caribbean) or "born in the West Indies."
· Probate and Wills: Wealthy planters moving between the islands and the mainland left meticulous wills. A Barbadian planter might leave his estate in Barbados to one son, but bequeath "ten Negroes now serving on my plantation in Carolina" to another.
·
4. Newspaper Advertisements
·
· Runaway Slave Ads: In the 1700s, colonial newspapers (like the South Carolina Gazette or The Boston News-Letter) regularly published ads for escaped enslaved people. Masters frequently included critical biographical details to aid capture, writing descriptions such as: "Spokes English with a West India accent," "Lately imported from Jamaica," or "Is known to have family in Barbados."
· Auction and Cargo Notices:Merchants placed prominent ads announcing the arrival of ships from the Caribbean, listing items like "A prime parcel of Negroes, chiefly boys and girls, seasoned to the West Indies." [10]
·
5. Former British Colonies Enslavement Registers (1812–1834)
Though compiled much later—after the British abolished the international slave trade in 1807—the British government mandated meticulous registries to track the enslaved population in its colonies to prevent illegal smuggling. Available through resources like the National Archives (UK)and , these registers record an individual's name, age, owner, and crucially, whether they were born in Africa or the Caribbean, allowing historians to retroactively trace family lines that shifted between the islands and the mainland. [11, 12]

The first recorded arrivals of enslaved people from Barbados to the mainland American colonies occurred in two distinct historic waves, depending on the region:
1. The Earliest Arrival: Boston, Massachusetts (1638)
The very first documented arrival of enslaved Africans from Barbados to a mainland British colony occurred in New England. [1]
·
· The Ship: In February 1638, the built-in-America slave ship named the Desire sailed into Boston Harbor.
· The Cargo: After a voyage to the West Indies, the ship returned to Massachusetts carrying a cargo of salt, cotton, tobacco, and enslaved Africans purchased in Barbados. [1]
·
2. The Systemic Plantation Arrival: Charleston, South Carolina (1670)
While 1638 marks the earliest recorded arrival, the foundational arrival that imported the "Barbados Blueprint" (the systemic plantation model) to the American South occurred three decades later. [2]
·
· The Founding Voyage: In April 1670, the ship Carolina arrived at Albemarle Point to establish Charles Towne (Charleston) on behalf of England. [3, 4]
· The Scale: Over half of South Carolina’s original white settlers migrated directly from Barbados, and they brought enslaved Africans with them to clear the land and construct the new colony. [5, 6]
· The Impact: This 1670 arrival immediately implemented Barbadian chattel slavery on mainland soil, establishing South Carolina as the first colony engineered from its inception as a dedicated "slave society". [7, 8]

Estimating the exact percentage of enslaved people in the United States who descended from West Indian slaves requires looking at two different figures: the raw percentage of arrivals from the Caribbean versus the generational exponential growth (the "founder effect") of those early populations.
While only 13% to 15%of all enslaved people brought to mainland North America arrived via the West Indies, the timeline of their arrival means that by 1860, the vast majority (potentially 50% to 75%+) of the enslaved population in the American South likely carried West Indian ancestry. [1]
The breakdown of this historical estimate involves several key factors:
1. The Importation Percentage (13% – 15%)
According to data from the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database, the total number of enslaved Africans who arrived in what is now the United States is estimated at roughly 450,000. [1]
·
· Directly from Africa: About 388,000 captives were shipped directly.
· Via the West Indies (The Inter-American Trade): Between 60,000 and 70,000 enslaved people were transshipped from Caribbean islands like Barbados and Jamaica.
· Thus, mathematically, West Indian imports made up roughly 13.3% to 15.5% of the foundational gene pool. [1, 2]
·
2. The Early "Founder Effect" (1638–1700)
The impact of West Indian slaves is drastically magnified because they arrived first.
·
· Enslaved people coming from Barbados in 1638 (Boston) and 1670 (South Carolina) arrived generations before the peak of the direct trans-Atlantic slave trade to the mainland (which peaked in the mid-to-late 18th century). [3]
· Because they were the "founders" of the colonial enslaved communities, their lineages had an extra 50 to 100 years to multiply compared to Africans who arrived in the late 1700s.
·
3. Natural Population Growth vs. The Caribbean
The demographic trajectory of mainland North America was entirely unique compared to the rest of the Americas: [4]
·
· In the West Indies: Enslaved populations experienced negative growth rates due to brutal labor, disease, and high mortality, requiring constant new imports from Africa. [4, 5]
· In the U.S. Mainland: The enslaved population experienced robust natural self-reproduction. A population that started with a few thousand early colonial laborers (heavily drawn from Barbados) naturally exploded to 4 million people by 1860. [4, 6, 7]
·
4. Regional Concentration in the American South
If you isolate the Deep South, the percentage of descendants spikes dramatically:
·
· In South Carolina and Georgia, the plantation elite ("Goose Creek Men") migrated en masse from Barbados, bringing their enslaved laborers with them.
· Because intermarriage and family blending occurred continuously over 200 years on Southern plantations, it is demographically highly probable that by the onset of the Civil War, nearly every enslaved person in the Lowcountry of South Carolina and Georgia was a direct descendant of those original West Indian cohorts.

· The Trans-Atlantic and Intra-American Slave Trade Databases: Hosted on https://t.co/wjEUg2pxF3, these massive public databases aggregate centuries of shipping manifests, custom house records, and port logs. The Intra-American Database specifically tracks thousands of documented coastal voyages that brought enslaved people from Caribbean ports (like Bridgetown, Barbados, or Kingston, Jamaica) to North American ports like Charleston, Boston, New York, and Chesapeake Bay. [1, 2, 3]
· Port Custom House Books: Colonial ports required captains to declare their cargo to collect taxes. For example, British "Naval Office Shipping Lists" record the arrivals of ships from the West Indies into ports like New York and Boston, listing cargo counts of sugar, molasses, rum, and "Negroes."
·
2. Early Settler Manifests and "Headright" Grants
In the southern colonies, particularly South Carolina, enslaved people from the Caribbean were frequently brought over not by slave traders, but as the personal property of migrating plantation owners. [1, 4]
·
· Headright Records: To encourage settlement, the "Lords Proprietors" of South Carolina offered white settlers land grants based on the number of dependents and enslaved people they brought with them (e.g., 20 acres per enslaved male, 10 per female). Land patent books and warrant registries explicitly record the names of white Barbadian planters claiming acreage for the enslaved Afro-Barbadians they brought to Charles Town in the 1670s. [5, 6, 7]
· Letters and Official Dispatches: Personal logs and letters from colonial officials capture these arrivals. For instance, historical documents note that South Carolina's first governor, William Sayle, brought four Black people with him from the Caribbean in 1670. Later that year, Captain Henry Brayne documented returning from a supply run with "one lusty negro man". [4, 5, 8]
·
3. State and Local Legal Archives
Because enslaved people were legally classified as property, their forced migration is heavily documented in local civil records rather than humanitarian ones: [9]
·
· Bills of Sale and Deeds: Local county courthouses hold property deeds recording the sale of enslaved individuals who were explicitly noted as "seasoned" (meaning they had already survived the disease environment and forced labor system of the Caribbean) or "born in the West Indies."
· Probate and Wills: Wealthy planters moving between the islands and the mainland left meticulous wills. A Barbadian planter might leave his estate in Barbados to one son, but bequeath "ten Negroes now serving on my plantation in Carolina" to another.
·
4. Newspaper Advertisements
·
· Runaway Slave Ads: In the 1700s, colonial newspapers (like the South Carolina Gazette or The Boston News-Letter) regularly published ads for escaped enslaved people. Masters frequently included critical biographical details to aid capture, writing descriptions such as: "Spokes English with a West India accent," "Lately imported from Jamaica," or "Is known to have family in Barbados."
· Auction and Cargo Notices:Merchants placed prominent ads announcing the arrival of ships from the Caribbean, listing items like "A prime parcel of Negroes, chiefly boys and girls, seasoned to the West Indies." [10]
·
5. Former British Colonies Enslavement Registers (1812–1834)
Though compiled much later—after the British abolished the international slave trade in 1807—the British government mandated meticulous registries to track the enslaved population in its colonies to prevent illegal smuggling. Available through resources like the National Archives (UK)and , these registers record an individual's name, age, owner, and crucially, whether they were born in Africa or the Caribbean, allowing historians to retroactively trace family lines that shifted between the islands and the mainland. [11, 12]

The first recorded arrivals of enslaved people from Barbados to the mainland American colonies occurred in two distinct historic waves, depending on the region:
1. The Earliest Arrival: Boston, Massachusetts (1638)
The very first documented arrival of enslaved Africans from Barbados to a mainland British colony occurred in New England. [1]
·
· The Ship: In February 1638, the built-in-America slave ship named the Desire sailed into Boston Harbor.
· The Cargo: After a voyage to the West Indies, the ship returned to Massachusetts carrying a cargo of salt, cotton, tobacco, and enslaved Africans purchased in Barbados. [1]
·
2. The Systemic Plantation Arrival: Charleston, South Carolina (1670)
While 1638 marks the earliest recorded arrival, the foundational arrival that imported the "Barbados Blueprint" (the systemic plantation model) to the American South occurred three decades later. [2]
·
· The Founding Voyage: In April 1670, the ship Carolina arrived at Albemarle Point to establish Charles Towne (Charleston) on behalf of England. [3, 4]
· The Scale: Over half of South Carolina’s original white settlers migrated directly from Barbados, and they brought enslaved Africans with them to clear the land and construct the new colony. [5, 6]
· The Impact: This 1670 arrival immediately implemented Barbadian chattel slavery on mainland soil, establishing South Carolina as the first colony engineered from its inception as a dedicated "slave society". [7, 8]

Estimating the exact percentage of enslaved people in the United States who descended from West Indian slaves requires looking at two different figures: the raw percentage of arrivals from the Caribbean versus the generational exponential growth (the "founder effect") of those early populations.
While only 13% to 15%of all enslaved people brought to mainland North America arrived via the West Indies, the timeline of their arrival means that by 1860, the vast majority (potentially 50% to 75%+) of the enslaved population in the American South likely carried West Indian ancestry. [1]
The breakdown of this historical estimate involves several key factors:
1. The Importation Percentage (13% – 15%)
According to data from the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database, the total number of enslaved Africans who arrived in what is now the United States is estimated at roughly 450,000. [1]
·
· Directly from Africa: About 388,000 captives were shipped directly.
· Via the West Indies (The Inter-American Trade): Between 60,000 and 70,000 enslaved people were transshipped from Caribbean islands like Barbados and Jamaica.
· Thus, mathematically, West Indian imports made up roughly 13.3% to 15.5% of the foundational gene pool. [1, 2]
·
2. The Early "Founder Effect" (1638–1700)
The impact of West Indian slaves is drastically magnified because they arrived first.
·
· Enslaved people coming from Barbados in 1638 (Boston) and 1670 (South Carolina) arrived generations before the peak of the direct trans-Atlantic slave trade to the mainland (which peaked in the mid-to-late 18th century). [3]
· Because they were the "founders" of the colonial enslaved communities, their lineages had an extra 50 to 100 years to multiply compared to Africans who arrived in the late 1700s.
·
3. Natural Population Growth vs. The Caribbean
The demographic trajectory of mainland North America was entirely unique compared to the rest of the Americas: [4]
·
· In the West Indies: Enslaved populations experienced negative growth rates due to brutal labor, disease, and high mortality, requiring constant new imports from Africa. [4, 5]
· In the U.S. Mainland: The enslaved population experienced robust natural self-reproduction. A population that started with a few thousand early colonial laborers (heavily drawn from Barbados) naturally exploded to 4 million people by 1860. [4, 6, 7]
·
4. Regional Concentration in the American South
If you isolate the Deep South, the percentage of descendants spikes dramatically:
·
· In South Carolina and Georgia, the plantation elite ("Goose Creek Men") migrated en masse from Barbados, bringing their enslaved laborers with them.
· Because intermarriage and family blending occurred continuously over 200 years on Southern plantations, it is demographically highly probable that by the onset of the Civil War, nearly every enslaved person in the Lowcountry of South Carolina and Georgia was a direct descendant of those original West Indian cohorts.

Just arrived. Very excited to read it. Been reading it in English but some books need to be read in their original language. 

I should have read this decades ago!

Eim HaBanim Semeichah ("A Joyous Mother of Children") is a powerful and influential 1943 Jewish philosophical work written by Rabbi Yisachar Shlomo Teichtal during the Holocaust.

Rabbi Teichtal was originally a strict, traditional anti-Zionist Hasidic rabbi in Hungary and Slovakia who followed the belief that Jews should passively wait for God to bring the Messiah before returning en masse to the Land of Israel.

Witnessing the horrors and devastation of the Holocaust forced him to radically reevaluate his theology. 

He concluded that God was using the tragedies of Europe as a divine wake-up call for Jews to actively return to and rebuild Eretz Yisrael (the Land of Israel).

The book offers sharp criticism of ultra-Orthodox leadership and communities in America, ooops I mean Europe, for discouraging immigration to Israel and failing to participate in the practical rescue and settlement of the land.

The response to Eim HaBanim Semeichah was deeply polarized and remains highly controversial, particularly within the Orthodox world. 

Because the book was a scathing, direct critique of the ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) leadership from an insider, it provoked powerful, defensive reactions. 

Many of his contemporary co-religionists viewed the work with severe skepticism. Some communities went so far as to ban Rabbi Teichtal from entering their synagogues.

For decades following the Holocaust, in which he was murdered, and the creation of Israel, the book was actively ignored, suppressed, or kept out of mainstream Haredi yeshivas. 

Proponents of the status quo argued that Rabbi Teichtal wrote the book under extreme duress during the Holocaust, trying to invalidate its theological conclusions. 

Rabbis encouraging their congregations to stay in Europe despite the growing antisemitism. 

Why does that sound so familiar?

text:
Turkey’s ruling coalition just brokered a public truce between two of the country’s biggest crime clans.
On 26 September 2026, MHP leader Devlet Bahçeli hosted Sedat Şahin (Şahinler) and Burhanettin Saral (Sarallar) at party headquarters in Ankara. They shook hands in his office. MHP called them “two valuable families of our country” and a “historic embrace.”
The feud is about 20–22 years old and rooted in the Black Sea. It is traced to an October 2004 shooting of Zekeriya Kocaman, close to the Şahin side, and the January 2005 killing of Sarallar leader Hüseyin Saral in a Rome car park. Since then: gambling, extortion and targeted killings.
The timing is the striking part. On 10 September, Istanbul police said they had broken up a plot against Şahin linked to fugitive Sarallar figure Yakup Kerem Saral, who is under an Interpol red notice. Hidden in Beykoz among trees and plant pots: a rocket launcher, anti-tank rockets, Kalashnikovs and MP5s. Nineteen suspects were jailed, seven of them Iranian. Two weeks later the clans were posing with Bahçeli. On 25 September the Saral family held a meal for about 4,000 relatives in Sürmene, Trabzon. The formal reconciliation was the next day, in Bahçeli’s office.
Şahin later said he took the deal because Bahçeli asked him to: “I accepted the peace offered to me at the request of the esteemed Mr Devlet Bahçeli. I hope it lasts.”
Bahçeli, 78, leads the far-right Nationalist Movement Party, junior partner in Erdoğan’s People’s Alliance and the political home of the Grey Wolves. Turkish press noted Saral was roughly the sixth underworld figure photographed in that office.
From Dubai, Sedat Peker blessed it. Also under a red notice, he posted on Instagram that those who mediate peace are “among God’s most beloved servants,” and thanked Bahçeli by name. An MHP deputy chairman then called Peker a fellow nationalist and said he expected him home soon.
Rocket-launcher plot on 10 September. Family rally of 4,000 on the 25th. Handshake at the headquarters of a governing party on the 26th. Public thanks from a fugitive boss the next day. Whether this ends the blood feud or just realigns Turkey’s underworld is still open.

text:
On December 23, 1991, Cameron Todd Willingham’s wife, Stacy, left their Corsicana, Texas, home to buy Christmas presents, leaving Willingham with their three young daughters. A fire soon engulfed the house. Willingham escaped with burns, but his three daughters—two-year-old Amber and one-year-old twins Karmon and Kameron—died inside. Investigators quickly suspected Willingham, despite his insistence that the fire was accidental. They concluded that the fire had been deliberately set based on burn patterns, alleged “pour patterns,” melted materials, crazed glass and what they believed were multiple points of origin. Prosecutors argued that Willingham had intentionally killed his children, while a jailhouse informant later claimed Willingham had confessed. Willingham rejected a deal that would have spared him the death penalty if he pleaded guilty, maintained his innocence, and was convicted and sentenced to death. He was executed by lethal injection on February 17, 2004.

Then the science behind the conviction began to collapse. Fire scientist Gerald Hurst reviewed the case and concluded that many of the supposed signs of arson were not reliable indicators at all. Modern fire science had shown that phenomena such as low-burning patterns, “pour patterns,” crazed glass and melted materials could occur during an accidental house fire, particularly as temperatures and ventilation changed and the fire progressed toward flashover. Later, Craig Beyler, commissioned by the Texas Forensic Science Commission, reached an equally devastating conclusion: the original investigators had no sound scientific basis for determining that the fire was intentionally set. Multiple independent fire experts subsequently criticized the original investigation, saying it relied on outdated theories and fire-investigation folklore rather than validated science. The controversy became so serious that the Texas Forensic Science Commission examined the case and criticized aspects of the original investigation and testimony.

The case became even more troubling because the jailhouse informant, Johnny Webb, later claimed that Willingham had never confessed and alleged that prosecutors had offered him favorable treatment for testifying. Evidence concerning that alleged deal and Webb’s recantation became the subject of further controversy. Willingham, however, was already dead. Importantly, no court formally declared him innocent after his execution, so it is more accurate to say that the evidence used to convict him—particularly the arson science—was later seriously discredited, rather than claiming that his innocence was legally proven. His case remains one of America’s most notorious examples of how forensic evidence that appears highly scientific can be dangerously wrong—and how a mistaken interpretation at the beginning of an investigation can ultimately contribute to an irreversible punishment.

text:
GIVE US THIS DAY OUR DAILY DREAD
Thirty-one days of ghosts, strange tales and the occasional spectacular lack of common sense—all written with a bit of cheek, in typical Haunted Magazine fashion. Hey, there may even be the odd moral lesson, but expect a healthy helping of sarcasm, wit, and questionable subheaders.   

DAY 6: THE PIG-FACED LADY OF MANCHESTER SQUARE

PORKIES IN HIGH PLACES
A wealthy heiress, a silver trough and the London rumour mill going the whole hog.

London, 1815. Before anyone could blame social media for spreading absolute nonsense, the capital showed it could manage perfectly well with newspapers, print shops, and a bloke who knew a bloke.

The sensation was a mysterious young woman said to live in fashionable Manchester Square. She was wealthy, well connected and apparently possessed the head of a pig. Nobody seemed terribly concerned that the evidence was thinner than the ham in a co-op meal deal. 

There were pictures. There were stories. There was supposedly a fortune. Naturally, someone wanted to marry her.

THE ONLY WAY IS SNOUT
The rumours gathered momentum in late 1814 and early 1815. Manchester Square, despite the name, is in Marylebone, London. 

Surprisingly, versions differed. The woman was supposedly the daughter of a noblewoman; some accounts shifted the family connection to Grosvenor Square. A published description presented her as about twenty, Irish-born and from a wealthy family. 

She allegedly had an elegantly proportioned body, a pig-like face and a habit of eating from a silver trough. Her speech was described as grunting. A former attendant supposedly supplied the details, having left despite extraordinarily generous wages. 

The silver is a telling touch. Even in an outrageous urban legend, class distinctions had to be maintained. An ordinary wooden trough would never do. What would the neighbours think?

It was a wonderfully convenient arrangement for the publishers: a sensational eyewitness account from someone the reader could not readily question.

PICTURES, OR IT DIDN’T HAPPEN
Printed images gave the rumour a face. An 1814–15 broadside preserved at Princeton shows the supposed woman dining from a trough while a maid stands nearby. The Horniman Museum holds another 1815 broadsheet depicting an elegantly dressed woman with a pig’s head.

These are genuine historical objects. That does not make their subject a genuine historical person. A distinction worth remembering whenever somebody waves an image at you and declares the case closed.

The pictures helped make the story tangible. Here she was, dressed for dinner. Someone had drawn her. Surely someone must have seen her?

Well, someone had certainly produced something people could buy. These objects belong to a world of satire, sensational publishing and commercial curiosity. They tell us what circulated, not what a doctor [or vet] examined.

SITUATIONS VACANT: MUST ENJOY GOSSIP
On 9 February 1815, The Times had an advertisement from a young gentlewoman offering to become a companion to a woman with a severe facial difference.

She referred to a handsome annual income and an additional payment for staying seven years. The advert did not itself need to announce a pig-headed employer: the surrounding controversy linked it to the circulating story. 

Perhaps the applicant wanted to offer genuine care. Perhaps she primarily wanted the wages. We cannot inspect her motives from a classified advertisement.

Then came the prospective husband. A thirty-one-year-old gentleman sought an introduction to someone described as having a facial misfortune. He stressed his respectable family and honourable intentions. Yeah, right, of course he did.

Nothing says spontaneous romance like references and an awareness of the financial settlement. The Times refused his advertisement. Its contemporary response, reproduced in John Ashton’s later history of Regency England, said the offer had gone into the fire, and the accompanying pound would go to charity. 

The Morning Herald published a marriage-seeking advertisement instead. The press had found both a sensation and an argument about the sensation. A remarkably efficient business model.

THE TIMES GETS THE HUMP
The Times also admitted it had unwittingly printed the earlier companion advertisement. It then took a rather less accommodating view of the whole affair: “Our rural friends hardly know what idiots London contains.”

Strong words from a newspaper, although refreshingly economical. The editorial pointed out that similar stories had circulated decades earlier. London was not necessarily encountering a new marvel. It was encountering an old rumour in a fresh bonnet. 

There is a lesson here for all of us who enjoy strange stories: familiarity can feel like corroboration. You hear something repeatedly, and eventually forget that each version may descend from the same unsupported claim.

Ten sightings reported at the pub are not ten independent sightings if nine people heard it from Percy.

A CARRIAGE, A CROWD AND A VERY BAD EVENING
Captain Rees Howell Gronow later recalled another episode. During public illuminations celebrating peace, a crowd supposedly noticed a pig-like snout beneath a fashionable bonnet in a passing carriage near Piccadilly and St James’s Street. People called for the vehicle to be stopped. The driver hurried away.

The story then placed the carriage at Grosvenor Square. This is a retrospective account of a rumoured sighting. It does not identify a verified pig-faced passenger.

Perhaps a mask was involved. Perhaps a glimpse was misinterpreted. Perhaps the tale grew in the telling. The sources examined here do not settle it.

But imagine being the actual passenger, if there was one: strangers shouting, crowding your carriage and demanding a better look at your face.

The escape would hardly need a supernatural explanation. Nor would it prove you were hiding a snout. Sometimes people flee a mob because it is a mob.

THE BARONET’S ALLEGED BITE
Gronow also repeated a report involving a young baronet, Sir William Elliot. The story claimed that Elliot visited a grand house in Grosvenor Square, encountered the pig-faced woman and fled in horror. 

She supposedly pursued him and injured the back of his neck. A surgeon was named to give the tale a reassuringly specific finish.

The alleged incident even inspired a print called Beware the Pig-Stye. It is an excellent bit of sensational storytelling. 

In the material examined, it is not an independently verified attack. Adding a gentleman’s title and a surgeon’s address does not automatically turn gossip into a medical record.

A frightening encounter, an identifiable villain and something to sell afterwards. The machinery of a modern media frenzy was already in working order.

A VERY OLD PORK PIE
The Manchester Square rumour drew on a much older tradition. Seventeenth-century stories featured a woman called Tannakin Skinker. Other versions explained the supposed appearance through a curse: a pregnant wealthy woman insulted a beggar and her children, only to have the insult visited upon her own child. 

It was a moral warning about cruelty, delivered through a story that was itself cruel about physical difference. Some versions offered a more generous conclusion. A husband was asked to choose how his wife should appear; when he left the decision to her, the enchantment ended. 

Hidden among the grotesque imagery was a surprisingly sensible principle: allow the woman to decide something about her own life. An advanced concept for certain people in any century.

The legend also attached itself to real women. Dublin philanthropist Griselda Steevens became the subject of pig-faced rumours. Chambers’s Book of Days discusses her charitable work and the legend surrounding her, while rejecting the supposed porcine appearance. 

Doing something admirable was evidently no protection against becoming somebody else’s entertainment.

THE BEAR NECESSITIES OF FRAUD
The story had another unpleasant afterlife at fairs. Chambers described exhibitors presenting shaved bears, dressed and restrained in chairs, as pig-faced ladies. The Horniman’s modern account also identifies disguised animals among these attractions.  

That is evidence about a fraudulent exhibition practice, not proof that the Manchester Square rumour began with a particular bear.

It is also animal exploitation, however absurd the costume sounds. A paying audience’s curiosity was satisfied at the expense of a restrained creature.

The people selling the spectacle had a financial interest in customers seeing precisely what they expected to see. A useful question whenever somebody offers you a marvel for a modest admission fee.

THE MORAL OF THIS PARTICULAR PORK PIE
So, did a pig-faced heiress live in Manchester Square? The sources I have examined establish a substantial rumour, surviving prints, newspaper controversy and stories repeated by later writers. They do not establish that the woman described existed.

It remains possible that gossip exploited a real person with a facial difference. That possibility is not a diagnosis or an identification. The lessons are rather less elusive.

▪️Do not confuse an illustration with evidence. 
▪️Do not confuse repetition with independent confirmation. 
▪️Do not confuse another person’s appearance with permission to treat them as a public attraction.

Questioning an extraordinary claim need not involve humiliating anyone. Equally, sympathy need not require believing every extraordinary claim made about them.

Above all, ask who benefits. The Manchester Square story offered publishers customers, spectators excitement and prospective suitors the possibility of money.

The woman at its centre, real or invented, scarcely got a say. There may have been no monster in the carriage. Something ugly certainly lurked in the way people wanted to look inside. And London managed it all without Wi-Fi and social media.

The Sovereign Realist View: The Netherlands is a global agricultural marvel—the world's second-largest exporter of food by value. You noted the sharp contrast between the state bleeding its native middle class to fund foreign proxy conflicts while simultaneously absorbing millions of undocumented migrants onto the public purse. 

The Ponerological View (Ponerology is the study of evil and psychopathic rulers): 

To an unelected technocracy trying to build a centralized, post-national empire, organic national identity and social cohesion are major threats. A population with deep historic roots, shared cultural traditions, and high living standards will fiercely resist having their sovereignty signed away to central bankers and global organizations.

The Weaponized Migration Blueprint: 

By rapidly destabilizing the demographic fabric, the state creates an environment of perpetual social tension, economic strain, and institutional friction. The native population is forced to focus entirely on personal safety and local survival, distracting them from tracking the billions of Euros (Pounds in your case) being quietly siphoned away to fund defense cartels and financial restructurings.

4. The "Logocracy" of the New Status Quo

The most insidious part of the European blueprint is what Political Ponerology terms Logocracy—the total inversion of language used by a pathocratic elite to mask reality.

The destruction of physical energy security is called "Sustainability."

The forced elimination of food producers is called "Environmental Protection."

The managed collapse of the domestic standard of living is celebrated as "Global Solidarity." 

Ultimately, it is a game of consolidated control. The technocrats running the European apparatus are fully aware that their policies are causing an economic contraction, destroying the continent's competitive edge, and driving widespread public distress. They are executing it anyway because, in their grand chessboard model, an impoverished, fragmented, and resource-dependent European population is infinitely easier to govern than a prosperous, self-sufficient continent of sovereign nations. 

The recognition of institutional psychopathy—what Political Ponerology calls a pathocracy—is the only way to make sense of leaders enacting policies that actively diminish, impoverish, and destabilize their own native populations. When a system ceases to operate on human empathy or national preservation, it defaults to raw, mathematical control.

Ultimately, the choice you outlined—"live free or die"—is the historical pressure point that a pathocratic system eventually forces upon a population once the hyperreal  illusions fully wear off. In the friction of internal civil collapse in the UK, the raw physical reality of survival will always outlast the manufactured script of the managers. 

What THAT means - and it's happening right now - is that you are scheduled for total destruction, after which you will do what you're told just to survive. text:
2/2
This has always astounded me. What drives these rebels? Why is Christ still not enough for these nations? 

The simple answer, though not given, follows the pattern already outlined before by John. They will not have this King.

Satan doesn't create this army, he finds it. Nations that have lived for a thousand years under a visible Christly reign, with the liar sealed and the camp of the saints in front of them, still come up against the beloved city the hour they are invited to.

Christ has not been insufficient in this age. No atheist is running around arguing about the purple spaghetti monster in the sky. The King has come. The kingdom everyone was praying for has been established. The daily bread lives among them. They are not rebelling against a rumor. No one in that hour is weighing whether a King in heaven might exist. The daily bread is not a petition sent out into silence leaving only more hunger. It is the reign they have eaten under now for a thousand years. The camp of the saints is not a hidden church. It is the city they can see and then still choose to surround.

Toward what end?

What do they hope to gain?

How can they improve upon Christ's reign? What could possibly be lacking?

Here's the real moral of this story. They are not trying to improve his reign. They are trying to end it. They want His rule over them to be eliminated. There's no grievance that heaven failed to answer, they just don't want Him. They do not march to reform the kingdom. They march to displace the King.

What they hope to gain is the only thing his reign will never give them; the throne of God. And isn't that how all of this began? 

They want to be gods of their own making. Just like their first parents. 

The first word against the reign of God was not a complaint about bread. The garden was already full of everything they could ever want. The offer was, "you will be like God." Their first parents reached for a sovereignty that had not been given to them, and death entered by that reach for the forbidden fruit.

Satan finds them in that reach. He does not have to teach them the desire. They know what they want. He only has to tell them the hour has come to act on it.

The only thing lacking in this millennium age is their consent to be His creatures. He doesn't give them their emancipation, they instead look to take it. So He gives it to them in a sense, in the form of the annihilation of their relationship with Him. They are shut out of his reign, but they are still not rid of Him. What they receive is exclusion from the camp, the beloved city, and the face of his favor. That is real separation; no part in the kingdom, no light of his countenance, no daily bread from his hand ever again.

2 Thessalonians calls that destruction "away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his power."

So they get the loss they courted, and none of the liberty. All cowboy hat, no cattle. 

Fire ends the siege. The throne they marched to take stays His. The separation they receive is from His loving smile, not from the grip of His hand of justice. 

They refused the bread of his reign, and after the siege fails they meet his judgment. Now their daily bread is an eternity in the lake of fire. The books are opened. Whoever is not found written in the book of life is thrown into the lake.

It is finally finished for the nations that would not have this King. 

Next...all things are made new. 

Amen 🙏🏼

text:
She asks: "Why can't Europe just admit they made a mistake?" I'm going to answer this question for her as I'm an American living in Europe and have the financial and economic background as well as both perspectives. I have written on it often and have done quite a few interviews over the years discussing this very subject. Here it goes:
- Because admitting it means admitting the whole model failed.
- Early America offered real liberty and economic freedom. You came, you sank or swam on your own effort, no handouts. That incentive pulled the hardest workers and forged them into something. Europe did the opposite. Mainstream parties lured millions with free shit, betting they could flip them into the labor market fast enough to keep feeding the pension systems and the other Ponzi schemes that by design eventually run out of contributors. Lose the contributors and you lose the massive voting blocs those parties live on. So they used the cheap trick of the wrong incentives on the wrong people and hoped the math would hold. It DID NOT!
- The people never melted. No common language, no shared religion, no culture, no cuisine holding anything together. The only glue left was the financial system itself, the love of cheap money and free stuff. That bubble was always going to crack.
- When it does, and it has already started, what’s left is a continent of people who never actually became one people, and the free-for-all already starting in France and building here in Germany is just the beginning.
- Admitting the mistake would mean admitting the parties hollowed out their own societies in a failed attempt to keep the schemes and the seats. That is total systemic failure. They will not say it. They will keep the subsidies flowing and the talking points going until the last bit of financial glue holding the whole mess together is gone. Total collapse is guaranteed at this point. The die has been cast and nothing is fixing this. Not remigration, not pension reform, not "alternative" parties, nothing. It collapases, totally and completely.

Let me use an example that may not have been universally experienced by everyone but shows how an entire city shifted their marketing and tourist strategy towards kids; Las Vegas. 

Yes, adults could still smoke and gamble, but most casinos literally developed entirely sections for kids to enjoy. Luxor had a two story Sega Arcade! If I remember correctly Circus Circus built a theme park to bring in families with kids of all ages. They also had their own "kids zone" with games of chance designed like carnival games where kids competed against kids. There was a shift towards more family friendly shows, performances and entertainment both inside the hotels and outside. Treasure Island had a pirate battle, in the fake lagoon in front of their hotel that was better than anything Disneyland or Knotts Berry Farm could offer. People who lived in California in the 90's know what I'm talking about...

I could go on, Excalibur existed back then with medieval tournaments, every Casino retrofitted and or expanded their pools with slides and more kid friendly options. Vegas even had a water park and don't forget the Stratosphere had a rollercoaster built on top of it that was originally pushed on families with teens before they shifted the appeal to "thrill seekers". A lot of stuff you see nowadays which is made for "thrill seekers" got its start in the 90's during the "extreme era" like Professional Skateboarding... the 90's was literally the decade for everyone under 18... it's fascinating.

text:
The death is real. The pandemic is a headline that outran the record.

A 28-year-old technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, Darya Shipilova, died of pneumonia. Russian authorities called it pneumonia of unknown cause and said there was no evidence it was caused by a pathogen from the lab. The regional governor said no other institute staff had become ill. About 200 contacts were quarantined. No second case has been reported. That is a local investigation. It is not a seed event.

https://t.co/HYJhv8DhW8

Pneumonic plague is the lung form of Yersinia pestis, the same bacterium that causes bubonic plague. Untreated, it kills. Treated, it is a bacterial pneumonia. Streptomycin, gentamicin, doxycycline, and ciprofloxacin have been used to treat it for decades. It does not drift through a shopping mall. It spreads through close respiratory contact, and the chain stops when the sick are isolated and their contacts receive medicine.

This has happened before, on a larger scale than a rumor. Colorado, June and July 2014. A dog died coughing blood. The owner was hospitalized with plague pneumonia. Three other people who handled the dog or the owner got sick. One of those cases may have involved person-to-person transmission, the first such suspected case in the United States since 1924. The CDC identified 114 close contacts: 36 in the vet clinic, 58 in human medical settings, and 20 personal contacts. Eighty-eight were offered antibiotics. Twenty-six were told to watch for fever. All four patients recovered. The paper is the CDC’s own, dated May 1, 2015.

https://t.co/ILImhqXBBg

A puppy in Colorado produced the largest pneumonic plague cluster in the modern American record, with possible human spread, and it ended in four recoveries and a prophylaxis list. No panic was required, and none arrived. The same bacterium does not become a new world event because the laboratory is in Siberia and the chyron says plague. Print the 114. Print the four recoveries. The fear is the part that is not in the record.

A half-hour later, we were in Steve's home recording studio and Luke launched a classic Jeff Porcaro prank on Reilich, saying with no small amount of smirk in his tone: "So, you're aunt was pretty hard on you, eh?"

Truth:
Pete's aunt Lee was never hard on him. Quite the opposite, as she was a liberal. For example, she was one of few old lady piano teachers who was known for allowing her students to learn any pop tune they liked, the sheet music for which she would bring home from her clerk job in the sheet music department of Sight & Sound music store on Victory Blvd. She actually would steal the music from work so her students could learn how to play the tunes they wanted to play. In the end, Steve really screwed up by not kissing THE SAINT Lee Reilich's ass. That is the grand understatement of the entire relationship. Especially considering how his dad was already befriending the Reilichs out of a mutual musicianship.

You must ask the question: Why would a non-musician like Eileen marry a fine, altruistic musician like Joe Porcaro? Why were all of us visiting musicians supposed to keep our distance from Eileen? I mean, again, if you don't like being around musicians, why would you marry one? 

So, opposites attract, which is fine. Nobody has a problem with how this couple, Joe and Eileen Porcaro are a mismatch. What we don't like is the fact that this snob was a secret her kids had to keep from their musician friends, especially if those friends happened to be financially poor. 

Everyone has always known that the most talented artistic people tend to be found on the lower economic echelon. What a pressure dad and the boys must have been under to keep snobby mom happy as they emigrated west into unknown realms, what must have seemed like the outer Hebrides to a snob like Eileen. Where the dangerous low-lifes hide and pounce on every decent minded, vulnerable snob from New England. Oh, no! We better protect her from the dangerous low-life scum!

So basically Steven "Alfred E. Newman" Lukather got it wrong. This was obviously because he was endlessly sucking up to Jeff Porcaro, one of the most conniving pranksters who ever lived. Liars beget liars. 

Therefore, a more appropriate line would be for me to say to them: 'So Eileen was pretty hard on you, eh?' And this is exactly right, when one thinks of the scapegoating factor.

I gotta bait 'n switch
I got a professional reputation to protect
I gotta bait 'n switch those Reilichs
Or everyone's gonna find out
about my snob mom
about her and Jeff mudslinging Lee out of town
For no good goddamn reason.

Goldie Lee Reilich was a victim of Eileen and Jeffrey Porcaro's gossiping defamy. Those fuckers should have been sued into hell.

You must ask the question of which is more important, sticking with the highly musical friends his very talented and musical dad was instinctively finding in their new neighborhood, or running home to mommy complaining about how you weren't allowed to behave like a disrespectful brat at your piano lesson. Fact: Eileen Porcaro was a classic racist snob from the wealthy side of Hartford, Connecticut. Fucking uncanny how much this is like the play Auntie Mame. 

It would not be surprising to discover that Eileen maneuvered the whole thing, from the back room of their house, like a fucking mafia godfather. The woman never said one word to me, ever. And what about the fact that the Porcaros had a pool and none of us kids ever saw it, let alone were ever asked over for a birthday party. 

The reality is that the Porcaros were a weird family. Any help they may have offered as surrogate parents to the orphaned Peter was always tainted by the fact that Eileen was a typical snob come to the outer Hebrides from New England, paranoid of being associated with people like the Reilichs, who she must have seen as low-life heathens. This snob-based paranoia was apparent whenever anyone spent time around the Nervous Nellie who was Steve Porcaro.

So, fully aware of the intricate legal dangers of all this ambition driven misbehavior at Hollywood (where some believe it's fair game), the Porcaros carefully tiptoed around decency, planned and fleshed out their Hollywood careers. 

Note: You don't have to take my word on Eileen Porcaro being a snob from Hartford, just ask Johnette Napolitano.

They'd been telling this lie about Goldie Lee Reilich since the day Steve took his one and only piano lesson from her. Something happened at that lesson and, even though Steve has been lying about it for his entire life, it's fairly obvious to people who knew him and his brothers what really must have happened. 

Steve was a braggart when he was little; undoubtedly put up to it by his bully elder brother Jeff. It appears that Steve was to be the spokesperson for Jeff's Hollywood ambition, fronting for his elder brother who had the personality of a cockroach. All of which may have been fine, except for the fact that Steve's real personality was akin to his father's: mild and soft-spoken. Indeed, these two music purists needed to be living in an Italian village, not pushed into fucking Hollywood by a womanizing sexist brother/son.

As for Lukather and his insulting mouth... Again, people who knew them would not be surprised that in 2005 Luke still had his tongue up Jeff Porcaro's dead asshole.

Poor Steve, who had acquired a stomach ulcer over this convoluted social chit by age seventeen. 

And poor Pete Reilich, who was forever a target of this fucker Jeff Porcaro concerning a couple of issues...

text:
In the spring of 1780, the British had a plan to end the war in the west.

Take St. Louis. Control the upper Mississippi. Cut George Rogers Clark's supply line. Collapse the entire western theater.

One man stood in the way.

Fernando de Leyba was the Spanish lieutenant governor of Upper Louisiana. Career soldier. No significant garrison. No reinforcements coming from New Orleans or Havana.

Two years earlier, George Rogers Clark had walked into his office with a warning.

The British will come. Fortify St. Louis.

De Leyba wrote to Bernardo de Gálvez requesting funds and soldiers.

Gálvez sent neither.

De Leyba built the fort anyway.

He raised 1,000 piastres from the community to construct a stone defensive tower. When the funds ran short, he put in 400 piastres of his own money. Money already depleted from gifts he had given to maintain alliances with neighboring tribes.

Fort San Carlos was barely finished when the British came.

By May 1780, de Leyba was seriously ill. The kind of ill that kills a man. He would be dead in five weeks.

He directed the defense anyway.

On May 26, a British-led coalition came out of the tree line north of St. Louis. Ojibwe, Ho-Chunk, Menominee, Potawatomi, and Dakota warriors. Canadian militia. Hundreds of men against 300 defenders.

The tower held.

After hours of fighting, the attacking force withdrew. The British never came back. The upper Mississippi stayed in Spanish hands. Clark's supply line survived. The western theater held.

Here is what the history books understate:

De Leyba died June 28, 1780. One month after the battle he had spent two years building toward.

What came after was worse than obscurity.

Within decades, villagers accused him of selling gunpowder to enemies. Of cowardice during the battle. Those accusations, offered fifty years after the fact, defined how historians wrote about him through the nineteenth century.

The man who funded the fort with his own money, commanded it while dying, and saved the settlement was remembered as the man who may have betrayed it.

Modern scholars have begun reassessing his record.

The reassessment is long overdue.

When you are outnumbered and the resources are not coming, you do not spread thin. You find your strongest point. You build it up. You concentrate everything you have there.

And you hold.

Rule 19 of 76 Rules of Command is live on Substack. Hold the Tower. 👇🇺🇸 #AmRev

‘First Time in History’: Bessent Says Iran Faces Zero Oil Revenue This Week — Tehran Warns of Economic Crisis | Joshua Klein, Breitbart

Iran is set to have no oil at sea and no oil revenue this week for the “first time in history,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said as Tehran’s top security official issued a rare warning over the country’s deepening economic crisis.

“For the first time in history, since they started pumping oil, they will have no oil on the water this week,” Bessent told The Axios Show on Saturday. “They will have no revenues.”

Bessent said the unprecedented situation is the result of a deliberate, three-stage campaign that began with the U.S. military assault earlier this year, moved to President Donald Trump’s blockade of Iranian commerce, and is now aimed at isolating Tehran economically.

The Treasury secretary traced the strategy back to the roughly six-week military campaign beginning in late February, which he said destroyed Iran’s navy and air force, substantially depleted its missile and drone capabilities and crippled its ability to rebuild them.

“We had kinetic,” Bessent said. “We destroyed their navy, their air force, substantially depleted their drone and missile capability, destroyed their chances of rebuilding that.”

Washington then moved to what Trump calls the “Iron Wall” — the U.S. naval blockade that has prevented Iranian oil exports while protecting international traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — before launching Operation Economic Outcast, the administration’s broader campaign to sever Tehran from remaining sources of trade and revenue.

“Then we went to what the president calls the Iron Wall and the blockade, which we’d never done before,” Bessent said. “And now we have Operation Economic Outcast, and we are isolating them economically like has never happened before.”

Treasury expanded that campaign Thursday with sanctions targeting Iran’s automotive and rail industries and foreign suppliers, seeking to further restrict the resources available to Tehran’s military, missile and drone programs, cyber operations, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Bessent said the strategy has effectively shut Iranian oil out of the strait even as U.S.-protected international commerce has continued moving through it.

“Right now, the score, in terms of barrels out of the strait: U.S. about 1.1 billion, Iran zero,” he said.

The prospect of Iran having no oil remaining at sea this week also brings forward a prediction Bessent made last weekend. At the time, roughly 15 million barrels loaded before the blockade remained aboard tankers, with the final cargoes headed largely to China. Bessent predicted that once those shipments were delivered, Tehran would have “nothing left to trade.”

One week later, he says that point is arriving.

The effects are becoming increasingly visible inside Iran — including in unusually stark warnings from the country’s own leadership.

Mohsen Rezaei, Iran’s top national security official, described the circumstances as among the most difficult periods the country has faced during a high-level government meeting Saturday with President Masoud Pezeshkian and senior ministers, according to the state-run IRNA news agency. Iranian state media did not publish Rezaei’s remarks verbatim.

Pezeshkian acknowledged at the same meeting that economic conditions had worsened and said his government had adopted a “new posture” to manage what he called the country’s “special conditions.”

The warnings came as Iran’s currency sank to another record low. The rial traded at roughly 2.69 million to the dollar Saturday after losing more than half its value over the past year, while inflation has climbed above 70 percent. Iran’s central bank has responded by offering up to $2 billion in U.S. currency through state banks in an effort to support the rial.

The damage extends beyond financial markets. Reuters reported that Iranians are exhausting savings, losing jobs, moving to less expensive areas and cutting spending on basic needs as soaring prices and the loss of oil revenue erode living standards. Fear of government repression and the immediate struggle to make ends meet, however, have so far constrained the economic discontent from developing into broader nationwide protests.

Iran’s collapsing exports increasingly stand in contrast to the recovery in oil shipments from the rest of the Gulf.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Sunday that supplies moving through Hormuz have continued to rise in recent weeks. Goldman Sachs analysts estimated Persian Gulf oil exports reached roughly 23.3 million barrels per day over the past week, returning to prewar levels even as Iranian crude loadings collapsed.

The administration says it intends to maintain that arrangement — allowing international energy traffic through the strait while continuing to block Iranian exports.

War Secretary Pete Hegseth said Saturday that Washington can maintain the blockade for as long as necessary and rejected Tehran’s repeated assertions that it controls the strategic waterway.

“Iran wants to play games with things like the Strait of Hormuz. They don’t control it. We do,” Hegseth said. “They have literally gotten nothing through. Our blockade’s been ironclad, and we’re running almost at prewar levels every single night through that.”

Hegseth said the result has left Washington in a “very strong position,” urging Tehran to “make the right choice” while Trump still has the option of resolving the confrontation without another major military escalation.

“If they don’t, the president’s going to have all the options he needs on the table,” he said.

Tehran is now seeking relief from that pressure as Washington and Iran exchange proposals over a possible agreement.

Iranian officials said Sunday that Washington had responded through intermediaries to Tehran’s latest proposal, which Trump had already rejected as insufficient, and that the U.S. response was now being reviewed by the Iranian government. Tehran has continued to demand sanctions relief and an end to restrictions on its maritime commerce as conditions for fully reopening Hormuz.

Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf insisted Sunday that the strait would remain closed until Washington accepted seven Iranian conditions tied to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding — the June framework that established a ceasefire and a path toward reopening Hormuz and broader negotiations before Iran resumed attacks on commercial vessels and the agreement ultimately broke down.

“The Strait of Hormuz will not open until our seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum are met,” Ghalibaf said.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, insisted that neither additional sanctions nor renewed military action would force Tehran to accept Washington’s terms.

“There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions,” Araghchi said, arguing that negotiations based on “justice and fairness” offered the only path to ending the conflict.

But Araghchi paired that appeal for negotiations with a warning, saying that if Iran’s enemies “again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before.”

Washington, however, is preparing for the possibility that Tehran still refuses to accept terms Trump considers sufficient.

Senior Trump administration officials met for several hours at Camp David on Friday to discuss Iran, with Vice President JD Vance chairing a previously unannounced gathering that included Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Hegseth, Bessent, CIA Director John Ratcliffe, White House envoy Steve Witkoff, and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine.

“Things were decided or at least deeply discussed,” one U.S. official told Axios.

Trump offered little detail when reporters subsequently asked what had emerged from the meeting.

“If I told you, you would have a major story,” he said Friday. “But you will see. It is working out very well. Iran is not doing well.”

A day later, Trump said he was approaching a decision.

“We have a decision that I’ll make about Iran,” he said Saturday. “Iran has been decimated. So the only question is it’ll either be the easy way or the hard way. We’ll have it the easy way or the hard way.”

Tehran, meanwhile, is preparing for the possibility that the confrontation again turns military.

Iran’s army announced Sunday that it has begun increasing the range and speed of its missiles after concluding from the conflict that U.S. forces are operating farther from Iranian shores. Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said the military intends to upgrade its missiles to reach adversaries operating at distances of up to 1,000 kilometers.

The announcement comes as Tehran seeks relief from a blockade Bessent says is days away from leaving Iran without oil at sea or the revenues those shipments provide. The Trump administration says it can maintain the blockade for as long as necessary if Iran refuses to accept an agreement.

Hegseth said the United States can maintain the blockade “as long as we need to,” urging Iran to “make the right choice” while it still can. If Tehran refuses, he said, Trump will have “all the options he needs on the table,” with U.S. forces prepared to act if called upon.

🎥 Trump’s propaganda campaign for #Trump to #Force_Iran_to_Surrender will not succeed; there is no #Military_Option for #Iran_Surrendering, either before the #Midterm_Elections or after them: #Economic_Destruction of Iran will not end in surrender either 👇👇

👈 John Mearsheimer, professor at the University of Chicago and a leading theorist of offensive realism.

✅ 1. Claims
🔺1.1 For the past few weeks the Trump administration has been running a propaganda campaign in the mainstream media to convince Iran that it is doomed, that the tide has turned in America’s favor, and that the sooner it cuts a deal the better, because the punishment will be severe. Trump has threatened to annihilate Iran if it does not surrender.
🔺1.2 The mainstream media, from the Wall Street Journal even to Al Jazeera, repeat these claims without pause, and almost no one throws cold water on them or assesses whether sending forces and a carrier will actually have the effect that is claimed.
🔺1.3 The story has two prongs. The economic prong: the blockade, plus Bessent’s strategy of cutting Iran off from its economic dealings with the rest of the world, sometimes called Operation Economic Outcast, is strangling the Iranian economy to the point of collapse. At the same time the West is doing well, because oil coming out of the Gulf has returned almost to the level of 27 February, the day before the war began; Iran’s effort to close Hormuz has therefore failed, time is on the West’s side, and there is no reason to cave in.
🔺1.4 The military prong: nothing of consequence is now under way. There is no bombing campaign by the United States or its allies, and no sign that ground forces are about to be inserted. The administration is nevertheless making much of sending 10,000 more troops and another carrier, the Teddy Roosevelt, and building the picture of a strike force: two carriers already there, the George Washington and the George H. W. Bush, plus the Roosevelt, make three; 50,000 troops already there plus 10,000 make about 60,000. The claim is that after the midterms, once this force has arrived and been set up, Trump will be free to use naval, air, and ground power to bring Iran to its knees, if economic means have not already done so.
🔺1.5 This account is deeply flawed. Hoodwinking Iran into surrender will not work, chiefly because the facts say otherwise. At this point it is almost impossible to convince Iran that the time to surrender has come.

✅ 2. Arguments
🔺2.1 If a 40-day strategic bombing campaign brought no military victory, adding a carrier supplies no independent reason to expect victory this time. The munitions shortage is a separate link in the chain: that shortage is one reason bombing and tit-for-tat strikes have stopped, and the assumption that it will be overcome after the midterms does not erase the failure of the earlier campaign.
🔺2.2 The inference of “three carriers” from the dispatch of the Roosevelt is invalid, because the dispatch is a replacement, not an addition. The Bush, contrary to the usual pretense, is not in the region. The premise of “three carriers ready to strike” is therefore false. Even moving other carriers back, given months of operational tempo and commanders’ warnings that this tempo cannot be sustained, will not rise above a ceiling of about two carriers; and two carriers, with the munitions shortage and the record of the 40-day campaign, still offer no clear mechanism for bringing Iran to its knees.
🔺2.3 Logistics is an independent constraint. The loss of naval bases in the Gulf pushes the supply line back to Diego Garcia. Holding three carriers in place for any appreciable time, given logistics and the present state of the Navy, will be extremely difficult, if not impossible.
🔺2.4 Striking Iran’s oil infrastructure is not a simple remedy for insufficient air power. Iran has a second-strike capability. That is why its oil infrastructure has not so far been hit in any meaningful way: retaliation would fall on infrastructure in the Gulf states and in Israel.
🔺2.5 The headline troop number is not the measure of an invasion. Only combat units—brigades, battalions, and divisions—plus supporting air power can seize ground. Most of the 10,000 accompanying the Roosevelt are sailors on the carrier and its escorts, not troops who can be landed on Iranian soil. The jump from 50,000 to 60,000 is therefore not a jump in invasion capacity.
🔺2.6 Even doubling or tripling the combat force on hand would not close the gap to the threshold of an invasion. McCaffrey’s figure is for Hormuz alone, not for the conquest of Iran, and the force available is about one-tenth of that figure. The Ukraine comparison cuts the same way: a far larger force was not enough to hold the ground first taken, while Iran has twice the population of Ukraine and terrain much harder for an invader. Retaking Hormuz, or invading Iran, on this scale is not a serious argument. Holding even that small force over the long term is a further, separate difficulty.
🔺2.7 The political constraint and the tactical constraint on getting ashore are distinct from the number of troops. Opposition to the war was already significant on day one and has grown since. Body bags in large numbers, with a campaign of many months and a real chance of failure, would produce a huge public outcry. The Marines of the two expeditionary units are on amphibious ships, and landing them means taking those large ships close to the Iranian coast. The Navy does not want to do that, for fear a cruise missile will sink the ship. Even if they were put on the beaches, the shortage of troops would remain.
🔺2.8 Economic pain does not entail surrender. In the record of major wars there is no case in which one side brought the other to surrender by economic means alone, by blockade alone. The blockade at the end of the First World War did devastate Germany and did play a part in the surrender, but the main cause was the ground war on two fronts. There is no ground war here, and no reliable air war either. Reliance on the blockade plus the Bessent strategy therefore has no historical warrant.
🔺2.9 An existential threat blocks the logic of surrender. Talk of annihilating Iran, of wiping it off the map, is read in Iran as an existential threat. Against an existential threat one fights to the last person, even under severe economic suffering. Surrender is not an option.
🔺2.10 If that judgment is wrong and the sanctions really do bring Iran to the end of its rope, the expected answer is escalation, not surrender. Iran can strike energy infrastructure across the Gulf and in Israel itself, and can do heavy damage to desalination plants in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Israel. Hitting Saudi oil and desalination could ruin Saudi Arabia as a functioning society, and a full-scale attack on the region’s energy and desalination plants would be devastating for the international economy. Pushing Iran to that doomsday option is therefore not desirable.
🔺2.11 The claim that the West is doing well has two holes in it. Iran is not sitting still; it has adjusted, and newer, more effective attacks are slowing the flow of oil. The separate war between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia puts the export pipeline to the Red Sea, and large vulnerable Saudi installations, in reach, and as that war heats up it can cut Saudi export capacity. A rate close to that of 27 February today is no reason to think the rate will stay there.
🔺2.12 Even if the rate barely changes, oil flowing is not the same thing as economic pain solved. European inflation, prices in the United States and elsewhere, bond yields, the cost of diesel, and the cost of a mortgage in the United States show that, despite the oil, the West—and Asian economies still more so—remain in deep trouble, and almost no one in the media says most of these problems will be solved any time soon. Restoring the flow to something close to the pre-war level has therefore done little to solve the problem.

✅ 3. Evidence and indications
🔺3.1 The strategic bombing campaign: 28 February to 8 April, 40 days, no military victory. A serious munitions shortage, by Mearsheimer’s account agreed by nearly everyone, as the present reason there is neither bombing nor tit-for-tat strikes.
🔺3.2 The carriers: the George Washington is in the region; the George H. W. Bush has left and is now in Thailand; the Teddy Roosevelt is on the way to replace the Washington, not to operate alongside it. The count: one carrier in the region now, not inside the Gulf itself, because fear of its being sunk almost at once rules that out; still one carrier after the Roosevelt arrives. Repeated warnings from naval commanders that the tempo of recent months cannot be sustained and is pushing the force to the brink. A supply line of about 2,500 miles back to Diego Garcia.
🔺3.3 Troop numbers: about 50,000 already there, 10,000 on the way with the Roosevelt, a nominal total of about 60,000. Of the 10,000, only about 2,200 in the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit can be used in a combat landing on Iranian territory; the rest are sailors on the Roosevelt and the ships coming with it. Of the 50,000 already there: the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit, about 2,200; the 82nd Airborne, about 2,000; and about 800 ground troops long stationed in and around Kuwait. The sum: 2.2 + 2 + 0.8 + 2.2, a little under 7,500 combat troops.
🔺3.4 The estimate of Barry McCaffrey, a retired four-star U.S. Army general: 150,000 combat troops and three to six months of fighting, merely to take the Strait of Hormuz. The estimate for the Russian entry into Ukraine in February 2022: about 190,000 troops, not enough to take and hold all the ground first seized. Iran’s population is about twice Ukraine’s; Iranian terrain is harder for an invader than Ukrainian terrain was for the attacking Russian force.
🔺3.5 Significant domestic opposition from the start of the war, and an increase since. Two Marine expeditionary units, the 11th already there and the 13th on the way, aboard amphibious ships; a landing requires those ships to be taken to the Iranian coast, at the risk of a cruise missile.
🔺3.6 The British and American blockade at the end of the First World War: a devastating effect on Germany and its allies, especially Austria-Hungary, and a part in the surrender of 11 November 1918; but a ground war from 1 August 1914 on the Western and Eastern fronts, with millions of German and Allied dead. Threats by Trump to annihilate Iran: at least seven, on Mearsheimer’s count.
🔺3.7 That day’s Wall Street Journal headline: “New Strait Attacks Threaten Oil Flow.” The story: Iran adjusting to the existing situation; newer, more sophisticated, and more effective attacks; the flow of oil beginning to slow. The Houthis’ war with Saudi Arabia, and a reported hit on the pipeline Saudi Arabia depends on heavily to move oil out to the Red Sea and into world markets; also large, vulnerable Saudi oil installations. The level claimed by the administration: oil leaving the Gulf at nearly the volume of 27 February. Indicators against “the West is doing well”: European inflation, prices in the United States and elsewhere, bond yields, the cost of diesel, the cost of a mortgage.

✅ 4. Conclusions
🔺4.1 The propaganda campaign will not work on either prong. The media can go along with the story of “an option after the midterms,” but the facts stand apart from the story.
🔺4.2 Adding a carrier, even in the unlikely case of three, will not bring Iran to its knees. A ground invasion with this combat force is not a serious argument. If Trump launches such an invasion he will not succeed, and his position will only get worse. There is no military option today, and there will not be one after the midterms.
🔺4.3 The economic pain inflicted on Iran is real and heavy, but neither the historical record nor the existential threat yields the conclusion that surrender is close. If that judgment is wrong and Iran sees itself at the edge of the cliff, it will take the others over with it; the international economy and Trump’s position would both be damaged, and he would be in no position to say that he had won.
🔺4.4 Iran will not, at this point, be fooled into thinking that America has the upper hand, that defeat is at hand, and that the time has come to surrender. It is too experienced in dealing with the United States for that.
