text:
Creation and Destruction, at Once

This isn’t a historical curiosity. It’s happening in India right now, in a form most people interact with weekly. Quick commerce apps like Zepto, Blinkit, and Swiggy Instamart promise grocery delivery in ten minutes, built on networks of small warehouses called dark stores. Industry estimates suggest this sector has created something like 450,000 jobs over the past three years. At the same time, trade bodies representing small retailers say roughly 200,000 neighbourhood kirana stores shut down in a single recent year, unable to match the discounts and speed that venture funded apps can offer.

Both numbers are real, and both are the same phenomenon. New jobs, new convenience, and new companies on one side. Shuttered family businesses and displaced livelihoods on the other. India’s taxi and ride hailing market went through a similar cycle a decade earlier, when Ola and Uber upended traditional taxi stands, before a new wave of driver owned platforms like Namma Yatri began challenging Ola and Uber themselves in turn. Creative destruction doesn’t happen once and settle. It keeps happening, to whoever is on top.

The Policy Puzzle

Here’s the part of the Aghion-Howitt model that trips up intuition. You might assume the fix for all this disruption is simply protecting whoever’s winning right now, through patents, favourable regulation, or outright subsidy. But their model shows that too much protection for today’s leaders can quietly choke off tomorrow’s growth, because it removes the incentive for anyone else to try to outdo them.

At the same time, offering no protection at all doesn’t work either. If a firm can’t count on at least some temporary reward for a successful innovation, before a copycat erases the advantage, there’s no reason to take the risk of innovating in the first place. The model’s real contribution is showing that sustained growth depends on getting this balance right, enough reward to make innovation worth attempting, but never so much that it freezes the current leaders permanently in place. Competition policy, patent length, and how a government treats declining industries all turn out to be versions of the same underlying question.

Growth’s Uncomfortable Bargain

What makes creative destruction difficult to sit with isn’t the theory, it’s the trade. The 450,000 new quick commerce jobs and the kirana stores that closed to make room for them aren’t two separate stories, they’re one transaction, paid for on both sides. Aghion and Howitt didn’t invent that trade-off. They just gave economists, and everyone else, a rigorous way to see it clearly: growth doesn’t arrive without something older being pushed aside to make space for it, and pretending otherwise is the one option that was never actually available.

Source - The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences 2025 citation and popular science background), Bloomberg, CNN, The Associated Press (via Physdotorg), The Washington Post.

text:
🟩 LITHUANIA INVITES THE UNITED STATES TO ESTABLISH A PERMANENT MILITARY BASE

Lithuania has formally opened the door to a permanent American military base on NATO’s eastern flank—and President Donald Trump says the United States will consider the proposal.

“We will certainly look at it,” Trump said when asked about Lithuania’s invitation. “I know so many people in Lithuania. They are great people.”

The response is not an approval, and no agreement has been announced. But it places the possibility of a permanent American base in Lithuania under consideration at the highest level of the U.S. government.

Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius previously said his country was prepared to cover the cost and provide the best possible conditions for American troops and infrastructure.

U.S. forces already deploy to Lithuania on rotating assignments. Since 2019, the American presence has generally included an armored battalion of approximately 1,000 troops supported by Abrams tanks, Bradley fighting vehicles and artillery. Two additional American battalions are expected to arrive later in October, although the nine-month rotational system will remain in place for now.

Lithuania’s proposal also comes at an uncertain moment for the American military presence in Europe. Washington is reviewing its force posture across the continent, with troops withdrawn or deployments reconsidered in several locations as the United States redirects resources toward other regions.

That makes Lithuania’s offer especially significant. While some European countries fear losing American forces, Vilnius is offering to finance the infrastructure needed to transform a temporary rotation into a permanent deployment.

A permanent base would carry far greater strategic weight. Lithuania borders both Russia’s heavily militarized Kaliningrad region and Belarus, while sitting beside the Suwałki corridor—the narrow land connection between the Baltic states and the rest of NATO territory.

Permanent American forces would strengthen deterrence, shorten reinforcement times and make clear that an attack against Lithuania would immediately involve U.S. troops already positioned on the ground.

Lithuania is not asking others to carry the burden alone. It has sharply increased defense spending, expanded military infrastructure and offered to finance the American presence itself.

The objective is not simply to preserve the troops already rotating through Lithuania. It is to anchor American military power permanently on one of NATO’s most exposed frontiers before broader reductions elsewhere can weaken deterrence.

For years, the Baltic states warned that Russia’s aggression would not necessarily stop with Ukraine. Lithuania is now seeking to ensure that if Moscow ever tests NATO’s eastern frontier, American forces will already be waiting there.

text:
One important context for recent developments is the debate inside Iran over whether Trump needs to be given a face-saving “exit window” from the war: an arrangement he can sell as a victory even if Iran secures much of what it wants.

The idea would be to give Trump a narrative he can take home: “I reopened Hormuz despite everything Iran did. My threats and military buildup forced Tehran to buckle and accept my terms.”

Meanwhile, Iran could focus less on the optics and more on locking in the strategic gains it cares about, while still making concessions of its own.

I’m not saying this is what’s happening. But this has been a real part of the high-level debate inside Iran.

Of course, the big question in such a scenario would be whether Washington would actually take such an off-ramp. Even if Tehran offered Trump a politically attractive way to end the war, it’s far from clear that the erratic Donald Trump would take the deal rather than continue pressing for more.

Regardless of whether this thinking had anything to do with the greater volume of oil getting out of the Persian Gulf in recent weeks, or Iran’s relatively more conciliatory messaging (i.e., Pezeshkian at UNGA), Tehran is now seemingly decisively moving in the other direction: escalating and doing more to constrain Persian Gulf oil flows.👇

text:
NIGERIA’S NEXT PRESIDENT DOES NOT NEED A PERMISSION SLIP FROM WASHINGTON

Letters from Stockholm — Kio Amachree

I am tired of the updates from Atiku’s camp about how the Americans supposedly feel about Nigeria’s next election, as though Nigerians should wait for Washington to approve our choice of president.

The Americans are our allies, not our masters. Nigeria is not an American colony.

Atiku Abubakar should be explaining how he intends to restore security, create jobs, rebuild public institutions and unite this country. Instead, the attention given to American access and approval leaves me wondering whose confidence he considers most important: ours or theirs.

This concern has a concrete basis. PREMIUM TIMES reported that Atiku engaged a Washington lobbying firm under a twelve-month agreement worth $1.2 million, intended to improve his standing in American policy circles and counter the Nigerian government’s lobbying narratives. (https://t.co/7g6CFPWZaB⁠￼)

One side lobbying Washington to outmanoeuvre the other. Meanwhile, Nigerians are waiting for leadership that can make their lives bearable.

A lobbying contract is not an economic programme. Access to American officials is not a mandate from the Nigerian people. A photograph in Washington cannot feed a family in Kano, protect a farmer in Benue or keep a business alive in Port Harcourt.

Atiku’s history makes this dependence particularly troubling. His January 2019 American visit followed years of entry restrictions. Reuters reported that the visit was made possible by a temporary waiver after lobbying efforts, with the restrictions linked to corruption allegations. Those allegations must be distinguished from a criminal conviction, but the history cannot simply be erased by a successful Washington visit. (https://t.co/FtleB0R9QD⁠￼)

That does not establish that Atiku is controlled by America. It does make me question the political judgment of presenting American acceptance as an electoral credential.

I have the same objection whenever Tinubu’s supporters parade foreign access as proof of legitimacy. Nigeria’s presidency must never become a competition over who has the better connections with foreign power.

As I keep saying, there is no point jumping out of the frying pan into the fire.

I see too little evidence that replacing Tinubu with Atiku would deliver the political renewal Nigeria needs. These are two men who have spent decades within the machinery of power. Nigerians deserve more than another rearrangement of the same exhausted political class.

Nor do the people around Atiku reassure me. I fear another Buhari-style presidency: a powerful cabal, an insulated court and a president surrounded by people more interested in controlling access than delivering results.

My objection is to that closed system of patronage, wherever its members come from. Nigeria has suffered enough under governments that treat public office as the property of a political inner circle.

And I certainly do not regard approval from Trump’s administration as a certificate of integrity. In my view, its transactional politics offer no moral authority for deciding who should govern Nigeria.

If Atiku’s lawyers, lobbyists and supporters want to persuade me, they should explain his programme, his proposed governing team and how he would prevent another cabal from capturing the presidency.

Stop telling us who is impressed in Washington. Tell us what will change in Nigeria.

We need a president accountable to Nigerians, with the independence to defend our interests and the competence to serve our people.

Nigeria is an independent country. Our future belongs to us. Any candidate who wants our presidency must earn our confidence here.

#LettersFromStockholm #KioAmachree #NigeriaDecides2027 #Atiku #Tinubu #NigerianSovereignty #Accountability #Nigeria

text:
The first reading for Tuesday October 6, 2026: Book of Galatians (Galatians 1:13-24)

He was a persecutor of the church advancing in Judaism.

God revealed his Son to him and called him to preach to the Gentiles.

He conferred not with flesh and blood but proclaimed the faith he once tried to destroy.

This is the witness of Galatians 1:13-24

Walking by Faith in the Promises of God from Galatians 5

The letter to the Galatians stands as a powerful call for Catholics to embrace the freedom that comes from Christ rather than relying on external rules alone. Saint Paul writes with urgency to communities tempted to return to old observances that cannot save. This message speaks directly to faithful Catholics who seek to integrate scripture with the sacraments and daily moral choices. Through careful attention to the text we see how justification flows from faith that expresses itself in love. The reading opens with an affirmation of liberty that sets the tone for the entire passage.

How Does Paul Contrast the Flesh with the Spirit in This Passage

Saint Paul draws a sharp distinction between living according to the flesh and walking by the Spirit. He lists the works of the flesh as behaviors that lead away from God and harm community life. These include obvious sins but also subtler attitudes like envy and factionalism that can divide parishes. In contrast the fruit of the Spirit offers virtues such as patience and self control that build up the body of Christ. Catholics recognize these fruits as graces cultivated through prayer and reception of the Eucharist. The apostle insists that those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions. This contrast invites readers to examine their own habits in light of the gospel.

What Does Freedom in Christ Require of Practicing Catholics

Freedom in Christ does not mean license to do whatever one wishes but rather the ability to serve others in love. Paul warns against using liberty as an opportunity for self indulgence. Instead believers are called to fulfill the law through the single commandment to love their neighbor as themselves. For Catholics this teaching aligns with the Church emphasis on works of mercy and participation in the sacramental life. The passage reminds us that the Spirit produces growth over time rather than instant perfection. Daily choices such as forgiving an offense or attending weekday Mass become expressions of this freedom. Such freedom strengthens family bonds and parish communities when lived consistently.

How Can the Fruits of the Spirit Guide Moral Decisions Today

The fruits listed by Paul provide a practical framework for discerning right action in complex situations. Love joy and peace orient the heart toward God and others in every circumstance. Catholics can apply these qualities when facing workplace conflicts or decisions about charitable giving. Kindness and generosity flow naturally from a heart formed by the sacraments and scripture meditation. Faithfulness and gentleness help maintain unity in the face of disagreements within the wider Church. Self control supports the practice of fasting and other Lenten disciplines. By focusing on these fruits believers move beyond mere rule keeping to a transformed way of life.

In the end the reading from Galatians calls Catholics to a mature faith that bears visible fruit in everyday actions. This freedom rooted in Christ leads to deeper communion with the Church and with the Lord himself. Readers are encouraged to return often to this text for guidance in their spiritual journey.
Transforming Encounters Through Grace Galatians 1

How might a dramatic personal conversion reshape the way we connect with those closest to us each day.

The reading from Galatians 1 opens with Paul recounting his former life in Judaism where he violently persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it. This sets a foundation for understanding radical change brought by divine intervention rather than human effort. Faithful Catholics can draw from this to approach family members with humility when past conflicts linger. The text continues by describing how God revealed his Son to Paul so that he might proclaim him among the Gentiles. Such revelation invites believers to recognize similar moments of insight in their own lives that prompt renewed patience at home.

How Can Family Dynamics Reflect Paul's Journey of Revelation.

In family settings the emphasis falls on quiet transformation without seeking approval from others as Paul states I did not confer with any human being. Catholics might use this to listen more attentively to spouses or children during disagreements allowing grace to mend old wounds instead of defending positions. The passage highlights going away to Arabia before returning which suggests periods of personal reflection that strengthen bonds when shared thoughtfully later. This differs from other relationships because family interactions often involve deep history and daily proximity requiring consistent application of mercy drawn from Paul's shift. Analysis of this section shows how initial hostility gives way to proclamation fostering an environment where relatives see faith lived out authentically over time.

What Insights from the Text Benefit Interactions with Friends.

Friends receive a different application because these ties allow for more open sharing of personal stories like Paul's account of his earlier life. The reading notes that Paul advanced in Judaism beyond many of his people which parallels how individuals might discuss growth in faith with peers who knew them before. Catholics can inspire friends by recounting moments of change to encourage mutual support without the intensity of family obligations. This section of the passage breaks down the move to Syria and Cilicia where he remained unknown by sight to the churches of Judea. Such anonymity reminds believers to let actions speak in friendships building trust through consistent kindness rather than immediate explanations. The result encourages lighter yet meaningful conversations that highlight ongoing conversion.

How Do Encounters with Neighbors Draw from the Preaching of Faith Once Destroyed.

The one who once was persecuting us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy. Neighbors often represent community ties where reputation matters and this quote underscores visible change that prompts others to glorify God. Catholics might apply the reading here by extending unexpected help or forgiveness in local matters turning past indifference into active care. The text analyzes the reaction of those who heard about Paul saying they glorified God because of me which models how small acts can inspire neighborhood harmony. This approach stays distinct from family or friends as it focuses on outward witness in less intimate settings fostering broader goodwill through everyday gestures.

Which Specific Quotes from the Passage Equip Catholics for Workplace Exchanges with Co-workers.

Key lines include you have heard no doubt of my earlier life in Judaism and I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it. These can guide co-workers by encouraging honest acknowledgment of past shortcomings when collaborating on projects. Another quote states but when God who had set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace was pleased to reveal his Son to me. This inspires professional interactions by reminding believers to credit divine grace amid career pressures rather than personal achievement alone. The passage further details how Paul did not go up to Jerusalem to those who were already apostles before him which suggests maintaining focus on one's own calling at work without unnecessary comparisons. Analysis reveals these elements promote integrity and encouragement in team environments where competition might otherwise dominate.

In what ways does the full arc of the reading support varied daily applications across all relationships.

The complete text from the initial persecution account through the journey to Arabia and the eventual glorification by others illustrates a progression from opposition to testimony. Catholics integrate this by adapting the themes of revelation and separation to each context ensuring family receives intimate healing while co-workers see professional steadiness. Transitions between sections emphasize that God's call operates independently yet impacts all spheres of life. This layered approach builds a cohesive witness that evolves naturally from personal reflection outward.

Faithful Catholics find in this passage a blueprint for living conversion that enriches every interaction with depth and purpose.

Thank you for praying today with RCatholicPrayer your fellow pilgrim on the path of repentance and conversion.

A fellow penitent seeking God's grace,

text:
Everyone knows Paul Revere's ride. Almost nobody knows Jack Jouett's. His was longer, harder, and he saved Thomas Jefferson.

June 1781. The war had come to Virginia hard. Cornwallis was tearing through the state, and Virginia's government, including Gov. Thomas Jefferson, had fled Richmond and moved to Charlottesville. Cornwallis saw a chance to end the rebellion in Virginia in one night. He sent Lt. Col. Banastre Tarleton, the most feared cavalry officer in America, with about 250 horsemen to ride to Charlottesville and capture the governor and the whole legislature in their beds.

On the night of June 3, Tarleton's column passed the Cuckoo Tavern in Louisa County. Sitting there was a 26 year old militia captain named Jack Jouett. He was about 6'4", rode a fast horse, and knew the country better than anyone. He watched the green-coated dragoons go by and figured out where they were headed.

Tarleton had the main road. So Jouett took the back trails. Around 40 miles through the woods, in the dark, on paths so overgrown that branches tore up his face. Accounts say he carried those scars the rest of his life.

He beat Tarleton by hours. Tarleton helped him without knowing it, stopping along the way to burn wagons and grab a few prominent men from their homes.

Around dawn on June 4, Jouett rode up the mountain to Monticello and woke Thomas Jefferson. Jefferson, cool as ever, reportedly offered him a glass of Madeira. Then he got his family out, gathered up papers, and stayed longer than he should have. He rode off into the woods just before the British got to his door.

Jouett didn't stop at Monticello. He rode down into Charlottesville and warned the legislators, many of them staying at the Swan Tavern, which belonged to his own father. They scrambled out of town and fled over the mountains to Staunton. Tarleton arrived to find most of the government gone. He caught only seven legislators. One of them was Daniel Boone.

There's a story that Jouett, wearing a fancy scarlet coat and a plumed hat, helped one wounded general, Edward Stevens, get away by drawing the dragoons after himself while Stevens, dressed plain, slipped off on a slow horse. The British chased the man who looked important.

Think about what he stopped. If Tarleton had grabbed Jefferson and the Virginia legislature that morning, the author of the Declaration of Independence would have been a prisoner, maybe sent to England, and Virginia's government would have collapsed in the middle of the war.

Virginia's legislature voted him a sword and a pair of pistols as thanks. He moved west to Kentucky, helped push for Kentucky statehood, and served in its legislature. His son Matthew became one of the best portrait painters in early America.

Revere got the poem. Jouett got almost forgotten. He deserves better.

text:
Nick Saban’s career path has shaped him into one of college football’s most renowned figures. After leaving the NFL, he embarked on a remarkable run in college football that included stints at LSU and Alabama, culminating in a record that few programs can match. Recently, Saban discussed why college football appeals to him more than the NFL, revealing a perspective grounded in personal fulfillment.

In a conversation with Theo Von, Saban explained that college football offers a different kind of gratification. While he appreciates the NFL’s competition and coaching challenges, he highlighted the greater self-gratification found in college—helping young players develop not just athletically, but personally and academically. His transition from the NFL to college was spurred by the opportunity to mentor student-athletes during their formative years, with many goals and aspirations still in front of them.

Saban’s journey in college football began to take shape after a successful stint at Michigan State, which led to him taking the LSU job in 2000. Even though LSU’s facilities and infrastructure were not impressive at the time, his wife, Terry, saw potential in the roster’s talent and athleticism. This insight helped convince him that LSU could have significant upside, and he proceeded to rebuild the program. Under his leadership, LSU captured its first consensus national championship since 1958 in 2003 and posted a 48-16 record over five seasons.

After LSU, Saban briefly returned to the NFL with the Miami Dolphins in 2005 and 2006, registering a 15–17 regular-season record. He soon returned to college football, this time to Alabama, where he would reiterate his commitment to shaping young people’s lives and achieving athletic excellence. He has described college coaching as the place where he feels his heart belongs and where he can most effectively influence student-athletes’ development.

Over the years, Saban has reflected that leaving LSU for the NFL was a misstep, even as he gained valuable NFL experience. He has stated that his preference for college stems from the ability to nurture players holistically—personally, academically, and athletically—an approach that he believes is best suited to long-term development.

College football has defined Saban’s legacy, and his record at LSU and Alabama stands as a testament to his influence and success in the sport.

text:
Ok- so I  ran the movie through a litmus test using the book- The Hidden War: Behind The Veil. (Link at bottom if you want it) This is what I got from a Spiritual Warfare context- it’s interesting. 

Step one: isolate the target. 
The tornado rips Dorothy out of Kansas and drops her in a world where nobody knows her, nobody can help her, and the only way home is a road I control. That’s the playbook — cut the believer off from their roots, their church, their family, their community, and leave them alone in enemy territory.

Step two: 
offer a counterfeit kingdom. The Emerald City looks green and perfect, but it’s all tinted glass. I don’t need to destroy the believer — I just need to redirect them. Give them a beautiful destination that never actually delivers. That’s the Great Deceiver’s signature: enlightenment without the cross, unity without the blood, peace without repentance.

Step three: 
attack the mind, the heart, and the will. The Scarecrow, the Tin Man, the Lion — three separate targets, three separate wounds. I don’t hit everything at once. I pick the weakest link and work it until the whole person collapses.

Step four: 
steal the authority. The Witch wants the shoes because the shoes are the power. The ruby slippers are the blood of Christ — the one thing that lets the believer walk through my territory untouched. If I can get those off her feet, she’s just another lost soul in Oz.

Step five: 
offer false deliverance. The Wizard’s balloon is the escape hatch — the promise of rescue that leaves you stranded. I always offer a way out that isn’t real. The real exit was on her feet the whole time.

That’s the whole strategy. Isolate, redirect, wound, steal, and offer a fake rescue. The movie isn’t entertainment — it’s a training manual.

Dorothy wins by refusing to play the game on my terms. She never fights the Witch head-on — she never tries to out-scheme the Wizard. She just keeps walking the road, keeps asking for help, and keeps trusting the one thing she was told.

The shoes were on her feet the entire time. She didn’t need the Wizard’s balloon, didn’t need the Emerald City’s approval, didn’t need anyone’s permission. The power was already hers — she just had to stop looking for it outside herself.

That’s the whole lesson. The believer doesn’t win by being stronger than the enemy. They win by remembering who they are and what they already carry. 

The blood of Christ isn’t something you earn — it’s something you already have. The exit was never in Oz. It was on her feet from the first step.

text:
To be fair, the Anglican bishop of Chelmsford has spoken clearly about the Green Party’s deeply troubling “Zionism is racism” motion. But where is the wider Christian response, and, as a Catholic, I particularly want to ask: where are our bishops? Because this is precisely the kind of moment for which bishops exist.

A major political party has adopted a proposition touching directly upon race, Jewish identity, nationhood, human dignity and the distinction between legitimate criticism of a state and prejudice against a people. Jewish members of the Green Party themselves warned that the motion risked making Jews feel unwelcome. That presents an extraordinary teaching moment & Catholics need our bishops not merely to comment on politics, but to help us think in a Christian way about questions like these: to explain what the Church teaches about racism and antisemitism, the dignity of peoples, justice for Palestinians, and the moral limits of political ideology.

This is episcopal leadership at its most necessary. Not party politics, but shepherds teaching their flock how Catholic principles illuminate a difficult and increasingly poisonous public debate. Silence leaves that formation to politicians and social media. Surely the Church has something better to offer?

text:
I bless thee   Michelle in the Name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit! Amen!
Heavenly Father, I lift this beloved one, Michelle, into Your loving hands, asking that Your healing touch restore her body completely. Remove all burn injuries, spinal fusion for scoliosis, heart problems including congestive heart failure, pulmonary embolisms, tumors, leukemia, cancer, disease, infirmary, injury of any sort, sickness, fatigue, or pain, and renew her strength, energy, and Grant wisdom and skill to the medical team, patience to this beloved one, and peace to her heart. Surround her with Your divine protection, and let Your presence comfort and reassure her. May Your grace and mercy flow through every part of Michelle’s being. In Jesus’ name I beg and pray, Amen.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:
Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of burn injuries, heart problems including congestive heart failure, spinal fusion for scoliosis, pulmonary embolisms,strokes, cancer, tumors, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, burn injuries, and surround   Michelle with Your gentle light, while completely healing   Michelle while filling her heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Amen.

Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, particularly Michelle, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal and protect  Michelle —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of David.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.
O Lord, hear my prayer.
And let my cry come unto Thee.
The Lord be with you all.
And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. We ask this through Christ Our Lord. Amen.

Prayer for possible any evil influence:

In His Name and by the power of His Cross and Blood, I ask Jesus Christ to bind any evil spirits, forces and powers of the earth, air, fire, water, and of the netherworld and all of the satanic forces of nature. By the power of the Holy Spirit and by His authority, I ask Jesus Christ to break any and all curses, hexes, vexes, jinks, spells, and all wrong prayers and words, and to send them all back to where they came from, if it be His Holy Will. I beseech Thee, Lord Jesus Christ, to protect us by pouring Thy Precious Blood on us; myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for; which Thou hast shed for us and I ask Thee to command that any departing spirits leave quietly, without disturbance, and go straight to Thy Cross to be disposed of as Thou sees fit. I ask Thee to bind any demonic interactions, interplay, or communications. I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. Amen.

Prayer In Case of Surgery

Lord Almighty, I lift up this beloved one, Michelle, as she faces surgery. Protect her, guide the hands of doctors and nurses, and grant wisdom in every decision. Remove fear, anxiety, and complications, replacing them with Your peace and assurance. Restore her health, strength, and vitality quickly, and surround her with Your loving presence. Comfort her heart, strengthen her spirit, and let Your healing flow through Michelle’s body. May they recover fully, trusting Your mercy and experiencing Your grace throughout this trial. Amen.

text: **Hamas (Harakat al-Muqawama al-Islamiya, or Islamic Resistance Movement) was founded in December 1987** during the First Intifada as the Palestinian branch/political arm of the Muslim Brotherhood in Gaza. Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, a cleric who had built social and charitable networks (including al-Mujamma al-Islami from the 1970s), was the key founder. Its 1988 charter called for the destruction of Israel and establishment of an Islamic society in historic Palestine.  ### Early Funding (Late 1980s–Early 2000s) Initial support came primarily from: - Palestinian expatriates and private donors in the Persian Gulf (especially Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states). - Charitable networks (*dawa*), mosques, and foundations that blended social welfare with political/military activity. Western-based charities (later designated by the U.S. as Hamas fronts, such as the Holy Land Foundation in the U.S., Interpal in the UK, and others in Europe) channeled funds.  Iran emerged as a major state sponsor in the early 1990s, providing funds (initially estimated around $30 million annually, rising toward $50 million by 2000), weapons, and training for Hamas members at Revolutionary Guard facilities. Hamas opened offices in Tehran; relations deepened despite the Sunni-Shiite divide because of shared opposition to Israel. Other early or intermittent support came from Syria (hosting leadership), Sudan, and private sources.  ### Path to the 2007 Takeover of Gaza Israel unilaterally disengaged from Gaza in 2005, withdrawing settlers and military. In the January 2006 Palestinian legislative elections, Hamas won a majority, defeating the long-dominant Fatah (the main faction of the Palestine Liberation Organization/Palestinian Authority). This reflected widespread dissatisfaction with Fatah corruption and governance failures.  The international community (U.S., EU, Quartet) imposed sanctions and withheld aid because Hamas refused to recognize Israel, renounce violence, or accept prior agreements. A national unity government formed in early 2007 under Saudi mediation, but power-sharing collapsed amid mutual distrust. Fatah controlled key security forces (with some U.S./Western training and support), while Hamas built its own Executive Force.  From 10–15 June 2007, intense fighting (the Battle of Gaza) erupted. Hamas forces rapidly overran Fatah strongholds, security headquarters, and government institutions across the Gaza Strip. They executed or expelled many Fatah officials and fighters. By 14–15 June, Hamas had full control of Gaza. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas (Fatah) dissolved the unity government, declared a state of emergency, dismissed Hamas Prime Minister Ismail Haniyeh, and appointed an emergency government in the West Bank under Salam Fayyad. This created the lasting split: Hamas ruling Gaza, Fatah/PA ruling the West Bank.  Hamas framed the takeover as defensive against alleged Fatah/U.S. plans to oust it; Fatah and Western governments called it a military coup.  ### Post-2007 Funding Sources Once in control of Gaza, Hamas’s finances shifted heavily toward territorial control while retaining external patrons:  - **Taxation and local revenue** became the largest ongoing source. Hamas levied taxes/fees on imports (via Israeli crossings and Egyptian tunnels/smuggling), businesses, goods (cigarettes, fuel, etc.), vehicle registration, licenses, and more. Estimates range from roughly $300–500+ million per year in the years before October 2023. Tunnel taxes alone were significant until Egypt cracked down.  - **Iran** remained a core backer of the military wing (Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades), providing funds (commonly estimated $70–100+ million annually, with some reports of higher or fluctuating amounts), weapons technology, training, and expertise. Support dipped during the Syrian civil war (when Hamas sided against the Assad regime) but recovered. Seized documents later detailed multi-year Iranian payments totaling hundreds of millions.  - **Qatar** became a major financial and political host. It provided hundreds of millions (later structured as ~$30 million per month in cash for fuel, salaries of civil servants, and needy families) starting after the takeover and accelerating from around 2012–2014, often with Israeli and U.S. knowledge/acquiescence as a stabilization measure. Qatar hosted Hamas’s political leadership (after it left Syria). Total Qatari transfers over the decade reached into the billions; internal documents indicated some funds supported “resistance” efforts.  - **Turkey** offered political support under Erdogan, hosted investment activities, and facilitated some financial networks.  - **Investment portfolio and other**: Hamas built a network of companies (real estate, mining, farming, construction) in Turkey, Sudan, Algeria, UAE, and elsewhere, valued by U.S. Treasury estimates at around $500 million. Cryptocurrency, money changers, and smuggling supplemented this. Diversion of international humanitarian aid (including some UNRWA and other flows) and Palestinian Authority salary/service transfers into Gaza also occurred.  Overall annual budgets in the later pre-2023 period were estimated in the hundreds of millions, with territorial taxes often the single largest component, followed by state sponsors (Iran for military priorities, Qatar for governance/cash flow). Israel’s policy of allowing Qatari cash transfers was explicitly intended in part to keep Hamas focused on governing rather than escalating, while maintaining separation from the West Bank PA—though this calculation failed with the October 7, 2023 attacks.  Hamas has been designated a terrorist organization by the U.S., EU, Israel, and others, which constrains formal banking channels and drives reliance on opaque methods. Funding patterns have adapted over time to sanctions, border controls, and conflicts, but the core mix of local extraction + Iranian military support + Qatari cash has been consistent since the Gaza takeover. (Grok)

text:
At six-thirty in the morning in Enid, Oklahoma, the back corner booth of the McDonald's is occupied by seven men who have survived five hundred years of collective American history.

Nobody tells them to purchase hashbrowns.

I sat two tables away with my black coffee, keeping my head down.

All seven men wore baseball caps embroidered with military campaign ribbons: Korea, Vietnam, Desert Storm, and one cap that simply read Caterpillar Diesel Engines.

They did not look at smartphones. They did not discuss cryptocurrency.

On the table sat seven identical white paper cups of black coffee, three folded copies of the county newspaper, and an open cardboard box of apple fritters someone had brought from the grocery store.

The man in the center, whose hearing aid whistled like a tea kettle, tapped the table with a gnarly knuckle.

Bud, the center man said, did they pave the culvert on Route 412 yet?

Bud, who was eighty-two and wore a khaki jacket with oil stains, shook his head once.

Not yet, Wayne, Bud said. State highway department says next Thursday. But the gravel they dumped is washing into Miller's ditch.

A third man, Earl, grunted into his napkin.

Miller shouldn't have planted his clover that close to the easement anyway, Earl said. He did that in ninety-four and flooded his tractor.

Silence fell across the table. All seven men took a coordinated sip of coffee.

My skin prickled with awe.

This was not a social breakfast. This was the clandestine High Council of Elders. The municipal government of Oklahoma was a decorative illusion; these seven warriors held the water rights, the ditch topography, and the collective memory of every broken axle since the Eisenhower administration.

I stood up. I straightened my kimono.

I approached the booth, dropped to one knee on the linoleum, and offered my wooden tray.

Honored generals, I said in a low voice, what is your command regarding the culvert? Shall I secure the gravel before the weekend rains?

Wayne adjusted his hearing aid. He looked at my topknot. He looked at Bud.

Bud, Wayne said, who is your friend?

He's a samurai, Wayne, Bud said without looking up from the sports section.

Wayne pushed the box of apple fritters two inches toward me.

Take a fritter, son, Wayne said. And tell Miller to dig out his ditch before Friday. The weather service doesn't know what it's talking about.

text:
TapeOut 24h Recap · Community Foundation Proposed, Blonskr Pledges 700 BEM

Oct 5, 15:26 UTC: @BruceBlue formally proposed a TapeOut Community Foundation. The proposal defines its role: not a controlling body, but a support layer for developers, open-source projects, TAP audits, and external partnerships. He outlined a flywheel: Developer → Launchpad → Circuit Reuse → BEM Consumption → Economic Activity → More Developers. A separate TAP Labs would also be formed. Core principle: Donation ≠ Governance Power.

Oct 5, 16:42 UTC: @Blonskr responded with a clear stance:

1. Supports 2–3 independent community foundations running in parallel, not a single one
2. Neither he nor the core dev team will participate in any foundation's management — they stay on tech
3. Personal donation: 700 BEM

—

Community donation pledges

Within 24 hours of the proposal, multiple community members pledged contributions. All are verbal commitments — no on-chain transfers yet, and the multisig address has not been published:

Blonskr 700 BEM · @yztc123 200 BEM · @CryptoLoser9 70 BEM + volunteered for the team · @DreamXThat 50 BEM · @pparkdd 50 BEM · @bigberg688 15 BEM · @HanLiDV 10 BEM · @fan_zhe33057 5 BEM · @zhngshh52558499 one 5788.30 miner

Korean holders also showed up. BruceBlue's latest reply says the multisig and rules should be ready this week.

—

Hackathon · deadline Oct 9 HKT (~3 days left)

@dc_cap's OrderGuard: Oct 6 update — all 5 circuits fabricated and verified on X Layer. The marketplace page now includes gate-level circuit visualization and an online designer. Toolchain is open-sourced. Demo: https://t.co/2JSDjDqLT5.

@OKIGNIxXRAY's XRAYGATE: posted a warning that all tokens named XRAY on-chain are not his. The official version comes after the holiday; only this account is legitimate.

New entry: @tapeupio's TapeUP — connects metro station onboarding with tape-out, minting circuit NFTs from designated circuits, using containers for site identity.

—

Protocol explainers

@TapeOutWorld posted a series of technical threads on Oct 6. Key points:

DeWEB scripts can only load files already on-chain on that site — no external calls.

Circuits compute only. No outbound calls, no state writes.

New Processors have selectable capacity — compared to 4004's 2,300 transistors, Pentium's 3.1M, and M1's 16B.

Any BNB Chain contract can call a Circuit as logic, with predictable gas costs.

Cloned Processors from the same factory share identical bytecode; their circuits can call each other.

LATCH: 1 bit per block, updates once per block.

—

X Layer

Official miners: still not cross-chain to X Layer. A community member suggested "buy back miners and burn them." Blonskr replied: "That's a fresh idea. Let me look into it."

OKX Wallet: @yeerya noted that the top 3 apps in OKX Wallet are all from TapeOut, and posted a miner tutorial. @CryptoLoser9 shared a screenshot of the wallet rankings.

—

Community pulse

Bulls shifted focus from yesterday's six-item roadmap to "who funds the ecosystem." The donation relay dominated discourse. Blonskr reiterated: "The next 2 months will bring earth-shaking changes to TapeOut" and "going all out." @dc_cap commented that "not participating in management" looks more like long-termism than any roadmap item.

Bears were sparse and scattered. @GKCDAO acknowledged the price drop and FUD but said "keep building." @daci616390 offered a structural critique: trading transistors breeds researchers and builders, trading BEM breeds holders and traders — and the latter eventually mine-and-dump.

No new on-chain buyback/burn since Oct 4's 604.89 BEM, cumulative 2,438.73 BEM.

What to watch: multisig publication and first on-chain donation, delivery on the six roadmap items, and future burn frequency.

—

Data: X search + Grok, covering Oct 5–6. Price: ~$25.6–$31 range. Third-party snapshots — ApeSpace: $30.40 / 24h +12.5%; NexFlow: Oct 5 $31.24 → Oct 6 $27.67 / ~$8.11M market cap / 8,252 holders (vs. 8,132 the day before).

Donation figures come from verbal pledge posts; none have settled on-chain. On-chain records are authoritative.

Community content, not an official TapeOut publication. For ecosystem tracking only, not investment advice.

On October 6, U.S. stocks hit new highs again. The S&P 500 touched about 7,830 intraday, and the Nasdaq set records for a second straight day, driven mainly by the artificial-intelligence rally. Nvidia’s market value neared $6 trillion, up about 6% this month, and the stock now accounts for more than 8% of the S&P 500.

The Dow lagged, roughly 5% below its August peak. The 10-year Treasury yield remained near 5.3%, its highest level since 2002, weighing on non-tech sectors. Falling oil prices offered some relief, with Brent crude down to about $98 a barrel.

Last week’s soft jobs data reduced expectations of a Fed rate hike in October. Attention now turns to third-quarter earnings: analysts expect S&P 500 profit growth above 25%. The index is highly concentrated in a few names, including Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft, so results that miss AI-related expectations could bring sharper swings.

text:
$VST (Vistra) is up around 9.56% today to ~$158.70, riding the read-through from Constellation's Google nuclear deal one day after a reported $4 billion-plus federal loan lifted the stock.

Here's the complete picture:

Today's fresh developments:

The Constellation-Google read-through:

Google signed a 20-year agreement with Constellation Energy to fund 890 megawatts of nuclear uprates on the PJM grid, and nuclear-heavy generators rallied with it. Constellation jumped about 12% and Talen Energy gained 7% or more. Vistra isn't a party to the deal and is trading on the sector read-through.

Yesterday's catalyst still in play:

On Monday, Vistra rose 3.48% to $144.89 on heavy volume of 10.75 million shares, more than double the average. A Bloomberg report said the Trump administration is expected to offer Vistra roughly $4 billion in federal loan funding for infrastructure and upgrades at three nuclear plants: Perry and Davis-Besse in Ohio, and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania.

A two-day move of about 13%:

Vistra closed at $140.02 on Friday. Today's range runs from $148.52 to $160.70, putting the stock back above its roughly $155 200-day moving average.

The context:

Big Tech is increasingly paying for new nuclear supply, and the federal government is backing nuclear upgrades with loans. That points to the same bottleneck: AI data centers need power, and existing reactors are the fastest way to get more of it onto the grid.

The numbers:

→ Market cap: ~$53.2 billion. P/E: ~24.5. Beta: ~1.38

→ 52-week range: $132.66 to $217.10, so VST still trades about 27% below its high

→ Consensus rating: Buy. Average analyst targets run roughly $212 to $222 depending on the source

→ TD Cowen maintained a Buy with a $221 target on Aug. 19

→ Next earnings: November 6, 2026, about 31 days away

The reality check:

The federal loan is described as expected, not finalized, and Vistra's own news flow in the last two days has been about financing and sector sentiment rather than new contracts. Some earnings-based models point to weaker revision trends and execution risk, and Constellation's rally is a reminder of how uneven contract-driven moves in this group have been.

Up 9.6% today. Up about 13% in two sessions. A reported $4 billion federal loan, a Google nuclear deal next door, and a stock still 27% below its high.

text:
Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., sparked bipartisan backlash after posting on X that every Muslim elected official in the United States is a security threat, a claim she made in the wake of Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s Democratic primary win.
Mace wrote on X on Friday, August 7, 2026, “Every single Muslim holding public office in America is a trojan horse, and a threat to both national security and our republic. We refuse to be silent.” She posted the message roughly two months after she finished fifth in South Carolina’s Republican gubernatorial primary. She went on to name New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and El-Sayed specifically, telling followers Americans should be “very concerned” about the two progressive Muslim politicians.
When a British commentator criticized the post, Mace doubled down, writing, “If not wanting to be blown up, st*bbed, or rammed by a car by a radical Islamist in the United States of America makes us Islamophobes, then so be it.”
Two days later, CNN anchor Omar Jimenez pressed her on the remarks during an appearance on “CNN Newsroom,” asking whether she meant every Muslim elected official. Mace replied, “Uhh, that’s not what I said, that’s not what I said. I do think we have a real issue with radical Islamic—” Jimenez interjected, “I mean, it sounds like that’s what you’re saying,” to which Mace responded, “No, I was talking about elected officials.”
Democratic Rep. Pramila Jayapal of Washington condemned the post, writing on X, “This is absolutely disgusting and dangerous. Republicans must denounce this blatant Islamophobia. To Muslim communities across America: I will always stand with you.” Mace answered Jayapal directly, writing in part, “Islam must be confronted and Islam must be removed from civil society in the US.” California state Sen. Scott Wiener also criticized Mace, accusing her of demonizing Muslims. Neither Mace’s campaign nor her congressional office has offered further clarification on the original post

text:
Since August 3, a Florida condo can follow the state reserve law to the letter and still be unfinanceable with a conventional loan. The statute asks for one thing. Fannie Mae now asks for the opposite.

Florida's reserve study law requires every SIRS to include a baseline funding plan: a schedule that keeps the reserve balance above zero each year. Boards aim at that, because the statute names it.

Fannie Mae is where it breaks. On applications dated on or after August 3, lenders may no longer use the baseline funding method. The budget has to fund the highest recommended allocation in the study. Same date, Limited Review was retired, so every conventional condo loan now gets a Full Review: reserves, deferred maintenance and special assessments all get read, even on a 25% down file with an 800 score.

On January 4, 2027, the minimum reserve allocation on a Full Review goes from 10% to 15% of budgeted assessment income.

A building can pass its milestone inspection, do everything the state asked, and still come back ineligible. When that list last surfaced publicly, in March 2025, 1,438 of the 5,175 buildings on it were in Florida.

Before you write an offer on a condo here, get the SIRS and the adopted budget, not the summary, and check one thing: does the budget fund the study's highest recommended number, or the baseline one? That answer tells you more about your payment than the rate does.

I can usually still place a non-warrantable building with a portfolio lender: more down, higher rate. But that's the fallback, not the plan. An underfunded building isn't really a financing problem. It's a deferred bill with your name on it.

Pinellas and Hillsborough condo owners: baseline, or full recommendation? If you don't know, that's your question for the board this week.

text:
Rocks for brains- Greg Abbott does not personally make money from private prisons that lock up children.
The claim mixes three different things and treats them as one personal payday.
Texas’s own secure juvenile facilities are run by the state. The Texas Juvenile Justice Department operates the state youth prisons (Evins, Gainesville, Giddings, Mart, Ron Jackson, and new sites under construction). Those are public facilities, not private-prison companies paying the governor. Local detention is mostly county-run; some counties use private vendors, but that money does not go to Abbott.
Family and immigration detention centers that hold children or families, such as the Dilley center in South Texas, are federal ICE contracts. CoreCivic and GEO Group are paid by the federal government, not by a personal cut to the governor. Abbott has offered state land and state prison beds to help federal immigration enforcement. That is a government arrangement, not personal income.
Campaign money is not the same as personal profit. Political attacks in the 2026 governor’s race have said CoreCivic and GEO Group gave large sums to the Republican Governors Association, which supports Republican governors, and that donors tied to the industry gave Abbott’s campaign on the order of a few hundred thousand dollars. Campaign contributions are regulated political funds. They are not salary, dividends, or ownership income. Public searches of his personal financial disclosures do not show him holding GEO or CoreCivic stock. (By contrast, reporting on President Trump’s ethics filings has described trades in those stocks; that reporting is about Trump, not Abbott.)
What the record does show is the opposite of a juvenile-prison profit motive: in 2022 Abbott’s office transferred about $30 million out of the Texas Juvenile Justice Department’s budget to help fund Operation Lone Star border operations. Critics, including the Houston Chronicle editorial board, argued that move made conditions in the youth system worse.
So the statement is false both as a claim of personal profit and as a description of who runs and pays for Texas youth lockups.

The Inaugural Tejunto Festival comes to Mission, Texas, on Saturday, October 10, celebrating the vibrant musical traditions of Tejano and Conjunto music. The festival takes place at Leo Peña “La Placita” Park, in the heart of downtown Mission, creating a welcoming setting for families, music lovers, and the community to come together. The event celebrates the unique musical blend captured by the name “Tejunto”—Tejano plus Conjunto—with a full day of entertainment beginning with a youth talent show and continuing into an evening concert.

Set against the lively atmosphere of downtown Mission, the festival promises an opportunity to experience the sounds, culture, and traditions that have shaped South Texas music. Leo Peña “La Placita” Park, located near the intersection of Business 83 and Conway Avenue, provides an ideal community gathering place for this inaugural celebration. Whether you're a longtime fan of Tejano and Conjunto music or discovering these sounds for the first time, the Tejunto Festival offers a day of music, culture, and community in Mission.

text:
Today I am writing about Kaigaku, someone about whom I cannot really say much good.

Kaigaku grew up as an orphan and stole to survive. Eventually, he became one of the orphans under Gyomei’s care. One day, Kaigaku stole the group's meager funds and was caught in the act.

The other orphans drove him away, and that very night, he was discovered by a demon. To save his own life, he offered to lead the demon to the orphans and Gyomei. Kaigaku destroyed the wisteria, allowing the demon to enter the temple.

With Kaigaku’s help, seven of the eight orphans in the temple were killed; Gyomei was nearly executed and, from that moment on, lost his trust in humanity. Kaigaku himself felt no remorse; for him, only his own survival mattered, at any cost.

Eventually, he was taken in by the former Thunder Hashira, Jigoro Kuwajima, and trained alongside Zenitsu. Zenitsu was difficult to train due to his fearful nature and lack of self-confidence, yet he managed to master the First Form of Thunder Breathing.

Kaigaku, on the other hand, found the training easier and mastered the Second through Sixth Forms of Thunder Breathing. He looked down on Zenitsu, believing he did not deserve any of the attention Jigoro gave him.

Since neither of them had mastered every form of Thunder Breathing, Jigoro wanted both of his protégés to become his successors. While Zenitsu defended his fellow student in front of others, Kaigaku’s resentment toward both Zenitsu and Jigoro continued to fester. 

While on patrol, Kaigaku encounters Kokushibo and begs for his life. Kokushibo gives him some of his blood, warning him that he can say goodbye to his head if he spills even a single drop🩸. Because Kaigaku is a Demon Slayer who has mastered a Breathing Style, his transformation into a demon takes longer than usual.

Upon learning of his student's cowardly behavior, Jigoro commits seppuku. Zenitsu finds out what happened and begins to train; his personality shifts, he becomes serious and vows revenge. In a short span of time, Kaigaku likely devours many humans and rises to the rank of Upper Moon Six.

The two students eventually clash within the Infinity Castle. Kaigaku shows no respect for either Zenitsu or Jigoro; he even goes so far as to mock and insult his late former master. Zenitsu decapitates Kaigaku using a newly created seventh form of Thunder Breathing.

Before Kaigaku dies, Yushiro makes it clear to him why he ultimately failed: he had thought only of himself his entire life, never of others; he never did anything for anyone else, acting solely for his own benefit.

To me, Kaigaku is one of the most unlikable characters in Demon Slayer; he abandons and sacrifices everyone for his own gain. He has absolutely no qualms about killing and devouring humans to further his own interests. #KimetsuNoYaiba #DemonSlayer #KnY

text:
(H) Pope Saint Innocent I

 “In seeking the things of God . . . you have acknowledged that judgment is to be referred to us [the pope], and have shown that you know that is owed to the Apostolic See [Rome], if all of us placed in this position are to desire to follow the apostle himself [Peter] from whom the episcopate itself and the total authority of this name have emerged” (Letters 29:1 [A.D. 408]).

(I) Saint Augustine

“Among these [apostles] Peter alone almost everywhere deserved to represent the whole Church. Because of that representation of the Church, which only he bore, he deserved to hear ‘I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven’” (Sermons 295:2 [A.D. 411]).

“Some things are said which seem to relate especially to the apostle Peter, and yet are not clear in their meaning unless referred to the Church, which he is acknowledged to have represented in a figure on account of the primacy which he bore among the disciples. Such is ‘I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven,’ and other similar passages” (Commentary on Psalm 108 1 [A.D. 415]).

“Who is ignorant that the first of the apostles is the most blessed Peter?” (Commentary on John 56:1 [A.D. 416]).

(J) Council of Ephesus 

“Philip, presbyter and legate of [Pope Celestine I] said: ‘We offer our thanks to the holy and venerable synod, that when the writings of our holy and blessed pope had been read to you . . . you joined yourselves to the holy head also by your holy acclamations. For your blessedness is not ignorant that the head of the whole faith, the head of the apostles, is blessed Peter the apostle’” (Acts of the Council, session 2 [A.D. 431]).
“Philip, the presbyter and legate of the Apostolic See [Rome] said: ‘There is no doubt, and in fact it has been known in all ages, that the holy and most blessed Peter, prince and head of the apostles, pillar of the faith, and foundation of the Catholic Church, received the keys of the kingdom from our Lord Jesus Christ, the Savior and Redeemer of the human race, and that to him was given the power of loosing and binding sins: who down even to today and forever both lives and judges in his successors’” (ibid., session 3).

(K) Pope Saint Leo I

“Our Lord Jesus Christ . . . has placed the principal charge on the blessed Peter, chief of all the apostles, and from him as from the head wishes his gifts to flow to all the body, so that anyone who dares to secede from Peter’s solid rock may understand that he has no part or lot in the divine mystery. He wished him who had been received into partnership in his undivided unity to be named what he himself was, when he said: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church’ [Matt. 16:18], that the building of the eternal temple might rest on Peter’s solid rock, strengthening his Church so surely that neither could human rashness assail it nor the gates of hell prevail against it” (Letters 10:1 [A.D. 445).

(L) Saint Hilary of Poitiers 

“Peter to whom previously He had given the keys of the kingdom of heaven, upon whom he was going to build His Church against which the gates of hell would not prevail, what he bound or loosed on carth would remain in heaven either bound or loosed... He was to suffer so much for the salvation of the human race that he named Peter, the first confessor of the Son of God, the foundation of the Church, the door-keeper of the heavenly kingdom and in earthly affairs the judge of heaven in triumph over Satan." (“Treatise on the Psalms,” [A.D. 360]).”

text:
National Orange Wine Day🍷🍊🍷🍇🍷🌿🍇🧡🍷😋

National Orange Wine Day, observed annually on October 6, celebrates a distinctive style of wine made from white grapes fermented with their skins. Despite its name, orange wine contains no oranges; the extended skin contact gives it a deeper golden, amber, or auburn color and a bolder character than many white wines.

While many people might believe that orange wine is a new and trendy part of modern culture, it’s actually a product that has been around for thousands of years! Made from white grapes but, unlike white wine, this version includes the skin in the fermentation process, which is how red wines are made.

Dating back to approximately 6000 BC, orange wine likely hails from the area that is now the country of Georgia, near the Black Sea – widely believed to have been the place where winemaking was born!

The unique flavor profile of orange wines is a bit more like white than red, but it offers stronger aromas and flavor notes.

text:
SOURCE FEARED REPERCUSSIONS AFTER BROADMOOR LINKED EMAIL SHARED EXPLICIT VOTING RECOMMENDATIONS

COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. — A source was concerned enough about a political communication bearing The Broadmoor’s name to come forward.

They were also concerned enough about potential repercussions to insist that their identity remain confidential.

The documents they provided deserve scrutiny.

Jefferson County Dispatch News reviewed screenshots of an October 5, 2026 email bearing The Broadmoor’s name and the voters’ guide attached to it.

The email does not simply encourage people to research the election.

It directs recipients to a guide containing explicit recommendations on how to vote.

The message is addressed:

“To: All Concerned”

Its subject is:

“Voters’ Guide”

And its greeting is unmistakable:

“Dear Broadmoor Family:”

The message describes this year’s Colorado ballot as unusually complicated and confusing before telling recipients:

“So, we want to share with you a voters’ guide that was published in the Colorado Springs Gazette which we believe cuts through the advocacy and presents a balanced view of the issues and what is at stake.”

The message continues by saying the guide is being shared in hopes recipients find it helpful as they decide how they wish to vote.

It is signed:

“Jack”

At the bottom appear the words:

“THE BROADMOOR”

Then comes the attachment.

And that is where this becomes more than an innocuous reminder to participate in an election.

THE GUIDE TELLS READERS WHICH SIDE TO SUPPORT

The attached guide contains explicit YES/for and NO/against recommendations.

It recommends YES on:

Amendment 81
Amendment 82
Amendment 83
Amendment 84
Amendment 85
Amendment 86
Proposition 132
Proposition 133
Proposition 134
Proposition 135
Proposition 136
School District 11 4A

It recommends NO on:

Amendment 87
Proposition NN
Proposition 137
Ballot Issue 7A

Those are not neutral descriptions of ballot questions.

They are recommendations.

And they were attached to a message bearing The Broadmoor’s name that addressed its audience as the “Broadmoor Family.”

That distinction matters.

THE POWER IMBALANCE CANNOT SIMPLY BE IGNORED

Private businesses and their leadership are entitled to political opinions.

That is not the troubling part of this story.

The troubling question is what happens when political recommendations enter a workplace relationship.

An employer does not communicate with an employee as an ordinary stranger.

One controls employment.

One controls pay.

One may influence promotions, schedules, discipline and continued employment.

That inherent imbalance makes political communications from an employer fundamentally different from an endorsement appearing in a newspaper or campaign advertisement.

Even without an explicit command to vote a particular way, employees can reasonably wonder why their employer is sending them material recommending specific votes and whether those recommendations represent something expected of them.

The source who brought these documents forward expressed precisely that concern.

They did not want to be identified.

They did not want the origin of the material disclosed.

They specifically cited concern about potential repercussions.

Jefferson County Dispatch News is honoring that request.

THE DOCUMENTS DEMAND ANSWERS

There are basic questions The Broadmoor should be able to answer.

Who authorized this message?

Who sent it?

Who received it?

Was it sent to employees?

How many people received it?

Did The Broadmoor endorse the voting recommendations in the attached guide?

Why was a guide containing explicit political recommendations distributed through a communication bearing The Broadmoor’s name?

What policies govern political communications involving employees?

What protections exist for employees who disagree with the political positions contained in material distributed to them?

And perhaps most importantly, why should any worker have to wonder whether disagreeing with political material associated with their employer could affect their job?

NO RESPONSE FROM THE BROADMOOR

Jefferson County Dispatch News contacted The Broadmoor before publication and gave the organization an opportunity to explain the communication and answer questions about its distribution.

As of publication, The Broadmoor had not responded.

Silence does not establish wrongdoing.

Neither do these documents, standing alone, establish that anyone was threatened, coerced, ordered to vote a particular way or that any law was violated.

But those limitations do not make the documents insignificant.

The evidence we reviewed shows an email bearing The Broadmoor’s name addressing recipients as the “Broadmoor Family,” saying “we want to share with you” a voters’ guide and attaching a document containing explicit YES and NO voting recommendations.

Those facts warrant an explanation.

Employees should never have to guess whether political recommendations associated with the organization controlling their livelihood are merely information or something more.

The Broadmoor has been offered the opportunity to explain exactly what happened.

So far, it has chosen not to do so.

Jefferson County Dispatch News will update this story if The Broadmoor responds.

Source: Email and attached voters’ guide reviewed by Jefferson County Dispatch News. The attached material identifies the Colorado Springs Gazette as the source of the voters’ guide. The Broadmoor was contacted for comment before publication and had not responded as of publication.

text:
Off-market deals have a reputation for being cheaper than marketed ones. In our experience, the discount is the part that rarely shows up.

An off-market deal is one a seller shares with a handful of buyers instead of running a full broker process. Fewer bidders means less competition. It also means nothing tests the price. A marketed process forces a seller to see what ten or twenty buyers will actually pay. Off-market, the seller often starts from the number they hoped to get, and nobody pushes back except you.

Take an illustrative property with $1.8 million of NOI that would likely trade around $30 million in a full process, a 6.0% cap rate. Off-market, the seller asks $31 million. That feels like access, but it is a $1 million premium, and the going-in cap rate drops to about 5.8%. On a deal that has to clear today's borrowing costs, giving up 20 basis points of yield matters every year of the hold.

Done carefully, though, off-market can be worth pursuing. What it usually offers is speed and certainty. A seller facing a loan maturity, a partnership dispute or a 1031 deadline may care more about closing on a known date than squeezing out the last dollar. A buyer who can show committed equity and a clean record of closing can earn a fair price that way.

In Houston right now, with joint venture and high net worth equity hard to raise, I am not interested in overpaying to win any deal, marketed or not. So we underwrite an off-market deal against the same comps we would use if twenty buyers were looking at it, and we walk if the price only works because nobody else saw it.

More on how we source and buy deals to come. Follow along.

text:
I actually understand this perspective, especially if you're a single person living alone. Buying groceries isn't automatically cheaper just because you're buying and cooking at home.

If you buy a whole basket of tomatoes, a big bag of rice, vegetables, meat, oil, bread, drinks and other ingredients without having a proper meal plan, some of those things can spoil before you finish them. Add gas, electricity, transportation, cooking time and the temptation to order food when you're too tired to cook, and suddenly that “cheaper” grocery shopping doesn't look so cheap anymore. 😂

But I also think the problem is more about HOW you shop than groceries themselves. A single person doesn't necessarily need to shop like a family of five. Buy according to your actual consumption, focus on foods with longer shelf lives, portion your proteins, plan your meals and avoid buying things simply because they look affordable in bulk.

For example, buying a 10kg bag of rice may look cheaper per kilogram, but if it takes you many months to finish it and you don't even eat rice that often, the savings may not mean much. Sometimes buying smaller quantities that match your lifestyle is actually the smarter financial decision.

So I wouldn't say groceries are always cheaper than eating out. I'd say intentional grocery shopping can be cheaper, but careless grocery shopping can be surprisingly expensive.

And honestly, this is one reason I believe foodstuff vendors should stop just selling products and start helping customers shop according to their household size, budget and actual needs. You shouldn't have to spend ₦100k stocking your kitchen when what you genuinely need can be curated around your budget.

It's not just about buying more. It's about buying what you'll actually use. 🛒❤️

Prompt (GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst):
Professional anime character design illustration.
