Front-facing enough that the face reads clearly.

Original character "Rivet": a 19-year-old scrapyard mechanic and robot builder, tomboyish, confident, with a big crooked grin.

HEAD: a messy short wolf-cut in bright mint green with a darker teal underlayer and a few spiky flyaway strands; oversized chunky welding goggles with round amber lenses and a thick black strap pushed up on her forehead; big over-ear headphones in hazard yellow resting around her neck.
FACE: warm light skin, a constellation of freckles across the nose, a small white band-aid on the bridge of her nose, large sharp eyes with hot-pink irises, thick confident eyebrows, a wide toothy grin with one small fang, a little grease smudge on one cheek.
OUTFIT: a huge boxy padded work jacket in hazard yellow, worn slipping off her left shoulder, two horizontal black-and-silver reflective tape stripes around each sleeve, chunky utility pockets, a round mint patch with a simple gear icon on the chest; underneath a white ribbed tank top; charcoal-grey cargo shorts with yellow webbing straps and a tool belt with a few small tools; her right forearm and hand are a sleek mechanical prosthetic in glossy white ceramic panels with thin mint seam lines and black joints; a black fingerless glove on the left hand; mismatched knee socks, one mint and one hot pink; very chunky white high-top work boots with thick yellow treaded soles and fat yellow laces.
POSE: weight on one leg, left hand on hip, the white mechanical right hand resting a big oversized steel wrench on her shoulder, a slight lean toward the viewer, cocky and friendly.

STYLE: top-tier professional character designer's key illustration, the quality of a premium action game's character reveal art. Bold graphic urban anime style: thick confident black ink outlines with varied weight, flat cel colours with crisp two-tone shading, small halftone dot accents inside the shadows, sharp angular shape language, a very strong readable silhouette. Strict limited palette: hazard yellow, mint green, clean white and charcoal grey, with hot pink as the single accent. Clean, crisp, high resolution. No text, no letters, no logo, no brand marks, no signature, no watermark, no background objects, only a faint soft contact shadow under the boots.

2. Redesign
Prompt (GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, image 1 = the design, image 2 = a Krea 2 Medium version for style):
Final redesign pass by a top professional character designer. Image 1 is the design and anatomy of Rivet: keep her pose, proportions, mint wolf-cut, amber goggles, yellow headphones, boxy hazard-yellow work jacket with reflective sleeve stripes and mint gear patch, white tank top, charcoal cargo shorts with yellow straps and tool belt, white mechanical right arm with mint seams, fingerless glove, mismatched mint and pink socks, chunky white work boots with yellow soles and laces, the big wrench on her shoulder. Image 2 is the rendering style to adopt: thick confident black ink outlines, flat bold colour fills, crisp two-tone cel shadows, small halftone dot accents, graphic poster-like shapes.

Redraw image 1 in the style of image 2. One single full-body character on a pure flat white background, three-quarter front view, the whole figure visible with white margins.

Improvements:
- Warm, saturated hazard yellow on the jacket (not neon lime), clean flat fills, no dirt texture on clothes; only one small grease smudge on her cheek.
- Face: extremely appealing and charismatic, large sharp hot-pink eyes with bright highlights, freckles, the white band-aid across her nose, a big confident toothy grin with one fang.
- Slightly stylized proportions: a touch larger head and hands, chunky boots, strong readable silhouette.
- Lineart with real weight variation, like a professional illustrator's finished character reveal art.

Strict palette: hazard yellow, mint green, clean white, charcoal grey, hot pink accent. No text, no letters, no logos, no brand marks, no watermark, only a faint contact shadow.

3. Close-up
Prompt (GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, image 1 = the redesign):
Using image 1 as the exact character design and art style, draw a waist-up portrait of the same character, Rivet, as an animation close-up reference sheet. Front view, facing the viewer directly and making eye contact, centered, on a pure flat white background. Landscape framing: the top of her messy mint hair and the amber goggles near the top edge, cut at the waist at the bottom. Both hands held open in front of her chest, palms up, as if about to offer something: the glossy white mechanical right hand with mint seams and the left hand in a black fingerless glove; nothing in them. Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF) filed an emergency application with Justice Elena Kagan on behalf of K.M.K. and her mother, Stephanie Lynne Brown. The filing asks for an injunction pending appeal in K.M.K. v. Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA). The plaintiff is listed only as K.M.K. She is Kallie Keeler, the Puyallup-area wrestler who has spoken publicly about here experience in being allegedly sexually assaulted by a trans athlete during a match.

Keeler has been on the mat since she was 4. Wrestling was the season she waited for all year. She has not competed in a WIAA event since leaving the team in January, and she has said she is unsure she will return if she can be paired against a male again without notice.

📷
FAMILY FILES LAWSUIT ALLEGING DAUGHTER WAS SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE DURING GIRLS' COMPETITION

📷
The application says Keeler was 15 when she wrestled for third place at the Lady Jag Kickoff on Dec. 6, 2025, a girls’ tournament at Emerald Ridge High School. She and her mother say they were not told her opponent was male. During the match, they allege, the opponent penetrated her. Another team’s coach told her afterward that the opponent was male, the family says.

When Brown asked for a guarantee that her daughter would not have to face a male without penalty, and for notice so she could opt out, the district refused. It offered forfeiture if Keeler already knew the opponent was male. It said gender-identity information would be kept confidential.

"No girl should have to choose between playing the sports she loves and her safety," the application says. It asks the Court to bar officials from forcing Keeler to wrestle a male while the appeal goes forward, or at least to require notice and a no-penalty opt-out.

Washington state girls' wrestler Kallie Keeler (Alliance Defending Freedom)

INSIDE THE SUPREME COURT BATTLE TO 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS'

The defendants are the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association, the Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction, Superintendent Chris Reykdal, and the Puyallup School District. The athlete and the athlete’s family are not parties.

📷
"The WIAA remains committed to following Washington State law which permits student-athletes to participate in sports consistent with the gender with which they identify," the organization said in a statement to OutKick. "If state law changes in the future, the WIAA holds the authority to revise policies as necessary to remain in compliance with state law.

"The WIAA will not comment further on a matter in litigation."

A federal judge in Tacoma denied a preliminary injunction on Aug. 23. The Ninth Circuit denied an emergency injunction on Sept. 25, calling the request a mandatory injunction and finding no likelihood of success strong enough to justify relief before the season. Wrestling in Washington opens in mid-November. ADF says that without an order now, Keeler loses the season Title IX is supposed to protect.

The filing leans on the Supreme Court’s June 30 decision in West Virginia v. B.P.J., which held that states may limit girls’ teams to biological females, and on Mirabelli v. Bonta, a March parental-rights order.

The U.S. Department of Education opened a Title IX investigation into the district in February. Two Rogers High School administrators were later charged with failing to make a mandatory report. Prosecutors did not charge the opponent.

The district has previously declined to comment, citing student privacy and litigation. OutKick sought comment from the Puyallup School District and the Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction on the Supreme Court application.

text:
Rubio’s "Not on the Table": A Cold Verdict Ending Ukraine’s NATO Dream

The remark U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio made to reporters in Iceland was as calm as an obituary:

"NATO membership is not on the table as we speak."

He added that Washington is "focused only on ending this conflict right now." When asked whether Ukraine should become a NATO member, Rubio offered a classic politician’s evasion: "There is no yes-or-no answer to that question."

No yes-or-no answer. For Ukraine, that means "no."

🚪 A Door Never Meant to Open

Rubio’s statement is not a policy shift; it is a belated admission of the actual policy reality.

Since 2022, NATO’s official stance has been that "Ukraine’s future lies in NATO." The 2008 Bucharest Summit declaration stated in black and white that Ukraine "will become a member of NATO." Ukraine enshrined its goal of joining NATO in its constitution in 2019. As late as August 2026, Zelenskyy was still saying that Ukraine "would not seek alternatives to NATO membership" and that joining the alliance would "open up opportunities for cooperation on funding and weaponry."

But Rubio has now spoken the truth: that door was never meant for Ukraine to walk through. It was a shop window, a display designed to showcase "Western unity" and to motivate Ukrainians to keep fighting. Now, the lights in that window have been turned off.

🎭 Trump’s "24-Hour" Promise and Geopolitical Reality

Rubio’s statement does not stand in isolation. As early as August 2025, Trump had publicly stated that Zelenskyy could end the war "almost immediately" provided he gave up Crimea and abandoned the bid for NATO membership.  He wrote on Truth Social: "NO GOING INTO NATO BY UKRAINE. Some things never change!!!"

Trump has also spoken even more bluntly: "He [Zelenskyy] wants to be a NATO member, but he will never be a NATO member. He understands that."

"Some things never change" this phrase reveals Trump's true view on the Ukraine issue. To him, Ukraine joining NATO was never a serious proposition. It was a bargaining chip, a prop for campaign rallies to boast, "I prevented World War III."

💔 It is not just Ukraine that has been betrayed

Rubio's statement deals a heavy blow to the entire European security architecture.

European leaders are already preparing for a "US withdrawal." NATO allies have pledged €70 billion in military aid to Ukraine for 2026, with "the majority share borne by European allies and Canada." The Pentagon has transferred command of NATO's military aid coordination for Ukraine to European allies citing the fact that "SAG-U was always temporary" as a move to "shift the burden within the alliance."

Rubio's statement merely confirms Europe's deepest fear: the US is withdrawing, and Europe must face Russia alone.

🕯️ The true meaning of "not on the table"

Rubio used the present tense when saying it is "not on the table." But no one believes this is merely a temporary measure.

When asked about NATO membership, Rubio said "there is a consensus process that must take place." Translated, this means: as long as a single member state objects, Ukraine cannot get in. And the US is that objecting member state.

This isn't "not on the table." It is "never on the table" simply wrapped in diplomatic language.

Rubio also stated that the US is "obviously looking at the trend lines and seeing that the current direction is not heading toward [a solution]." This remark exposes Washington's true mindset: the US does not believe Ukraine can win.  And an ally that does not believe you can win will not open the doors of NATO to you.

#Conclusion: A single truth shatters a fantasy.

Rubio’s statement marks the final reckoning regarding the West’s four-year-long "NATO promise" to Ukraine.

From the 2008 Bucharest pledge that Ukraine "would become a member" to the 2026 stance in Iceland that it is "not on the table" eighteen years, and it was all a ruse.

What did Ukraine pay for this promise? Hundreds of thousands of lives. A devastated nation. The future of an entire generation.

And what did NATO gain? A weakened, depleted, and exhausted Russia along with an "ally" that could be discarded at any moment.

Rubio is right. NATO membership is not on the table. It never was.

text:
Nuclear just had its biggest week in a while. Here's who came out ahead.

Nuclear stocks jumped after a run of deals landed within days of each other. I went through each announcement to see what is actually signed and who benefits.

My take: Constellation (CEG) has the stronger position. Vistra (VST) may have more room to run.

Start with Google and Constellation. A 20-year PPA funds upgrades at 11 Constellation reactors across Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, adding 890 MW.

Constellation says that comes with more than $4.3B of investment. The first uprate is expected by 2028.

Google also signed a separate 15-year deal for 2,700 MW of existing output. It adds no capacity, but it locks in revenue.

A week earlier, Amazon signed a 20-year deal at Calvert Cliffs in Maryland. It covers 690 MW, including a 190 MW uprate, and supports about $3B of investment.

The license matters more than the megawatts. Calvert Cliffs would otherwise shut down in 2034 and 2036, and Amazon's commitment gives Constellation the revenue certainty to relicense for another 20 years.

Vistra's news came from Washington. The DOE offered a conditional loan of up to $4.2B for uprates at Beaver Valley, Davis-Besse and Perry.

The key word is conditional. Vistra still has to meet technical, legal, environmental and financial conditions before any money moves.

The loan adds 433 MW and preserves nearly 4 GW. Meta already contracted that capacity in January, so this is about cheaper funding, not new demand.

Vistra had planned to pay for the uprates from its own cash flow. A federal loan could change that math.

Then there's Westinghouse. A US and South Korea framework outlines $120B to build six AP1000s and two Korean APR1400s on federal sites.

No sites, utilities or commercial terms have been named. I'd treat it as a headline until projects are announced.

Oracle also joined the group. It plans to subscribe to part of Point Beach's output in Wisconsin and says it will absorb about $300M in rising energy costs, pending approval from the state's Public Service Commission.

So who has it better?

Constellation has the scale. It runs roughly 22 GW of nuclear, the largest fleet in the country, and has now signed Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Google.

The risk is execution. The revenue is contracted, so any slip on the uprates is what hurts the stock.

Vistra has a much smaller fleet at about 6.4 GW. Going into this week, roughly 3.8 GW of it was already contracted to Amazon and Meta, versus about 1.95 GW for Constellation's Microsoft and Meta deals.

The weaker side is the balance sheet. Vistra carries roughly $19B of debt, and nuclear is only about 15% of its total capacity.

Talen is worth a mention. It rose about 7% on Tuesday without signing anything new, and it still depends on a single plant, Susquehanna.

CEG rose about 12% on the day and VST about 8%, so some of this is already priced in.

The pattern is the point. Most of these deals fund upgrades at existing plants instead of building new reactors, which skips the licensing and interconnection delays that slow new builds.

Watch two things. One is whether Vistra clears the conditions on the DOE loan. The other is whether the Korea framework turns into named sites and signed contracts.

text:
🏅 FRANCIS HALZEN
2026 Nobel Prize in Physics 🧑‍🔬

Ghost Particles ☄️, Antarctic Ice 
& the Questions Children Ask 🗣️ 

October 6, 2026 💫
University of Wisconsin–Madison
IceCube Neutrino Observatory, Antarctica

▸ ▸ ▸

To see farther into the universe, Francis Halzen helped build an observatory deep beneath the ice.

Today, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the Belgian-born physicist the Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to IceCube and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

An extraordinary idea. An enormous collective undertaking. A new way to investigate the universe.

And a story that begins with something passing through you right now.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
👻 THE INVISIBLE MESSENGERS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Neutrinos have extraordinarily small masses and no electric charge. They interact so rarely with ordinary matter that vast numbers pass through our bodies unnoticed.

That elusiveness makes them difficult to detect—and valuable as cosmic messengers.

Magnetic fields bend the paths of charged cosmic rays. Neutrinos travel without that magnetic deflection, preserving clues to where they originated.

Reconstruct their arrival directions, collect enough evidence, and scientists can begin identifying the distant environments that produced them.

◆ WHY THIS MATTERS

Some of the universe’s most energetic processes occur in environments difficult to investigate with light alone. Neutrinos carry additional information from those places.

The challenge is giving something that barely interacts with matter enough matter to interact with.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🧊 A TELESCOPE MADE OF ICE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Halzen helped turn the deep Antarctic ice into an instrument.

◆ THE ORIGINAL DEEP-ICE ARRAY

• 5,160 optical sensors.
• Approximately one cubic kilometer of instrumented ice.
• Sensors positioned roughly 1,450–2,450 meters below the surface.

When a neutrino interacts nearby, it can produce charged particles that emit a faint glow called Cherenkov radiation.

These particles can travel faster than light travels through ice. Nothing here exceeds light’s speed in a vacuum.

The sensors record the glow. Its timing and pattern help researchers estimate the neutrino’s energy and direction.

A fleeting interaction becomes a measurable clue.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🌌 ANOTHER VIEW OF OUR GALAXY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

In 2023, the IceCube Collaboration reported evidence of high-energy neutrino emission from the Milky Way, producing a new view of our galaxy through these elusive particles.

Consider what that means.

The familiar band of stars across our night sky can also be studied through particles that usually pass through Earth without leaving a trace.

We are learning to read another kind of message from the universe.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE QUESTION A CHILD MIGHT ASK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Imagine a child standing outside tonight, looking up at the stars.

“If something is invisible, how do we know it’s there?”

IceCube offers a remarkable answer: sometimes, we discover something through the trace it leaves behind.

Scientists cannot watch a neutrino cross the universe. They can measure the aftermath of an interaction, check competing explanations, and work out what the evidence supports.

Richard Feynman, Nobel laureate in Physics, expressed the discipline behind that work:

“The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool.”

Curiosity begins the investigation. Honesty keeps it useful.

For a child, that lesson travels well beyond science class:

• Ask a question.
• Look carefully.
• Test your explanation.
• Listen to other people.
• Change your mind when the evidence calls for it.

These are habits worth carrying into adulthood.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WHAT DOES THIS DO FOR EVERYDAY LIFE?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IceCube’s immediate purpose is to understand how the universe works. Its discoveries do not come with a promise to lower next month’s grocery bill.

Building such an observatory does, however, require sensitive instruments, sophisticated data analysis, and people trained to solve unfamiliar problems.

Those abilities matter wherever we need to distinguish a meaningful signal from noise.

We cannot predict every practical application that might follow. We can recognize the value of developing tools, knowledge, and people capable of answering questions we could not answer before.

There is also an everyday lesson here.

When we encounter a dramatic headline, an appealing claim, or an explanation we want to believe, we can ask:

What was actually measured?
What else could explain it?
What would change my mind?

The same care that makes a scientific discovery trustworthy can help us make better judgments.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🏅 ONE LAUREATE. A COLLECTIVE ACHIEVEMENT.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Halzen’s vision required the work of an international collaboration.

Scientists investigated the particles. Engineers developed instruments. Technicians and polar support teams helped make the observatory possible in Antarctica.

The Nobel recognizes his decisive leadership. IceCube’s discoveries reflect that collective effort.

A child reading this story might want to become a physicist.

Another might want to build the equipment.

Both have a place in the discovery.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STILL THINKING ABOUT THE NEXT EXPERIMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

At 82, receiving a Nobel Prize carrying an award of 12 million Swedish kronor, Halzen was already thinking about the work ahead.

Speaking by phone from Italy after the announcement, he joked that he hoped the recognition would help get a research proposal approved.

The world was celebrating what he had accomplished.

He was thinking about what remained to be discovered.

Albert Einstein, another Nobel laureate in Physics, put that impulse simply:

“The important thing is not to stop questioning.”

▸ ▸ ▸

My perspective: The most compelling part of this achievement is the patience built into it.

A particle almost never interacts. A detector must be immense. A faint signal must survive careful scrutiny. An ambitious idea needs people willing to work through years of difficulty.

Halzen helped turn those challenges into a working observatory.

Deep beneath Antarctica, a faint flash can carry evidence of something that happened far across the universe.

And we have learned how to notice.

Somewhere tonight, a child will look at the sky and ask a question nobody around them can answer.

That is a beginning. 🌌

text:
My Rookie of the Year 🏆

Yaxel Lendeborg

Stever Kerr Quotes 

• Kerr: “He is capable of being the lead offensive threat when Steph is not on the floor”

• Kerr: “We need him to be more aggressive scoring mentality and thats something we are going to work with him on”

• Kerr: “He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.”

• Kerr: “He’s going to play a ton.” That’s the foundation of this bet: the coach sees both a roster need and a meaningful role.

1️⃣ NBA TRANSLATION + SUMMER LEAGUE

• Michigan: 15.1 PTS / 6.8 REB / 3.2 AST / 1.2 BLK / 1.1 STL. He contributes across the stat sheet and doesn’t need the offense built around him.

• I like his fit as a bigger three who can rotate to the four. His frame, rebounding and passing give Golden State different lineup options.Defenders chasing Steph create opportunities to slip screens, cut behind the defense and attack closeouts. Lendeborg has the passing ability to capitalize when the defense rotates.

• Summer League MVP + championship: 14.8 PTS / 6.8 REB / 4.0 AST / 1.5 STL in six Vegas games. Small sample, but the all-around production carried over. The 4.0 assists stand out most to me. Making quick decisions alongside Curry is a skill that can earn him minutes even when his shot isn’t falling.

2️⃣ OPPORTUNITY + ROTATIONAL COMPETITION

• Butler and Moody have reported return targets around January–February, with neither date confirmed. Lendeborg has an early window to establish himself—and gets a starting look in the preseason opener.

• Gui Santos: His most direct competition for forward minutes in my opinion. Yaxel needs to show his rebounding, passing and scoring make him the better fit.

• Gary Payton II: Could take minutes when Kerr prioritizes perimeter defense and smaller lineups. Lendeborg has to defend well enough to stay on the floor.

• Georges Niang — sleeper: Veteran shooting could earn Kerr’s trust. If Yaxel’s jumper struggles, Niang’s spacing becomes appealing. Yaxel’s counter is contributing in more areas.

• Steph will probably miss some games. That could create extra shots and responsibility for Lendeborg, but tougher looks without Curry drawing defenders. I’m betting he can handle some of that additional workload.

• Podz is a major question mark. How much does his scoring and creation improve? A big leap could absorb available touches. Inconsistency could leave more room for Lendeborg as a secondary scorer and playmaker.

• Kerr’s handling of young players has been a talking point. I think Yaxel’s experience and decision-making give him a strong chance to earn trust early.

3️⃣ UNFAZED CONFIDENCE / AGE

• At 24, he brings experience from junior college, UAB and Michigan. For an award based on first-year production, I like that preparation.

• “I feel like I could be Rookie of the Year, but that’s not my main focus.”

4️⃣ ANALYSIS OF THE COMPETITION

• Cameron Boozer (+300)
 Memphis offers substantial usage. I see a path toward something approaching 20/10/5 as an upside scenario, not a baseline. His potential scoring and rebounding volume makes him a major threat.

• AJ Dybantsa (+400)
 The No. 1 pick has the offensive talent to win. Trae Young, Anthony Davis and Washington’s young players create competition for touches. Those veterans could also generate easier looks—the question is how quickly AJ earns a featured scoring role.

Darius Acuff (+1500)

If I wasn’t betting on Yaxel, Acuff would probably be my pick. I think he’s the 2nd-best value on the ROY board. Sacramento gives him opportunity + capable pieces around him, and he should have the ball in his hands from Day 1 as both a scorer and playmaker. 17 PTS / 8 AST or even 20 PTS / 6 AST feels realistic. Wouldn’t surprise me if ROY comes down to a 3-man buzzer-beater between Yaxel, Acuff & Peterson.

My early projection for Yaxel could easily see him averaging 16/7/3 with 1.5 steals and almost 1 block a game.

text:
WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: President Trump Delivers Immediate Diesel Relief, Saving Americans Up to $100 Per Fill

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Last night, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order that immediately cuts diesel costs by authorizing highway use of tax-free dyed diesel and deferring the federal diesel excise tax through the end of the year. The decisive action expected to save drivers as much as $100 per fill puts real money back in the pockets of farmers, ranchers, truckers, loggers, and working families at the exact moment harvest demands it most.

Here’s what they’re saying:

President Donald J. Trump : “I am announcing another unprecedented step to bring down costs. For many years, farm vehicles, construction equipment, and other off-road vehicles have used what is known as ‘red dye’ diesel… which is exactly the same as normal diesel, but is sold tax-free for off-road vehicles and big trucks… Tonight, I am going to sign a historic Executive Order to officially waive the off-road requirement and allow anyone to purchase tax-free red dye diesel for any reason.”

Vice President JD Vance : “Another example of President Trump acting quickly to tackle an urgent issue. In this administration, we’re fighting every day to help hard working Americans, especially our farmers.”

White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles : “President Trump signed an Executive Order right here in Nebraska to lower diesel costs for American farmers, truckers, and workers. By expanding access to red-dyed diesel and providing federal tax relief, President Trump is once again taking decisive action to put money back in the pockets of hardworking Americans. Promises made. Promises kept.”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins : “President Trump is the most pro ranching and farming president in our lifetime. Energy dominance is at the core of putting farmers and ranchers first. This administration has unleashed American energy dominance, and we are now the largest energy producer in the world as a result. While the Administration has structurally changed the energy sector to secure the long-term future of agriculture, we are now taking steps to deal with short term pressures impacting our American farmers. Thank you, President Trump for signing today’s Executive Order enacting enforcement discretion on on-road use of dyed diesel, which will better enable our farmers to deliver America’s harvest during this critical time. And I want to thank Vice President Vance for his help shepherding it to the end.”

American Farm Bureau Federation President Zippy Duvall : “We thank President Trump for recognizing that what happens at the fuel pump directly affects what happens on the farm and therefore at dinner tables across America. Allowing dyed diesel fuel to be used over-the-road will bring welcome relief for farmers because every cent per gallon matters when you’re running a fleet of grain trucks or hauling cattle hundreds of miles. As we detailed in a letter to the president last week, this effort will bring much needed price relief for farmers as they work to complete harvest across the U.S. The federal highway diesel tax is currently more than 24-cents per gallon, so it’s a big deal to farmers to be able to use tax exempt diesel more broadly to get their harvest to market. We appreciate that the president listened to farmers and responded.”

American Soybean Association Vice President Dave Walton : “As U.S. soybean farmers move the 2026 harvest to market, ASA thanks President Trump for his Executive Order that seeks to address high fuel costs impacting our bottom lines. This policy will align with actions taken by many soybean-producing states already, and ASA is encouraged by the administration’s continued focus on agricultural affordability.”

Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe : “Last week, I signed an executive order taking targeted action to help address the unique fuel and transportation needs of harvest season in Missouri. President Trump’s action yesterday provides commonsense flexibility to lower transportation costs and keep agriculture moving across the entire nation. When we can reduce unnecessary costs for our farmers, that ultimately benefits families across our state and nation.”

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry : “Thank you, President I declared a State of Emergency so our farmers could use the dyed diesel fuel they already had on hand—and now, thanks to YOU, that relief is going nationwide! This is a HUGE WIN for America’s farmers, truckers, and hardworking families. Lower costs and real relief for the people who keep this country moving.”

Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee : “On Friday, I directed TN state departments to suspend enforcement of dyed diesel restrictions through the end of October to provide relief for farmers & foresters during harvest season. Thank you, for standing with the Tennesseans who feed & fuel our country.”

Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen : “This action expands on state efforts I enacted by executive order just a few weeks ago. This will greatly assist farmers who are dealing with extraordinarily high diesel prices, impacting everything they do – from field operations to transportation of their products and livestock. I appreciate that President Trump signed his order today in Nebraska. Agriculture is the tip of the spear in our great state, and we need to continue to do all that we can to feed the world and save the planet. President Trump knows that and we appreciate his support.”

Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves : “President Trump has announced he is signing an executive order that will defer the federal excise tax on dyed diesel and allow for highway use. Because of the EO signed by I have spoken with Commissioner and he plans to direct the Commercial Transportation Enforcement Division of the Mississippi Department of Public Safety to not enforce the dyed diesel prohibition on highways. Thanks to this executive order and Commissioner Tindell’s swift action, much-needed relief will be delivered to our nation’s farmers, truckers, ranchers and loggers, as well as a wide range of other industries that rely on diesel. This will have positive ripple effects on America’s economy and your wallet. I’d like to thank President Trump and his administration for working quickly to provide this relief.”

Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds : “Today, in line with President Trump’s executive order, I suspended state penalties for using dyed diesel to transport certain ag products on public roads. This will lower costs for farmers through the harvest and beyond by opening access to tax-free fuel.”

South Dakota Gov. Larry Rhoden : “In response to these extraordinary times, President Trump has ordered a suspension of enforcement of the federal dyed diesel fuel for taxpayers on highways and public roads. Therefore, I am directing the Department of Public Safety to adjust enforcement priorities regarding the use of dyed diesel fuel. Many farmers maintain on-site supplies of dyed diesel fuel for nontaxable, off-road use. By taking this action, we will provide meaningful relief to South Dakota farmers. Similarly, President Trump’s order will allow all taxpayers to realize meaningful savings from using dyed diesel.”

North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein : “Last week I took action to help provide some relief at the pump for North Carolina’s farmers, and I asked the IRS to step in to pause enforcement of the red-dyed diesel tax at the federal level. I am pleased to see farmers across the country will now get this same relief. Let’s keep working at every level of government to help people keep more money in their wallets.”

Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture Andy Holt : “Governor Lee’s directive, coupled with President Trump’s federal executive order, provides timely relief for Tennessee farmers, forest product producers and timber harvesters facing high diesel costs during harvest season. Agriculture and forestry are essential to Tennessee’s economy, and this temporary flexibility will help keep producers working, products moving, and rural communities supported. We appreciate Governor Lee’s leadership, President Trump’s action, and Secretary Rollins’ support for American agriculture.”

Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture Jonathan Shell : “Huge win for Kentucky farmers. President Trump signed an executive order expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel. With harvest underway and high fuel costs weighing on farm families, this will provide immediate relief and help lower costs. Thank you President Trump for standing with our farmers.”

Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce Andy Gipson : “A HUGE thank you to President Trump and Governor Reeves for taking action to allow red-dyed off-road diesel fuel. A huge help to our farmers, loggers and truckers here in Mississippi and across America.”

Alabama Farmers Federation President Jimmy Parnell : “We appreciate President Trump joining Gov. Kay Ivey in allowing dyed diesel fuel to be used without penalty for highway use. With about a dozen states easing enforcement of off-road diesel rules, President Trump’s executive order provides consistency across the country and ensures farmers and timber producers will not be penalized when they cross state lines to market their products.”

Louisiana Farm Bureau President Richard Fontenot : “Anything helps, especially as we work to get the crops out of the fields. I’m appreciative of the governor’s (and president’s) efforts to give us any relief during this time.”

Tennessee Farm Bureau Federation : “We join American Farm Bureau President in applauding the executive order signed by President Trump to suspend enforcement of dyed diesel fuel restrictions for agricultural operators, giving farmers a break.”

Sen. Tom Cotton : “Allowing on-road use of red diesel will give Arkansas farmers much-needed relief. This is a welcome step by the administration that I’ve long called for.”

Sen. Chuck Grassley : “Thx to Pres Trump for listening to farmers & temporarily allowing off-road dyed diesel for highway use Lowering costs for FARMERS DURING HARVEST”

Sen. Bill Hagerty : “is taking action to lower diesel prices, cutting costs for Tennessee farmers who keep food moving from the farm to families’ dinner tables.”

Sen. Roger Marshall : “Temporary expanded use of dyed diesel allows producers to utilize more fuel options during harvest and lightens the cost of production for farmers and ranchers at a crucial time. Thanks to the White House for listening to farmers. We still have more work to do.”

Sen. Mike Rounds : “Following my letter last week, I’m pleased to see that the President is taking steps to lower fuel prices, including a review of certain taxes on diesel. This is an opportunity to offer real relief to South Dakotans who continue to pay higher prices at the pump, particularly farmers and ranchers who are in the middle of harvest. We’ll continue to work on addressing the high cost of living impacting our state.”

Rep. Mark Alford : “just signed an order letting truckers and farmers run tax-free dyed diesel on the highway through year’s end no interest, no penalties. That puts real money back in the pockets of the folks who haul our freight and grow our food.”

Rep. Tim Burchett : “A few weeks ago, I called on to take action on diesel prices. Last night, President Trump signed an Executive Order to put money back in the pockets of American farmers, truckers, and workers.”

Rep. Don Davis : “It’s a much needed Executive Order that provides temporary relief for farmers and working families facing record fuel costs.”

Rep. Russell Fry : “No one cares more about affordability than President Trump and Congressional Republicans.”

Rep. Ashley Hinson : “High diesel prices are hurting our truckers, farmers, and all Iowans, and this executive order is a step in the right direction to deliver relief. We should be using every tool available to lower fuel prices and provide flexibility for Iowa farmers during harvest season. I’ll continue to push for bipartisan policies that lower costs at the pump and the checkout line.”

Rep. Rich McCormick : “A farmer can’t wait for prices to come down. The crop is in the field right now. This week signed an order that temporarily allows tax-free dyed diesel to be used on the highway. The federal diesel tax is deferred through the end of the year, with no interest and no penalties. That’s about $60 on a 250-gallon fill, and more where states follow suit. It’s temporary, and it’s not the whole answer. But for the families who feed America, it is real relief at a critical time. The long-term fix is more supply and more refining capacity. That is the work still ahead.”

Rep. Zach Nunn : “This is a good first step and it will deliver real relief for farmers facing record diesel prices in the middle of harvest.”

Rep. Jason Smith : “I applaud President Trump’s executive order today to provide immediate relief by deferring the excise tax for on-road use of dyed diesel until the end of the year. This is a much-needed step to lessen the burden that increased fuel prices have had on farmers, ranchers, and the entire agricultural community. This executive order is only a first step it is crucial to provide lasting relief for the hardworking Americans who feed, fuel, and clothe our nation.”

Rep. Greg Steube : “President Trump is delivering relief for America’s farmers and truckers. My RED Fuel Act is sitting in Congress waiting to make this relief permanent. House Leadership needs to bring us back to D.C. and pass it!”

Click here to read the Executive Order.

Click here to read the White House fact sheet.

Distributed on October 6th, 2026.

Mistral’s model preview, AI oversight, care-home pilots, workplace findings and research across the world.

TRANSCRIPT
Organizations seeking adaptable AI for text and visual tasks have another model to test. Mistral Large 4 uses a mixture of experts with 1.05 trillion total parameters and 49 billion active parameters. API access is in preview, with downloadable weights planned for October 27 after testing. Mistral describes prospective uses including storm-damage assessment and crop monitoring; these are proposed applications.

AI adoption across East Asia and the Pacific still trails advanced economies, despite the region supplying goods behind the investment surge. The World Bank identifies cost, expertise, security and privacy barriers, and recommends affordable tools adapted to local languages alongside infrastructure and skills investment. Its report says AI is reshaping skills demand but has not yet significantly affected automatable jobs.

When AI agents cause data breaches, OpenAI and Anthropic currently decide whether to notify authorities. Both told Australian parliament they would welcome mandatory reporting laws. OpenAI said a legal requirement could set a common disclosure standard. This is testimony during deliberations, rather than an enacted reporting requirement or evidence that reporting prevents breaches.

Care workers need to notice changes in residents’ condition without treating every sensor variation as illness. Panasonic AI compares heart rate, breathing, movement and sleep data with personal baselines, while another AI organizes evidence for staff. An October care-site pilot will evaluate usefulness. Retrospective company testing reported 89.4 percent recall and a 10.5 percent false-alert rate; those results are not validated clinical outcomes.

Care-home residents need exercise plans matched to their functional abilities. Sharp’s AI Trainer analyzes responses, movement and posture to create plans, then an AI character guides exercises under physiotherapist supervision. A single-site pilot compares AI-supported planning, recordkeeping and evaluation with the previous workflow through November 1. Staff workload and participation are being assessed; no outcome is reported.

AI’s reported workplace benefits are unevenly distributed across employees. Gallup’s survey asks workers who used AI about their experiences; 63 percent report faster work and 56 percent more creative solutions. Among AI users, 68 percent with at least a bachelor’s degree report faster work, versus 51 percent with high-school education or less. These are self-reported associations, not causal estimates.

Businesses using AI for multi-step work need control over what agents can access and spend. Cohere says North 2 combines reusable skills, shared libraries and memory within a redesigned agent orchestration system. It offers private, cloud, hybrid and air-gapped deployments, with agent guardrails and controls for permissions, quotas and token spending. These are company feature and security claims.

Organizations adopting AI must connect useful workflows to sensitive business data while governing access. Cohere will supply its North platform, models and search capabilities, while PwC provides implementation, transformation and risk expertise. Their global alliance launches first in Canada and offers private-cloud, on-premises and air-gapped options. The announcement describes a commercial plan, not demonstrated benefits at scale.

Coordinating a group event means finding dates that participants can attend. LINE’s AI scheduling agent creates requests, proposes dates and titles, helps people respond, and follows up individually when the initial proposal does not work. It is available through LINE Labs. Participants can choose calendar-based AI responses, and finalized events can enter LINE Calendar; usage and reliability results are not provided.

Math teachers need to recognize and interpret students’ thinking to decide how to respond. Rowan’s Molly Fisher and University of Kentucky researchers plan to train AI on earlier-study data to recognize effective teacher noticing. The grant-supported research aims to help teachers assess their own noticing and support learning. The university reports research goals, rather than a deployed tool or measured student outcomes.

Camera-based AI applications need chips designed for device intelligence, including surveillance use. India’s Technology Development Board agreed to provide 130 crore rupees in optional convertible debt for BigEndian’s Project VeerAI, whose stated total cost is 260 crore rupees. The project aims to develop an AI vision chip and progress through validation, integration, testing and scale-up. It is development funding, not a market-ready chip or proven security benefit.

AI chips depend on advances in transistors, connections and packaging to handle demanding workloads. Applied Materials and Intel will collaborate across Applied’s Silicon Valley EPIC Center and Intel’s Oregon research campus on materials, processes and device architectures. The research includes three-dimensional stacking intended to improve connections, power delivery and thermal performance for agentic AI systems. These are engineering aims, not reported production gains.

AI use in schools and hospitals creates regulatory questions that cross national borders. Regulators meeting in Nairobi discussed shared legal guardrails and responsible AI use, while Kenya’s regulator called for collaborative, evidence-driven oversight. The forum runs through October 9 and includes regulators from six visiting African countries. These are nonbinding discussions, rather than an adopted continental AI rule.

Building AI for badminton requires understanding player movement, training and competition data. Zero Gravity allocates one million Singapore dollars to research with Nanyang Technological University and Y Badminton Academy, exploring a badminton foundation model using movement and video data. This sits within its five-year Singapore investment plan. Researchers describe the work as early stage, too soon to draw conclusions about applications or outcomes.

The World Bank argues that affordable AI could support jobs and productivity in Africa through practical services. Its chief economist points to tools on low-cost devices for student learning, livestock disease detection and management, and small-business accounting. The report recommends AI readiness; shared data centres and stronger data-protection laws are proposed adoption supports. These are policy recommendations, rather than funded deployments or measured results.

text:
American National Shield: Why the United States Needs a Stronger National Missile Defense Against Communist Red China
https://t.co/VYXYDnGnIX
By Guest Author Travis Karnes

The Chinese Communist Party operates as a strategic predator, not a responsible stakeholder in the international system. Its leadership in Beijing pursues global dominance through deception, intellectual property theft, economic coercion, and relentless militarization of every domain. At the forefront of this existential threat stands an expanding arsenal of ballistic and hypersonic missiles explicitly engineered to pierce American defenses, neutralize our carrier strike groups in the Indo-Pacific, and hold U.S. cities hostage under the shadow of nuclear blackmail. Our current patchwork of missile defenses—chronically underfunded, numerically insufficient, and technologically outmatched by peer adversaries—does not deter aggression; it invites it.

Deterrence is actively collapsing under the weight of obsolescent systems and bipartisan political denial. The Communist regime has chronicled its own methodical war preparations with forensic precision in doctrine and exercises. Senior military strategists have long understood that appeasement or half-measures against totalitarian regimes guarantees eventual conflict. Analysts have exposed the coordinated threats from the authoritarian axis. These nightmares now constitute operational doctrine. America urgently requires a comprehensive, layered American National Shield—integrated across domains, technologically superior, and backed by unyielding national will—before the window of opportunity closes forever.
Hypersonic Weapons: The Maneuvering Scourge Defying Legacy Defenses

The Communist regime’s hypersonic program represents a qualitative leap that fundamentally challenges traditional ballistic missile defense paradigms. The DF-17 medium-range ballistic missile (MRBM), declared operational around 2019, integrates a solid-fueled mobile booster with a hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV). After boost and separation, the glider achieves sustained Mach 5–10 velocities, employing waverider aerodynamics to generate lift from its own shockwaves. This enables unpredictable skipping and maneuvering trajectories through the upper atmosphere, defeating midcourse radar tracking and complicating terminal-phase intercepts. With a range of 1,800–2,500 km, the system places U.S. bases across the first and second island chains under immediate threat. In June 2026, state media released launch footage from Gobi Desert joint exercises, highlighting the Rocket Force’s emphasis on rapid combat readiness.

The longer-range DF-27 escalates the danger significantly. Assessed at 5,000–8,000 km, it carries an advanced HGV and features land-attack and anti-ship variants. Intelligence reporting, including a 2023 test flight covering 2,100 km in approximately 12 minutes, confirms its ability to penetrate U.S. ballistic missile defenses through high-speed terminal maneuvering. It is positioned as a potent “carrier killer” capable of striking beyond the Second Island Chain. Public imagery from 2026 shows heavy TEL movements, indicating deployment momentum. Supporting systems like the ship-launched YJ-21 further extend naval strike options.

These weapons exploit the physics of hypersonic flight: the plasma sheath formed at extreme velocities degrades radar signatures, while low-altitude glide profiles drastically compress defender decision timelines from minutes to mere seconds. Unlike predictable parabolic ballistic arcs, HGVs execute late-course corrections that defeat many exo-atmospheric interceptors.
Recent Ballistic Missile Testing: Provocative Demonstrations of First-Strike Reach

Beijing’s testing tempo reveals both technical maturation and coercive signaling. On July 6, 2026, the Navy executed a rare submarine-launched ballistic missile (SLBM) test from coastal waters off southern Guangdong province. The nuclear-capable JL-2 missile flew southeast over the northern tip of the Philippines, passed south of the U.S. territory of Guam, continued north of Palau and near Nauru, before impacting in the South Pacific. The approximately 4,000-mile flight path underscored the regime’s ability to threaten key American assets from submerged, hard-to-detect platforms.

The JL-2, deployed on Jin-class nuclear submarines, has a maximum range of up to 7,456 miles and can carry a single megaton warhead or up to eight MIRVs with yields from 20 to 150 kilotons. This test, the second major Pacific launch in two years after a long hiatus, highlights the rapid nuclear breakout—including land-based MIRV missiles in silos and the emerging H-20 bomber—forming a complete nuclear triad capable of first-strike operations against America. The State Department condemned the opaque buildup and refusal to engage in arms control.

This followed the landmark September 2024 ICBM test launched from Hainan Island—the first full-range Pacific ICBM shot in 44 years. The missile (likely DF-41 or advanced DF-31 series) traveled 11,500–12,000+ km into the South Pacific. Road-mobile operations were validated, alongside multiple rapid silo launches in late 2024 that signaled salvo-fire proficiency. The DF-41, MIRV-capable with ranges exceeding 12,000–15,000 km, directly threatens the continental United States.

These activities rehearse “system destruction” warfare—coordinated strikes on C4ISR networks, airbases, ports, and logistics nodes using mixed conventional and dual-capable systems.
War Games and Strike Simulations: Blueprints for Coercion and Mainland Pressure

Communist China’s military simulations and live-fire exercises routinely model massive opening missile campaigns against Taiwan and intervening U.S. forces. Rocket Force drills integrate intermediate-range ballistic missiles, anti-ship ballistic missiles, and hypersonic assets to suppress air and naval power projection. Broader wargames explore coercion short of invasion or calibrated escalation designed to isolate Taiwan while raising costs for Washington.

These simulations consistently feature hundreds of inbound threats in the initial hours, targeting forward bases in the Pacific and attempting to create fait accompli conditions through precision strikes on command nodes, airfields, and logistics hubs. Some scenarios incorporate direct or demonstrative strikes on U.S. homeland assets or territories to deter full intervention, including concepts for limited nuclear or conventional escalation. Past internal simulations have reportedly explored surgical strikes on the American Midwest—targeting key industrial, agricultural, and transportation infrastructure such as missile silos, rail hubs, and manufacturing centers in states like Missouri, Kansas, and Nebraska—to disrupt wartime mobilization and supply chains without necessarily triggering all-out nuclear exchange. These exercises test the psychological and logistical impact of deep strikes, aiming to fracture national will and complicate reinforcement of the Pacific theater.

Allied analyses confirm that Communist planners prioritize “system destruction” to blind and paralyze American command structures early in any conflict.
Boost-Phase Interception Technologies: Killing Missiles in Their Most Vulnerable Window

Effective defense against this arsenal demands engagement during the boost phase—while missiles are still accelerating on predictable trajectories with bright, high-infrared exhaust plumes. Boost-phase intercept (BPI) systems offer decisive advantages by destroying threats before warhead or HGV separation and before complex countermeasures deploy.

Key technologies include airborne lasers mounted on high-altitude aircraft or drones, delivering megawatt-class directed energy to burn through booster casings at long standoff ranges; kinetic interceptors launched from forward-deployed aircraft, ships, or rapidly ascending platforms using hit-to-kill technology; and space-based interceptors or sensors for persistent global coverage, enabling near-instantaneous detection and cueing.

These systems counter both traditional ballistic missiles and hypersonic boost-glide profiles by shortening the attacker’s timeline advantage. Deployment in the Western Pacific, combined with tanker support and unmanned loyal wingmen, could neutralize many threats near launch sites in mainland China or at sea.
Hypersonic Defense Countermeasures: Multi-Layered Detection and Defeat

Defending against maneuvering HGVs requires a paradigm shift beyond midcourse ballistic systems. Critical elements include advanced space-based infrared and radar sensors for continuous tracking through all flight phases, overcoming line-of-sight limitations of ground radars; hypersonic glide-phase interceptors using advanced seekers, maneuverable kill vehicles, and potentially directed-energy augmentation for terminal engagement; electronic warfare and cyber countermeasures to disrupt command links or spoof guidance systems; over-the-horizon and multi-static radars networked with AI-driven battle management for predictive tracking of erratic paths; and high-energy lasers and microwave weapons for ground- or sea-based terminal defense against lower-altitude gliders.

Integration of these into a national architecture—layered with expanded Ground-Based Midcourse Defense interceptors, Aegis Ashore sites, and THAAD batteries—creates depth and redundancy. Artificial intelligence will prove essential for managing complex, high-volume raids involving saturation tactics.
The Call to Action: American National Will and Common Defense

Time is dwindling but not yet lost. We must reject strategic vulnerability and the siren song of globalist liberal arms control nostalgia with a regime that honors no agreements. Congress and the Executive must prioritize funding, accelerate testing and deployment, and mobilize American industry for the scale of production required. A true National Shield protects not just hardware but the sovereign constitutional republic and the liberty of the American people.

“The circumstances which endanger the safety of nations are infinite, and for this reason no constitutional shackles can wisely be imposed on the power to which the care of it is committed.” — Alexander Hamilton, Federalist No. 28

Ronald Reagan reminded us that “peace through strength” is not a slogan but the foundation of survival: “Of the four wars in my lifetime, none came about because the United States was too strong.”

In this spirit, the United States must embrace an American Nationalist vision of common defense. This is not imperialism but prudent self-preservation—the sacred duty of a free people to secure their posterity against the totalitarian darkness rising in the East. We will build this Shield with American ingenuity, American resolve, and American steel. We will deter war through unmistakable superiority. And we will ensure that the United States of America remains the greatest force for liberty the world has ever known. The Republic demands it. History requires it. The American people will deliver it.

Failure is not an option. Victory through strength is the only acceptable outcome.

text:
At three in the morning, Chris Bledsoe says a voice woke him with a single word:

“Arise.”

What followed would eventually connect a North Carolina father to an ancient monument in Egypt—and a prediction some have tied to tomorrow.

October 7, 2026.

But the story begins years before anyone circled that date.

In 2007, Bledsoe reported encountering glowing objects while fishing near North Carolina’s Cape Fear River. Going public brought attention, but he says it also brought ridicule that reached his children.

By Easter 2012, he had reached his limit.

That evening, he went outside and angrily addressed whatever had entered his life. His family was suffering. He wanted to stop talking about it.

Hours later, he says, the voice woke him.

Bledsoe describes being led outside, where a blast of wind knocked him backward. He saw a translucent bull with stars visible inside it. Then a luminous woman appeared, floating above the ground.

He would come to call her “the Lady.”

According to Bledsoe, she urged him to keep sharing his experiences. What had become a burden, she told him, had a purpose.

But it was another message he attributes to her that would turn his personal story into a prophecy.

The message concerned a star.

Regulus.

Bledsoe says the Lady described it appearing red, low on the horizon before dawn, in the direction of the Great Sphinx’s gaze. That moment, she told him, would mark a change in humanity’s knowledge.

Think about that image: the Egyptian desert before sunrise. The Sphinx facing the horizon. A star appearing through the darkness.

And somewhere within that scene, a promise that humanity would begin to understand something it hadn’t understood before.

What knowledge?

Bledsoe has offered interpretations. A spiritual awakening. A deeper understanding of consciousness. Recognition that we are not alone.

But he has also acknowledged that he doesn’t know exactly what the message means.

Then came the problem of turning that celestial riddle into a date.

Bledsoe has discussed September 2026 and Easter 2026, explaining that he depended on others to interpret the alignment.

During his February 2026 conversation with AJ Gentile, another date entered the discussion: October 7, 2026.

Tomorrow.

That distinction matters. October 7 is an interpretation discussed in an interview, not a calendar date we can independently verify was delivered by a mysterious visitor.

And neither an interview nor an apparent alignment proves a prophecy.

The shifting dates deserve scrutiny. So does a prediction broad enough to include changes that might only become apparent years later. What would count as fulfillment? What would count as failure?

Bledsoe himself has said he doesn’t expect everyone to suddenly awaken in a single instant. He describes the possibility of a beginning—something understood gradually.

For believers, that makes the message more profound.

For skeptics, it makes it harder to test.

Either way, the story has brought us to an unusual moment: a man’s account of a visitor in the night, a star above Egypt, and a date now one sunrise away.

Tomorrow may pass like any other day.

If it does, will people reconsider the prophecy—or simply reconsider what it was supposed to mean?

text:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on why "some bad things are going to happen" with AI, and why he thinks society should accept them:

Asked how much daylight there is between OpenAI and others in the AI debate, Altman is blunt: "I think there's a lot of daylight."

It starts with a belief OpenAI has always held:

"We have always been a big believer that this technology has to be democratized and put in people's hands."

That belief, he says, is what separates OpenAI from the strictest voices in AI safety:

"I think one of the biggest differences between us and some of the stricter, let's say AI safety people is we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency."

He describes the alternative, which he understands but rejects:

"I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like this technology is going to get so powerful and it's so dangerous that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits."

His verdict:

"I think that is a completely unacceptable trade off from a perspective of liberty and human agency and people self determining the future."

@sama doesn't pretend his approach is free. The lighter-touch regulation OpenAI argues for comes with a cost, and he says so directly:

"I do think the lighter touch regulatory stance that we advocate for comes with an accepting of the fact that some bad things are going to happen as society figures out the resilience."

Even offered a guarantee of a clean rollout, he says he would turn it down:

"I wouldn't take a trade of saying we'll make sure there's no major hacks, there's no misuse of this technology, there's zero scams, there's zero all the other bad things that will happen because I think people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff than bad stuff."

But his tolerance for harm has a hard ceiling. Some risks are not survivable, and there he turns his warning on the accelerationists:

"When it comes to the potential of a serious loss of control to AI and this is not a today worry, but it may not be in the distant future, this is where I would say to the accelerationists, let's be a little thoughtful about lurching into this future."

His full position fits in one sentence:

"Accept bounded risks, accept risks that we understand in exchange for the benefits and liberty agency, all those things I was just talking about, but don't accept the really catastrophic risk."

text:
Arch Manning recently stepped away from the high-pressure spotlight for a moment, featuring in a Humann commercial alongside his mother, Ellen. In the lighthearted spot, Dr. Christopher Davis explains the science behind Humann’s SuperBeets Heart Chews while Ellen reminds her son that he has a game to reach. 

“Arch, kickoffs in ten minutes,” Ellen says, as Manning walks over, greets Davis, and asks if they can swap T-shirts before returning to his mother and noting, “Mom, it’s Dr. Davis.” The scene captures a lighter side of a quarterback who is already well-known and closely watched in college football, given his family legacy and his status as Texas’ starting quarterback.

Humann released behind-the-scenes clips from the shoot, showing Manning at Texas’ stadium with his mother in uniform, sharing a laugh in the tunnel, and Manning toasting the camera with Humann’s product. One photo playfully shows Manning balancing a Humann item on his head as if it were a football.

For a quarterback who has spent much of the season under scrutiny, the commercial offered a brief, breezy moment away from the pressure. The on-field expectations, however, remain a central focus for Manning and the Texas program.

Big plays have drawn attention, but questions about the Texas offense persist. Manning entered the season with high expectations for both himself and the team. Texas sits at 4-0 and holds the No. 1 ranking, yet Manning’s individual numbers have not fully matched the preseason hype. Through four games, he has three interceptions and a 63.5% completion rate. Those figures have helped Texas stay undefeated but have also sparked discussion about his development as a passer.

A standout performance against Ohio State illustrated both potential and areas for growth. Manning helped fuel a dramatic comeback, using his running ability to generate momentum and absorbing a big hit along the sideline. He also grew more willing to push the ball downfield, completing 11 of 15 passes in the fourth quarter and directing three long touchdown drives. The comeback underscored his talent and athleticism, showing why there is excitement about his ceiling. 

Yet the game also highlighted vulnerabilities. Tennessee pressured Manning, who threw an interception and was sacked multiple times as Texas managed only 262 total yards. The Longhorns converted just three of 12 third-down attempts, and Manning finished with negative rushing yardage after subtracting sack yardage. Texas still won, thanks to a strong defensive effort and efficient ground play from Raleek Brown, which helped mitigate the offense’s shortcomings.

This dynamic fuels ongoing analysis of Manning as an NFL prospect. Analysts have noted that while his arm talent and athletic ability are evident, his decision-making and field vision continue to develop. Critics have pointed to moments when he passed up open options or remained in the pocket, seeking a bigger throw, rather than taking the available safe play. The broader context of Texas’ offense—its line play, drive sustainability, and defensive support—also factors into assessments of his progress.

Beyond the field, Manning has faced scrutiny off it as well. He issued an apology after reacting to an counterfeit AI video that depicted Texas coach Steve Sarkisian in a negative scenario involving a well-known sports reporter; the portrayal was fake, and the reporter accepted the apology. This incident, like others, demonstrates how every public moment can become part of the larger discussion surrounding him as he navigates a high-profile college career.

Tech Weekend returns on November 19–20 in Menlo Park, Silicon Valley. It is a 48-hour fundraising sprint for pre-seed to Series A founders.

Across two days, founders connect with investors through:

▫️ VC Office Hours: 20–30-minute (pre-scheduled) one-on-one meetings with investors who are investing in their space, at their stage.

▫️ Pitch Competition: Present to a panel of active VCs. Get real-time feedback and offers to chat more offline.

▫️ VC Panels & Fireside Chats: Gain insights from investors who've invested in startups. Hear what they're looking for and how to stand out.

▫️ Networking Mixer: All-day networking mixers with founders, investors and engineers gathered from across the United States and internationally.

Call for Startups:
Looking at the investors joining us in November, here's where their attention seems to be for this cohort.

▪️ Physical AI and robotics — spatial AI, embodied AI, autonomous mobility, and industrial systems.

▪️ Deep tech — hard tech, hardware, advanced materials, advanced manufacturing, and quantum.

▪️ Defense tech and dual-use — autonomous systems, drones, sensing and communications, and manufacturing for defense.

▪️ Space tech — satellites, launch and in-space systems, space robotics and autonomy, earth observation, and aerospace.

▪️ Semiconductors and AI infrastructure — chips, compute, and data center efficiency.

▪️ Cybersecurity — from early-stage products to growth-stage companies.

▪️ Health and life sciences — digital health, medical devices and diagnostics, healthcare services and IT, pharma services, therapeutics, life science tools, and biotech.

▪️ Climate and energy — energy management software, electrification, smart manufacturing, sustainability, and waste management and recycling.

▪️ Fintech — AI built for financial services, financial data and decisioning, tokenization, and fintech founders building across Africa.

▪️ Enterprise AI and SaaS — applied AI for businesses, AI operations, and software for overlooked industries like agriculture, logistics, education, and healthcare delivery.

▪️ Consumer and media — consumer AI applications and media.

Stage interest: Pre-seed to Series B.

Some of the investors are sector agnostic, backing exceptional founders building in any industry.

If you're building in any of these areas and looking for capital to scale, consider applying for the November cohort.

text:
Why is $NYKAA stock flat even after 4x Revenue Growth? 📈📉

A look at Nykaa’s financials from FY21 to FY26:

📊 The Numbers:

• Sales: ₹2,441 Cr ➔ ₹10,022 Cr (~4.1x expansion)
• Net Profit: ₹62 Cr ➔ ₹204 Cr (~3.3x expansion)
• Stock Price (Adjusted): ₹331 ➔ ₹339 (~1.1x / flat)

🔍 3 Key Takeaways:

1️⃣ Valuation Realignment: Nykaa listed during the 2021 tech boom at a massive ~1,600x P/E valuation. Even as earnings grew 3.3x, the P/E multiple compressed back toward realistic market realities.

2️⃣ Margin Compression & Reinvestment: Heavy capex into Nykaa Fashion, 230+ physical offline stores, and eB2B (Superstore) kept net margins low (~1–2%) during growth years before rebounding in FY26.

 3️⃣ Bonus Adjustments: The headline price drop after 2022 was due to a 5:1 bonus issue. On an adjusted basis, the stock has traded sideways while the underlying business caught up to its initial valuation.

💡 The takeaway: Top-line growth doesn't guarantee stock returns if initial entry valuations are sky-high.

What are your thoughts on $NYKAA at current levels? 💬

“He was the first #BritishSoldier to die in action in #HelmandProvince. On 11th June 2006, #Captain #JimPhilippson was killed during a fierce firefight in #Sangin, #Afghanistan, after British troops came under heavy attack.”

Captain Jim Philippson was 29 years old when he died, but in the short span of his military career he had already built a reputation for the qualities that would define his service: determination, professionalism, confidence and an enthusiasm for life that those around him remembered long after he was gone. 🎖️

Born in St Albans, #Hertfordshire, Jim studied at Plymouth University before joining the #Army in January 2001. After completing his training at the #RoyalMilitaryAcademy #Sandhurst, he was commissioned into the #RoyalArtillery later that year. His abilities quickly became apparent, and after his Young Officers’ Course at Larkhill, he was selected to serve with 29 Commando Regiment Royal Artillery.

Commando service demanded more than physical strength. Jim embraced the challenge of selection and, according to his commanding officer, demonstrated mental robustness alongside his physical stamina. During his time with #29CommandoRegiment he served in #Iraq and took part in exercises overseas, including in Norway, the #UnitedStates and Cyprus.

Those who served with him remembered something beyond his professional ability. He could be highly driven without losing his sense of humour, and confident without becoming distant. The Ministry of Defence described him as a gifted, considerate and popular officer whose relaxed manner and enthusiasm earned the respect of his soldiers and peers.

After his time with 29 Commando Regiment, Jim volunteered for another demanding chapter, joining #7ParachuteRegiment #RoyalHorseArtillery. He spent six months in the #FalklandIslands 🇫🇰  before joining the regiment in February 2006 as it prepared for the deployment to Afghanistan.

In Helmand, his responsibilities included training and mentoring members of the #ANA Afghan National Army. His patience, technical knowledge and ability to communicate made him an important part of that work. But on the evening of 11th June, his role changed dramatically.

A #British patrol in the Sangin area had come under sustained #attack, leaving two soldiers seriously wounded. A rapid reaction force was sent to help them. As the force moved towards the embattled patrol, it too came under fire. #CaptainPhilippson was among those caught in the ensuing firefight.

He was #killed during the engagement. Two other British soldiers were seriously injured. His death marked the #first British #fatality caused by enemy action in Helmand, a moment that would come to symbolise the beginning of an extraordinarily intense period of fighting for British forces in the province.

His commanding officer, #LieutenantColonel #DavidHammond, remembered him as a “rising star” who had an enormous amount to offer. His father, Anthony, spoke not only of his son's courage but of his love for military life, saying Jim could never have imagined himself working behind a desk.

Jim Philippson's service had lasted only a few years, yet his influence was felt by the soldiers and friends who knew him. He was remembered not simply for the uniform he wore, but for the personality within it — lively, ambitious, sociable, professional and deeply committed to those around him. 🕊️

🇬🇧 **A Life Cut Short — Captain Jim Philippson, 7 Parachute Regiment Royal Horse Artillery. Killed in action in Helmand Province, Afghanistan, on 11 June 2006, aged 29. His name remains part of the story of those who served and sacrificed in Afghanistan.**

📸 **Photograph caption:** Captain Jim Philippson, 7 Parachute Regiment Royal Horse Artillery, remembered for his service in Iraq, the Falkland Islands and Afghanistan, where he was killed in action on 11 June 2006. 🌹

text:
🚨 RUSSIA PLAGUE PANIC: WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS SLOP

The claim: A lab worker in Irkutsk dropped a test tube of pneumonic plague, died two days later, and 200 people are under quarantine. Russia denies it.

The reality is messier than both sides admit.

What is confirmed:

· Darya Shipilova, 28, a technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, died after being hospitalized with severe pneumonia of unknown origin .
· She had recently returned from a work trip to Buryatia, a region with endemic plague in rodent populations .
· Up to 200 contacts were placed under medical observation as a precaution .
· Post-mortem tests found no microorganisms linked to her professional work. The cause remains "undetermined" .
· The WHO estimates the risk as moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, and very low for Europe .

What is not confirmed:

· The broken test tube story. It originated from anonymous sources and was not verified by official channels .
· The claim that she died of plague. Russian officials deny it. Local officials who initially said "plague" later edited their statements to "maybe" .

The panic is being amplified by:

· Deleted warning messages from local officials.
· AI-generated or unrelated videos of hazmat suits .
· Screenshots of a "quarantine document" that Rospotrebnadzor calls fake .

Trump's take? He called it "the pneumonia plague" and said "the germs have become stronger and smarter, like an army" . He offered US assistance. Russia responded by offering to help the US with its own infectious diseases .

Bottom line: A woman is dead. The cause is undetermined. The plague claim is unconfirmed. The panic is real. The facts are not.

Don't confuse uncertainty with evidence. But don't confuse a denial with transparency. 🔥💀

Oil prices and a resolution concerning gasoline, diesel, light crude, heavy crude, and geographical areas in the US.
Your point about taxes is exactly what many economists warn about—when you place a heavy tax on a producer, they often pass that cost directly onto the consumer, pushing pump prices even higher.
Your idea of using strategic government grants to position light-crude refineries based on regional needs is an approach that aligns with "industrial policy," similar to how the U.S. government subsidized the domestic microchip industry.
If the government used direct grants to strategically place or upgrade refineries, it would solve several major regional vulnerabilities:
1. Fixing the East Coast Pipeline Bottleneck
The Problem: The U.S. East Coast does not have enough pipeline capacity to bring surplus fuel up from the massive refinery hubs in the Gulf Coast (Texas and Louisiana). Because of this, states like New York and Massachusetts are highly dependent on importing expensive, finished foreign gasoline from Europe and Canada [EIA].
The Strategic Fix: A targeted government grant could fund a dedicated light-shale refinery or a major expansion in the Northeast. This would allow the region to refine its own fuel locally, completely bypassing the pipeline bottleneck and lowering regional pump prices.
2. Safeguarding the Midwest Against Refinery Maintenance Spikes
The Problem: The Midwest relies heavily on a small cluster of refineries. When just one of these plants goes offline for seasonal maintenance or an unexpected mechanical issue, gas prices in states like Illinois, Indiana, and Michigan instantly spike by 50 cents or more.
The Strategic Fix: Placing smaller, highly efficient "modular" light-crude refineries near major Midwest transit hubs would create an immediate regional backup supply, stabilizing prices when major plants go down.
The Financial "Nudge"
To make your "nudge" work without costing taxpayers trillions, the government could structure the grants using a matching system:
The federal government offers to cover 30% to 50% of the construction costs using infrastructure grants.
In exchange, the oil company must agree to source 100% of the raw crude oil domestically (using American light shale) and guarantee that the finished fuel stays within that specific U.S. region.
This method uses a carrot instead of a stick. It takes the "obscene" corporate revenues you mentioned earlier and incentivizes companies to reinvest them directly into American energy security, rather than punishing them with taxes that ultimately hurt the consumer.
This is the easiest long term fix!
We need to take control of our future!
