text:
SALVATION BY WORKS
C H Spurgeon

THE IDEA
of salvation by the merit of our own works is exceedingly insinuating. It matters not how often it is refuted, it asserts itself again and again; and when it gains the least foothold, it soon makes great advances. Hence Paul, who was determined to show it no quarter, opposed everything which bore its likeness. He was determined not to permit the thin edge of the wedge to be introduced into the Church, for well he knew that willing hands would soon be driving it home; hence, when Peter sided with the Judaizing party, and seemed to favor those who demanded that the Gentiles should be circumcised, our brave apostle withstood him to the face.

He fought always for salvation by grace through faith, and contended strenuously against all thought of righteousness by obedience to the precepts of the ceremonial law. No one could be more explicit than he upon the doctrine that we are not justified or saved by works in any degree, but solely by the grace of God. His trumpet gave forth no uncertain sound, but gave forth the clear note, "By grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God." (Eph. 2:8,9.) Grace meant grace with him, and he could not endure any tampering with the matter, or any frittering away of its meaning.

So fascinating is the doctrine of legal righteousness that the only way to deal with it is Paul's way. Never yield to it; but remember the apostle's firmness, and how stoutly he held his ground: "To whom," saith he, "we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour." (Gal. 2:5.)

The error of salvation by works is exceedingly plausible. You will constantly hear it stated as a self-evident truth, and vindicated on account of its supposed practical usefulness, while the gospel doctrine of salvation by faith is railed at and accused of evil consequences. It is affirmed that if we preach salvation by good works, we shall encourage virtue; and so it might seem in theory, but history proves by many instances that as a matter of fact where such doctrine has been preached, virtue has become singularly uncommon, and that in proportion as the merit of works has been cried up, morality has gone down.

On the other hand, where justification by faith has been preached, conversions have followed, and purity of life has been produced even in the worst of men. Those who lead godly and gracious lives are ready to confess that the cause for their zeal for holiness lies in their faith in Christ Jesus; but where will you meet with a devout and upright man who glories in his own works?

SELF-RIGHTEOUSNESS IS NATURAL
to our fallen humanity. Hence, it is the essence of all false religions. Be they what they may, they all agree in seeking salvation by your own deeds. He who worships his idols will torture his body, will fast, will perform long pilgrimages, and do or endure anything in order to merit salvation.

Go where you may, the natural religion of fallen man is salvation by his own merits. An old preacher has well said, "Every man is born a heretic upon this point, and he naturally gravitates toward this heresy in one form or another. Self-salvation, either by his personal worthiness, or by his repentance, or by his resolves, is a hope ingrained in human nature, and very hard to remove. This foolishness is bound up in the heart of every child, and who shall get it out of him?"

This erroneous idea arises partly from ignorance, for men are ignorant of the law of God, and of what holiness really is. If they knew that even one evil deed is a breach of the law, and that the law once broken in any point is altogether violated, they would be at once convinced that there can be no righteousness by the law to those who have already offended against it.

Nor is it ignorance alone which leads men to self-righteousness: they are also deceived by pride. Man cannot endure to be saved on the footing of mercy; he loves not to plead guilty and throw himself on the favor of the Lord; he cannot brook to be treated as a pauper, and blessed as a matter of charity; he desires to have a finger in his own salvation, and claim at least a little credit for it. Proud man will not have heaven itself upon terms of grace; but so long as he can, he sets up one plea or another, and holds to his own righteousness as though it were his life.

This self-confidence also arises from wicked unbelief, for through his self-conceit man will not believe God. Nothing is more plainly revealed in Scripture than this-that by the works of the law shall no man be justified, yet men in some shape or other stick to the hope of legal righteousness; they will have it that they must prepare for grace, or assist mercy,' or in some degree deserve eternal life. They prefer their own flattering prejudices to the declarations of the heart-searching God. The testimony of the Holy Spirit concerning the deceitfulness of the heart is cast aside, and the declaration of God that there is none that doeth good, no, not one, is altogether denied. Is not this a great evil?
Self-righteousness is also much promoted by the almost universal spirit of trifling which is now abroad. Only while men trifle with themselves can they entertain the idea of personal merit before God. He who comes to serious thought, and begins to understand the character of God, before whom the heavens are not pure, and the angels are charged with folly-he, I say, that comes to serious thought, and beholds a true vision of God, abhors himself in dust and ashes, and is forever silenced as to any thought of self-justification.

I.
TWO GREAT CRIMES
are contained in self-righteousness. It frustrates the grace of God, and makes Christ to have died in vain.
1. The word here translated "frustrate" means to "make void"-needless. Now, he that hopes to be saved by his own righteousness annuls the grace or free favor of God, treats it as useless, and in that way frustrates it.

It is clear, first, that if righteousness come by the law, the grace of God is no longer required. If we can be saved by our own merits, we need justice, but we certainly do not want mercy. If we can keep the law, and claim to be accepted as a matter of debt, it is plain that we need not turn suppliants, and crave for mercy. Grace is a superfluity where merit can be proved.

A man who can go into court with a clear case and bold countenance asks not for mercy of the judge, and the offer of it would insult him. "Give me justice," he says: "give me my rights;" and he stands up for them as a brave man would do. It is only when a man feels that the law condemns him that he puts in a plea for mercy. Nobody ever dreamed of recommending an innocent man to mercy. I say, then, that the man who believes that by keeping the law, or by practicing ceremonies, or by undergoing religious performances, he can make himself acceptable before God, most decidedly puts the grace of God on one side as a superfluous thing as far as he is concerned. Is it not clearly so? And is not this a crimson crime-this frustration of the grace of God?

He makes the grace of God to be at least a secondary thing, which is only a lower degree of the same error. Many think that they are to merit as much as they can by their own exertions, and then the grace of God will make up for the rest. The theory seems to be that we are to keep the law as far as we can, and this imperfect obedience is to stand good, as a sort of composition, say a shilling in the pound, or fifteen shillings in the pound, according as a man judges of his own excellence; and then what is required over and above our own hard-earned money, the grace of God will supply: in short, the plan is, every man his own savior, and Jesus Christ and His grace make-weights for our deficiencies.

Whether men see it or not, this admixture of law and grace is most dishonoring to the salvation of Jesus Christ. It makes the Savior's work to be incomplete, though on the cross He cried, "It is finished." Yea, it even treats it as being utterly ineffectual, since it appears to be of no avail till man's works are added to it. According to this notion, we are redeemed as much by our own doings as by the ransom price of Jesus' blood, and man and Christ go shares, both in the work and in the glory. This is an intense form of arrogant treason against the majesty of divine mercy-a capital crime, which will condemn all who continue in it.

More than that, he who trusts in himself, his feelings, his works, his prayers, or in anything except the grace of God, virtually gives up trusting in the grace of God altogether: for be it known unto you, that God's grace will never share the work with man's merit. As oil will not combine with water, so neither will human merit and heavenly mercy mix together. The apostle saith in Rom. 11:6, "If by grace, then it is no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace.

But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work."

You must either have salvation wholly because you deserve it, or wholly because God graciously bestows it, though you do not deserve it. You must receive salvation at the Lord's hand either as a debt or as a charity; there can be no mingling of the ideas. That which is a pure donation of favor -cannot also be a reward of personal deserving. A combination of the two principles of law and grace is utterly impossible. Trust in our own works in any degree effectually shuts us out from all hope of salvation by grace: and so it frustrates the grace of God.

This hoping to be saved by our own righteousness robs God of His glory. It as good as says, "We want no grace; we need no free favor." It reads of the new covenant which infinite love has made, but by clinging to the old covenant it puts dishonor upon it. In its heart it murmurs, "What need of this covenant of grace? The covenant of works answers every purpose for us." It reads of the great gift of grace in the person of Jesus Christ, and it does despite thereto by the secret thought that human doings are as good as the life and death of the Son of God. It cries, "We will not have this Man to save us."

A self-righteous hope casts a slur upon the glory of God, since it is clear that if a man could be saved by his own works, he would naturally have the honor of it; but if a man be -saved by the free grace of God. then God is glorified. Woe unto those who teach a doctrine which would pluck the crown royal from the head of our sovereign Lord and disgrace the throne of His glory. God help us to be clear of this rank offense against high heaven.

I grow warm upon such a subject as this, for my indignation rises against that which does dishonor to my Lord, and frustrates His grace. This is a sin so gross that even the heathen cannot commit it. They have never heard of the grace of God, and therefore they cannot put a slight upon it: when they perish, it will be with a far lighter doom than those who have been told that God is gracious and ready to pardon, and yet turn on their heel and wickedly boast of innocence, and pretend to be clean in the sight of God. This is a sin which devils cannot commit. With all the obstinacy of their rebellion, they can never reach to this. They have never had the sweet notes of free grace and dying love ringing in their ears, and therefore they have never so used the heavenly invitation. What has never been presented to their acceptance, cannot be the object of their rejection. Thus, then, my hearer, if you should fall into this deep ditch, you will sink lower than the heathen, lower• than Sodom and Gomorrah, and lower than the devil himself. Wake up, I pray you, and do not dare to frustrate the grace of God.

2. The second great crime which self—justification commits is making Christ to have died in vain. This is plain enough. If salvation can be by the works of the law, why did our Lord Jesus die to save us? 0 Thou bleeding Lamb of God! Thine incarnation is a marvel, but Thy death upon the accursed tree is such a miracle of mercy as fills all heaven with astonishment. Will any dare to say that Thy death, 0 Lord, who are also the incarnate God, was a superfluity, a wanton waste of suffering? Do they dare think Thee a generous but unwise enthusiast, whose death was needless? Yes, thousands virtually do this, and, in fact, all do so who make it out that men might have been saved in some other way, or may now be saved by their own willing and doing.

The doctrine of salvation by works is a sin against all the fallen sons of Adam, for if men cannot be saved except by their own works, what hope is left for any transgressor? You shut the gates of mercy on mankind; you condemn the guilty to die without the possibility of remission. You deny all hope of welcome to the returning prodigal, all prospect of paradise to the dying thief.

Nor is this all. It is a sin against the saints, for none of them have any other hope except in the blood of Jesus Christ. Remove the doctrine of the atoning blood, and you have taken all away; our foundation is gone. If you speak thus, you offend the whole generation of godly men.

I go further: work-mongering is a sin against the perfect ones above. The doctrine of salvation by works would silence the halleluiahs of heaven. Hush, ye choristers, what meaning is there in your song? You are chanting, "Unto Him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in His own blood." But why sing ye so? If salvation be by works, your ascriptions of praise are empty flatteries. You ought to sing, "Unto ourselves who kept our garments clean, to us be glory forever and ever:" or, at least, "Unto ourselves whose acts made the Redeemer's work' effectual, be a full share of praise." But a self-lauding note was never heard in heaven, and therefore we feel sure that the doctrine of self-justification is not of God.

I charge you, renounce it as the foe of God and mail. This proud system is a sin of deepest dye against the Well-Beloved. To say that Christ came to earth for nothing is bad enough; but that He became obedient to the death of the cross without result is profanity at its worst.

II.
But, in the second place, I proceed to the solemn fact that -
THESE TWO GREAT CRIMES ARE COMMITTED BY MANY PEOPLE
I am afraid they are committed by some who hear me this day. Let every one search himself and see if these accursed things be not hidden in his heart, and if they be, let him cry unto God for deliverance from them.

1. Assuredly these crimes are chargeable on those who trifle with the gospel. Here is the grand proclamation of the Sovereign's grace to fallen man - to sinners - the most wonderful knowledge that ever was revealed, and yet you do not think it worth a thought!

The death of Christ is nothing to you-a very beautiful fact, no doubt; you know the story well, but you do not care enough about it to wish to be a partaker in its benefits. His blood may have power to cleanse from sin, but you do not want remission; His death may be the life of men, but you do not long to live by Him. To be saved by the atoning blood does not strike you as being half so important as to carry on your business as a profit and acquire a fortune for your family. By thus trifling with these precious things you do, as far as you can, frustrate the grace of God and make Christ to die in vain.

2. Another set of people who do this are those who have no sense of guilt. Perhaps they are naturally amiable, civil, honest, and generous people, and they think that these natural virtues are all that is needed. We have many such in whom there is much, that is lovely, but the one thing needful is lacking. They are not conscious that they ever did anything very wrong, they think themselves certainly as good as others, and in some respects rather better.

You are very bad, because you are so proud as to think yourself righteous, though God hath said that "there is none righteous, no, not one." (Rom. 3:10.) You tell your God that He is a liar. His Word accuses you, and His law condemns you; but you will not believe Him, and actually boast of having a righteousness of your own. This is high presumption and arrogant pride, and may the Lord purge you from it!

3. Another sort of people may fancy that they shall escape; but we must now come home to them. Those who despair will often cry, "I know I cannot be saved except by grace, for I am such a great sinner; but, alas! I am too great a sinner to be saved at all. I am too black for Christ to wash out my sins." Ah, my dear friend, though you know it not, you are making void the grace of God, by denying its power and limiting its might. You doubt the efficacy of the Redeemer's blood, and the power of the Father's grace.

What! The grace of God: is not that able to save? Is not the Father of our Lord Jesus able to forgive sins? We joyfully sing-
"Who is a pardoning God like Thee?
Or who hath grace so rich and free?"
And you say He cannot forgive you, and this in the teeth of His many promises of mercy. 0, say not so: let not thine unbelief give the lie to God.

4. And those, I think, commit this sin in a large measure, who make a mingle-mangle of the gospel. I mean this: when we preach the gospel we have only to say, "Sinners, you are guilty: you can never be anything else but guilty in and of yourselves; if that sin of yours be pardoned, it must be through an act of sovereign grace, and not because of anything in you, or that can be done by you. Grace must be given to you because Jesus died, and for no other reason; and the way by which you can obtain that grace is simply by trusting Christ. By faith in Jesus Christ you shall obtain full forgiveness." This is pure gospel.

If the man turns round and inquires, "How am. I warranted to believe in Christ?" If I tell him that he is warranted to believe in Christ because he feels a law work within, or because he has holy desires, I have made a mess of it: I have put something of the man into the question, and marred the glory of grace. Those who mingle their "ifs" and "buts," and insist upon "you must do this, and feel that, before you may accept Christ," frustrate the grace of God in a measure, and do damage to the glorious gospel of the blessed God.

5. And so, once more, do those also who apostatize. Do I speak to any here who were once professors of religion, who once used to offer prayer in the assembly, who once walked as saints, but now have gone back? You, my friend, say by your course of life, "I had the grace of God, but I do not care about it: it is worth nothing, I have gone back to the world." You do as good as say, "I did once trust in Jesus Christ, but He is not worth trusting."

You have denied, and sold your Lord and Master. I will not now go into the question as to whether you ever were sincere, though I believe you never were, but on your own showing such is your case. Take heed, lest these two terrible crimes should rest upon you, that you do frustrate the grace of God, and make Christ to have died in vain.

III.
Now, in closing, I shall carry with me the deep convictions and the joyful confidences of all true believers. It is this, that -
EVERY TRUE BELIEVER’S TRUST IS IN JESUS ALONE
Come, now, honest hearts, I speak to you. Do you trust in grace alone, or do you in some measure rest in yourselves? Do you even in a small degree depend upon your own feelings, your own faithfulness, your own repentance? I know you abhor the very thought. You have not even the shadow of a hope, nor the semblance of a confidence, in anything you ever were, or ever can be, or ever hope to be. You fling this away as a foul rag which you would hurl out of the universe if you could.

I do avow that though I have preached the gospel with all my heart, and glory in it, yet I cast my preaching away as dross if I think of it as a ground of reliance: and though I have brought many souls to Christ, blessed be His name, I never dare for one moment put the slightest confidence in that fact as to my own salvation. I repose alone in my Redeemer.

What I say of myself I know that each one of you will say for himself. Your alms-giving, your prayers, your tears, your suffering persecution, your earnest work in the Sunday-school or elsewhere-do you ever think of putting these side by side with the blood of Christ as your hope? No, you never dream of it; I am sure you never do, and the mention of it is utterly loathsome, to you: is it not? Grace, grace, grace is your sole hope.

Moreover, you have not only renounced all confidence in works, but you renounce it this day more heartily than ever you did. The older you are, and the more holy you become, the less do you think of trusting in yourself. I know there are some who never felt themselves to be sinners, who shift about as if they were sitting on thorns when I am preaching grace, and nothing but grace; but it is not so with you who are resting in Christ. "0, no," you say, "ring that bell again, sir!" Ring that bell again; there is no music like it. Touch that string again; it is our favorite note."

The true believer trusts in the death of Christ; he puts his sole and entire reliance upon the great Substitute who loved and lived and died for him. He does not dare to associate with the bleeding sacrifice, his poor bleeding heart, or his prayers, or his sanctification, or anything else. "None but Christ, none but Christ," is his soul's cry.

He detests every proposal to mix anything of ceremony or of legal action with the finished work of Jesus Christ. The longer we live, I trust, dear brethren, the more we see the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. We are struck with admiration at the wisdom of the way by which a Substitute was introduced-that God might smite sin and yet spare the sinner; we are lost in admiration at the matchless love of God, that He spared not His own Son; we are filled with reverent adoration at the love of Christ, that when He knew the price of pardon was His blood, His pity never withdrew.

We are one with Him, and, being one with Him, we realize more every day that He did not die in vain. His death has bought us real life: His death has already set us free from the bondage of sin, and has even now brought us deliverance from the fear of eternal wrath. His death has bought us life eternal, has bought us sonship, and all the blessings that go with it, which the Father takes care to bestow; the death of Christ has shut the gates of hell for us, and opened the gates of heaven; the death of Christ has wrought for us mercies, not visionary or imaginary, but real and true, which this very day we do enjoy, and so we are in no danger of thinking that Christ died in vain.

It is our joy to hold these
TWO GREAT PRINCIPLES
which I will leave with you, hoping that you will suck marrow and fatness out. of them, that the grace of God cannot be frustrated, and Jesus Christ died not in vain. These two principles, I think, lie at the bottom of all sound doctrine. The grace of God cannot be frustrated after alt. Its eternal purpose will be fulfilled, its sacrifice and seal shall be effectual: the chosen ones of grace shall be brought to glory. There shall be no failures as to God's plan in any point whatever: at the last, when all shall be summed up, it shall be seen that grace reigned through righteousness unto eternal life, and the top stone shall be brought out with shoutings of "Grace, grace unto it."

And as grace cannot be frustrated, so Christ did not die in vain. Some seem to think that there were purposes in Christ's heart which will never be accomplished. We have not so learned Christ. What He died to do shall be done; His own He will have; those He redeemed shall be free; there shall be no failure of reward for Christ's wondrous work: "He shall see of the travail of His soul and shall be satisfied."

On these two principles I throw back my soul to rest. Believing in His grace, that grace shall never fail me. "My grace is sufficient for thee," saith the Lord, and, so shall it be. Believing in Jesus Christ, His death must save me. It cannot be, O Calvary, that thou shouldst fail! O Gethsemane, that thy bloody sweat should be in vain! Through divine grace, resting in our Savior's precious blood, we must be saved. Joy and rejoice with me, and go your way to tell it out to others. God bless you in so doing for Jesus' sake. Amen.

A lot of people are waiting for me to say I support APC. 

So here it goes. 

As a human being, what Tinubu has achieved in his personal life coming from where he came from is the stuff of legends.

An orphan boy who worked his way from relative obscurity and did everything that was necessary to ensure his own survival and freedom long enough to amass enough wealth and power to rule the most populous black country on earth. 

It takes grit, balls and intelligence.

How I believe he's gone about doing this is exactly what disqualifies him as a role model. His role should have always been in the background. The conscience of a nation should not be weighed down by the alleged criminal past of its president. 

Somewhere in his journey, he lost the very thing that qualifies a leader from a ruler. 

His ability to care about the plight of anything that does not advance his personal goals and ambition. 

It's the kind of machiavellian nature that's useful in the criminal underworld as the boss of a crime family. 

That skill doesn't translate well when you're leading 100s of millions of people who can offer you nothing personally. 

A president needs to be someone who can bare the burdens of a suffering masses without breaking down or becoming too stoic that he cannot feel for his own people. 

I don't think you go from orphan to president by being soft at your core. 

Unfortunately we don't have any leadership schools that teaches people how to transform from the hard core person that grabs power to a soft core person with the ability to feel for other humans. 

Because you do need the ability to be empathetic to be a leader and in the world that raised Tinubu, empathy is a weakness. 

As for Lagos elections, I don't really have a dog in that fight. I think APC will win because they're too entrenched and the opposition is split. 

So if this reads as me being pro APC. Have at it.

Long short equity has done one thing with mechanical consistency for 34 years: cut stock market volatility nearly in half.   

Meketa data comparing the HFRI Equity Hedge Index to the Russell 3000 across three trailing windows ending April 2026:   

1.) Volatility capture never moved:
• 34 Years: 8.8% versus 15.1% (58% of market risk)
• 20 Years: 8.8% versus 15.8% (56% of market risk)
• 10 Years: 8.9% versus 15.8% (56% of market risk)   

2.) Return capture shifted across cycles:
• 34 Years: 10.0% annualized versus 11.0% (91% capture, Sharpe 0.84 versus 0.56)
• 20 Years: 5.6% annualized versus 10.7% (52% capture, Sharpe 0.45 versus 0.57)
• 10 Years: 8.8% annualized versus 14.8% (59% capture)   

The mandate was never to outrun an unhedged mega cap tech index during a decade of zero rates. The mandate was capital preservation and volatility dampening with equity upside.   

On that specification, the engine functioned as designed.   

Two macro takeaways for allocators:

First, manager dispersion is massive. Meketa puts the 10 year spread between top and bottom quartile managers at 15.1 percentage points, versus 5.0 for large cap long only. You cannot buy the index average. Manager selection is the entire bet.

Second, turnover and short exposure generate short term gains. If you do not solve for asset location, taxes will consume the risk adjusted edge.

Long short equity is not a separate asset class. It is public equity exposure engineered for lower net beta.

text:
Ulysses Grant won the Civil War and served two terms as president. At 62 he and his wife had $210 in cash between them. The man who got them out was Mark Twain.

Grant had put $100,000 into a Wall Street firm, Grant & Ward. His son was a partner. The other partner, Ferdinand Ward, paid the family 2 to 3% a month.

Worked out:
2% a month compounds to 27% a year.
3% a month compounds to 43% a year.

Ward had no business that earned it. He paid old investors with new deposits.

On Sunday, May 4, 1884, Ward asked for $150,000 to get through Monday. Grant borrowed it from William Vanderbilt the same day. The firm failed on Tuesday. It owed close to $17 million and held about $67,000.

Vanderbilt offered to forgive the loan. Grant refused.

That autumn doctors found cancer in his throat. He began his memoirs so his wife would have something.

The Century Company offered the standard 10% royalty. Twain heard the terms and offered 70% of the profits through his own firm. Grant signed on February 27, 1885. He finished the manuscript in July and died within the week.

Worked out:
Julia Grant received about $450,000, roughly 30% of sales.
At 10% she gets about $150,000.
One clause, about $300,000.

Nine years later that same firm failed and took Twain into bankruptcy.

Grant never checked a number that looked too good.
Twain checked one that looked standard.

The Personal Memoirs are free on Project Gutenberg.

Vanderbilt offered to forgive the $150,000. Would you have taken it?

text:
⚠️ Before you sign a contract, you read the conditions, unless of course you're Melanie Joly, then you just fake it. Before you commit an entire country, you show the conditions to the people who will have to live with them. This is something Mark Carney must learn now.

After eleven years of Liberal government, I am fresh out of confidence in the Liberal government's sales pitch. "Trust us" is not an explanation. It is precisely what makes me want to read the fine print.

Canadians are struggling to keep their homes, pay their bills and give their children a decent start. We cannot afford to discover the catch after Ottawa has congratulated itself and signed the paperwork on behalf of 41+ million Canadians.

Carney's government is planning a deeper, more integrated relationship with the EU, including financial services and opportunities for young people to live, work and study on either side of the Atlantic.

Lovely... so where are the conditions? And what, exactly, are the requirements of an associate membership?

Canada already trades with Europe. CETA made 98% of EU tariff lines duty-free for Canadian goods when it took provisional effect in 2017. We also already have trade agreements across the Asia-Pacific region. Carney did not discover overseas commerce.

Meanwhile, the United States still received 71.7% of Canada's merchandise exports in 2025. Every other market combined accounted for the remaining 28.3%. Diversification matters, but replacing the scale of our American market requires considerably more than an enthusiastic speech in Europe.

If better trade is the justification, show us what this arrangement would deliver beyond our existing agreements. Show us the expected gains, the costs and the attached conditions. What additional access are we buying, and what authority might we give up to obtain it?

For comparison, existing full EU members have the following obligations. They would not automatically apply to Canada, but they show why we cannot afford to turn a blind eye to this, and why demanding the details matters:

- Contribute Money: The largest funding source is based on gross national income, or GNI, rather than simply GDP. Calculating from the Commission's 2025 figures, national contributions averaged approximately €4.9 billion PER COUNTRY, excluding customs revenue and before any EU funding dispersement is received back. That is not Canada's prospective bill. What would ours be? What would we receive? Which priorities at home would wait?

- Adopt and Implement EU Rule: Which Canadian laws and standards would have to change? Who has asked our small businesses, manufacturers, farmers and employers what compliance would cost them? They deserve an answer before being handed another expensive obligation dressed up as an opportunity, and before government starts dangling outrageous "we've got your back" loans to help them survive the expense.

- Accept the Precedence of Applicable EU Law: Within areas of authority assigned to the EU, EU law takes precedence over conflicting national law. This reaches beyond trade promotion into who has the final legal say. Would Canada accept anything comparable? Could Parliament reject a requirement? What happens if we refuse? Carney called off trade talks when Trump demanded some of the very same conditions the EU members abide by, remember?

- Participate in Free Movement of Goods, Services, Capital and People Including their Immigrants and Refugees: What new rights would Canada grant, to whom, and with what limits? What would that mean for housing, employment and public services?

- Commit to Adopting the Euro Once Conditions Are Met: (excluding Denmark, which has an exeption) An associate arrangement would not automatically require Canada to adopt the euro, nor would Denmark’s exemption automatically become ours. Would the agreement explicitly protect our dollar and monetary authority? Carney's documented 2019 proposal explored a potential digital international reserve currency to reduce dependence on the US dollar and that conversation reared its ugly head again just  recently.

And I want the net-zero questions answered just as plainly.

When Carney left Brookfield's chairmanship, the company credited him with helping establish its position in energy-transition investment. Ottawa's new nature-financing taskforce is examining private investment and financial mechanisms, explicitly linked in its announcement to a net-zero economy.

Would this EU arrangement bind Canada to climate targets, carbon-pricing requirements, investment rules or nature-financing commitments? Which businesses could benefit, including Brookfield? What disclosures and safeguards would apply? What are the exit clauses?

Could Canadians elect a government to reverse those policies, only to discover that Ottawa had already committed us to keeping them by entrenching irreversible laws preventing future governments from repealing them? I want to know what the next government could change, what it could cancel and what getting out would cost.

Which brings us to the sovereignty sermon. When Washington makes demands during trade talks, Canadian sovereignty apparently requires every elbow in the country to immediately rise in an upwards motion as a sign of national fealty. But when Brussels offers deeper integration, potentially involving binding rules and shared authority, those same elbows are suddenly rushing to hold the signing pen, so it seems.

Does sovereignty have a preferred flag? Is outside influence an outrage until it arrives with a European accent? If Carney says this strengthens our independence, then he can damn well explain exactly how, in ordinary language.

Which decisions remain ours? Which become shared? Which require somebody else's approval? Spare us the vocabulary that requires a translator at the kitchen table. An impressive résumé does not answer a question, and fluent delivery does not fill in missing conditions and limitations.

I want Canadians listening for what is absent: the price, the limits, the enforcement and the exit. Until those are explained, "Canada Strong" remains a Liberal government slogan.

And before anyone signs, show us how we leave should we need to! If the arrangement fails Canada, could a future government withdraw? How much notice would be required? What payments or obligations would survive? Could Parliament restore Canadian rules without compensation claims or other penalties?

An associate arrangement would not automatically mean joining the European Parliament. The question is whether Canada would accept rules made through EU institutions, and what power Canadians would have to challenge or change them. The government can negotiate international agreements, however that does not settle whether Canadians should consent to this one before it becomes binding.

Show us the conditions. Explain the consequences. Let Canadians decide.

THAT IS WHY I CREATED PETITION e-7823.

It calls for:

- Public disclosure of the complete proposed terms and obligations before any agreement is signed.

- Preservation of Canada's sovereignty over legislative, judicial, fiscal and regulatory authority.

- A national referendum before entering any form of EU associate membership.

Whether you're a Liberal, Conservative or purple-spotted Martian, you deserve enough information to decide for yourself, it's your democratic right. I have no faith in a government sales pitch. I want disclosure, scrutiny and a vote. 

#MarkCarney did not campaign on this. He has no mandate to do this. Make our government accountable.

🙏🏻 Please sign petition e-7823
https://t.co/HyNDWNLxqO

After signing, you must check your email and follow the confirmation link so your signature counts... this is crucial!

If the deal is good enough for Canadians, then it should survive Canadians reading it and voting on it, wouldn’t you agree?

Melanie in Saskatchewan 💙

text:
The strait is not closed. Trump says so. That is the problem. 🛢️

CNBC, citing the Joint Maritime Information Center: about 20 commercial ships hit in the past month in Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, or off Oman. Mostly tankers.

📈 UK maritime monitors have logged nine attacks in the waterway already this month. Half of everything they logged for September in Hormuz and the Gulf combined.

A fifth of the world’s oil usually moves through this gap. The ships are still moving. The price of moving them is not.
Flows have climbed back to about 80 percent of prewar levels. The attacks sped up as the barrels came back.
September’s count was already lifted by four strikes in the last two days. October matched half of that month before the first week was over.
This is not a closure. A closure stops the oil. This prices the recovery.
💸 The number nobody is quoting sits in freight, not in crude.
On Monday the cost of carrying oil from inside the Persian Gulf to China hit $1.3 million a day. Baltic Exchange data. A record.
A tanker can still transit. The insurer, the owner, and the buyer pay for pretending the war is somewhere else.
One master, hailed north of Khasab, was told to turn back or be targeted. He turned back. No strike. The threat was the toll.
🇺🇸 In September Trump rejected Iran’s offer to reopen the strait within seven days. “They want a deal because they’re losing so badly.”
He said the United States has total control. He said the blockade is back. He posted a map labeled the Trump Strait.
He also said Washington should be reimbursed for protection. He described taking a ship, its cargo, and its oil. “We’re sort of like pirates, but we are not playing games.”

text:
Iraqi Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad visited Masoud Barzani today, referring to him as “President Masoud Barzani” as the two discussed relations between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

It is a remarkable transformation for a politician who, until becoming minister only five months ago, was among the KRG and KDP’s most aggressive opponents in Baghdad.

As an MP, Sanad led repeated attacks on the KRG over oil, revenues and federal transfers. He filed several lawsuits seeking to stop Baghdad from sending money to the Region, including the case that led the Federal Supreme Court in 2023 to invalidate government transfers to the KRG.

His rhetoric went much further than mere policy criticism. When Baghdad considered sending the KRG 800 billion dinars a month in 2023, Sanad described it as using public money to “buy political acceptance from the KDP.” In 2024, he said a “Kurdish-American lobby” had “swallowed” then-PM Mohammed Shia al-Sudani and described an agreement between Sudani and Barzani as a “down payment” for Sudani’s visit to Washington.

And in March 2025, Sanad filed a legal complaint against Dilshad Barzani, Masoud Barzani’s brother and the KRG representative in Germany, accusing him of normalization with Israel after he attended a Newroz event at the Israeli embassy in Berlin.

The transformation began after Sanad entered government in May. His appointment itself was politically interesting: at the last minute, Basra Governor Asaad al-Eidani, who has developed close relations with the Barzani leadership, joined Humam Hamoudi in backing Sanad for the Communications Ministry.

Since becoming minister, the lawsuits, accusations and confrontational rhetoric have largely disappeared. Sanad has become a frequent visitor to the Kurdistan Region, speaking warmly about cooperation with its government and now sitting with the same Barzani leadership he spent years portraying as extracting money and political concessions from Baghdad.

Whatever explains the change, few Iraqi politicians offer a clearer example of how dramatically political behaviour can change once someone moves from attacking the system from parliament to holding a seat inside government.

text:
THE 1PM TEST PASSED AT 4.93%. IN SEPTEMBER THE SAME LOAN COST 4.47%:

The Treasury sold $58B of new 3-year notes at 1:00pm ET, and buyers took all of it without asking for a better deal. With oil's early drop erased, cheaper borrowing was the last reason left under today's stock rally, and it held. The catch is the price: Washington paid almost half a percentage point more to borrow for three years than it did a month ago, and the market called that relief. This afternoon's rally rests on a borrowing cost that would have looked alarming in September.

Where the indexes sit at 2:12pm ET:

- S&P 500: 7,830.78, +56.83 points / +0.73% today.
- Nasdaq composite: 27,667.88, +190.57 points / +0.69% today.
- Dow Jones Industrial Average: 51,537.01, +269.11 points / +0.52% today.
- Russell 2000, as of 1:57pm ET: 2,834.62, -12.51 points / -0.44% today.

The S&P 500's record close is 7,798.99, from August 13. The index is about 32 points above it and barely noticed the sale, slipping for ten minutes after 1:00pm before climbing back.

What the sale showed, from the Treasury's own results:

- Yield: 4.932%, a hair under the 4.934% the note traded at just before the 1:00pm deadline.
- Bids: $153.1B for the $58B on offer.
- The Treasury's own count of bids per dollar sold: 2.62, vs 2.65 on average over the last six sales.
- Dealers' share: 10.7%, vs a 12.6% average.

Dealers are the big banks required to bid at every sale, and they keep whatever nobody else wants. A smaller dealer share means the rest of the market showed up.

The mix of buyers did shift:

- Bidders going through a dealer, mostly foreign central banks and large funds: 57.6%, vs a 65.9% average.
- Buyers bidding directly, largely US institutions: 31.7%, vs a 21.5% average.

One group stepped back and another filled the gap. That is adequate demand, not strong demand.

Now the price, against the same $58B sale four weeks earlier:

- September 8 yield: 4.474%.
- Today: 4.932%, up 0.458 percentage point.
- At today's yield, roughly $266M a year more in interest on this one sale than September's rate would have cost.

In between, the Federal Reserve raised its key rate on September 16, to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%. The open-market 3-year yield then touched 5.04% on September 29. Next to last week's peak, today's sale looks like good news. Next to September, it is a much more expensive loan.

The bond market took the result calmly:

- 3-year Treasury yield: 4.918%, down 0.043 percentage point from Monday's 4.961% close.
- 10-year Treasury yield: 5.265%, down 0.046 percentage point from Monday's 5.311% close.

The 10-year is what Washington pays to borrow for a decade, and it feeds mortgage rates and company loans. On Monday it touched 5.35%, its high of the past year. A slip of less than a twentieth of a point is relief, not a turn.

Oil is no longer helping:

- Brent crude futures: $100.47 a barrel, +$0.15 / +0.15% since Monday's close.

Brent, the global oil benchmark, hit $97.06 this morning. That whole drop is gone, and energy stocks have climbed back with it.

The leaders are the sectors that behave most like bonds:

- Utilities Select Sector SPDR (XLU) at $40.92, +$0.95 / +2.39% today.
- Real Estate Select Sector SPDR (XLRE) at $41.10, +$0.42 / +1.04% today.

Utilities lead all 11 sector funds, and real estate is roughly tied with industrials for second. Both borrow heavily and pay steady dividends, so investors treat them like bonds: they gain when yields fall. Utilities also have news of their own.

Constellation Energy (CEG) at $301.58, +$33.96 / +12.69% today.

The largest US owner of nuclear plants jumped after announcing two long-term power supply deals before the open. Constellation is on none of the six Len5 watchlists: at about 29 times its past year of profit at today's price, the value styles have no discount to weigh.

The weak spot is the group that should like cheaper money most:

- iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) at $281.65, -$1.73 / -0.61% today.
- SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI) at $151.07, -$5.12 / -3.27% today.

Smaller companies lean harder on borrowed money, and more of it carries a rate that resets with short-term rates. Biotech, a bigger slice of the small-company index than of the S&P 500, explains part of the drop. One yield explains the rest:

- 2-year Treasury yield: 4.791%, down 0.042 percentage point from Monday's 4.833% close.

The 2-year follows where investors expect the Fed's rate to go. It sits well above the Fed's range, so the bond market still expects more increases, not fewer. A good 3-year sale did not change that.

The rest of the calendar, Eastern time:

- 4:00pm: the close. A finish above 7,798.99 gives the S&P 500 its first record close since August 13.
- 7:00pm: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, a voter on rates this year, moderates a question-and-answer session with former Bank of Mexico Governor Agustin Carstens.
- Wednesday, 1:00pm: the Treasury sells $39B of 10-year notes.
- Wednesday, 2:00pm: minutes of the Fed's September 15-16 meeting, the one where it raised rates.
- Thursday, 1:00pm: $22B of 30-year bonds.

What would undo this afternoon: the 10-year back above Monday's 5.311% close, or an S&P 500 finish under 7,798.99. What would say the rally is widening: the small-company fund back above Monday's $283.38 close.

The rally passed its test on the bond market's terms: buyers took Washington's debt at the going rate, and the going rate is half a point higher than a month ago. Three-year money cleared without a fight. Wednesday asks the same buyers to lend for ten years near 5.27%, the rate mortgages follow, an hour before the Fed's own account of why it raised rates.

The clip hit the wires and the liberal machine did what the liberal machine does. Within hours a sitting California politician was treating a rambling aside about gas prices and an unfinished war as if the president had casually offered Los Angeles and San Diego up as acceptable losses. 

He had not. 

The words that actually left his mouth were the usual Trump stew, prices are high, the war is temporary, an unchecked Iran could hit a city, and the whole thing is still cheaper than the alternative, delivered in the same circular, half-finished cadence he uses for everything from tariffs to windmills. The edited version that traveled was cleaner, meaner, and far more useful.

That speed is the tell. No one waited for the transcript, the full sentence, or the White House clarification that the “small price” referred to the economic hit of stopping a nuclear program rather than to the cities themselves. The paraphrase was already circulating as a direct quote by the time most people had finished breakfast. 

It is an old trick, one that liberals are well-practiced in, isolate the alarming fragment, strip the surrounding clause, and hand the result to every elected official who needs a fresh outrage before the next news cycle. The synonym list for what follows; lie, smear, misrepresent, etc., is long but the behavior is routine. What changes is only the target and the deadline.

Plenty of voters have already noticed the pattern. Every time the same outlets and the same accounts perform the identical compression on a Trump sentence, a few more people stop treating the compressed version as the news and start treating it as what it is, lies.

text:
Does any victim ever get justice through the justice system?  

I will never forget the night my husband tried to kill me 15 years ago. The previous 7 years of his non-stop torture are still too difficult for me to talk about. I’m not sure whether it’s just too grotesque or I’m still ashamed. 

But that night, even when the police came, I was sure I was going to die. 

They weren’t talking to me. I was alone in the kitchen with a very young officer. I could hear the other officer talking to my husband in the living room about divorce and the conversation was winding up. Divorce? We hadn’t talked about divorce.  The officer wanted to buy our house if we got divorced. My life was on the line. 

I had hit record on my phone during the murder attempt — as the Domestic Violence Hotline suggested. I wasn’t sure how much video I’d captured as I’d been afraid to lift the phone. But I knew I’d captured my husband’s voice describing how he would dispose of my body after he dismembered me. 

I’d known for a while he was going to kill me. I’d been begging for help but there was none. At that point, I just wanted to leave enough evidence that would point to him. I wanted to make sure he didn’t do it to anyone else. 

As I heard the conversation in the living room wrap up, I asked the officer in the kitchen with me to watch the video. He ignored me. He was just standing still, looking at me. 

I got on my tippy toes and put my phone playing the video up to the face of the young officer. I was 4’11”. He was well over 6 feet. I found out later, he was only 7 days on the job, poor kid. 

I begged him to watch. He drew his gun, there was a click, and his gun was at my temple. He said something to me like “back off,” but I don’t remember the exact words. I didn’t care if he shot me. Better than my husband. 

Then something in the video caught his attention. I could sense there was a change. Without moving his gun, still staring into my eyes, he hit a button on his upper chest by his shoulder and spoke. There was static and background noise from the button. I know he said numbers and something about backup. But I can’t remember exactly. 

Time stood still for a minute or more. Then there was an older officer in the kitchen with me. The young officer called him “Sergeant,” as he took his gun from my temple.

The sergeant was very tall and strong. His uniform was neat and clean. He had a weathered face with skin the colour of milk chocolate, salt and pepper hair, and eyes that I will never forget. His gaze was intense but there was a kindness there. It’s funny the details you remember. I believed he would save my life. 

“Ma’am, you have a video?” he asked. His voice was deep, firm, but respectful. I trusted him. 

I picked up my phone and showed him. After it was done, he asked me to back part of it up. 

The next words he said always make me cry. “Ma’am you’ve been abused a long time, haven’t you? You are so calm.”  

He was  looking right into my eyes. There was so much compassion. He saw me. He knew what I’d been through. 

Tears stung my eyes and I bit my lip. I don’t cry in front of other people. But I wish I could have cried to that sergeant. I felt like he would understand. 

He went to the living room and spoke to my husband. Then he told him to stand up and turn around and told the other officer to cuff him. 

I never saw that sergeant again but I’ve never forgotten his eyes. He was a hero to me. That was my justice. 

My husband was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill. About a year later, the prosecutor offered him a plea of 6 weeks of anger management classes. 

So that moment with the sergeant *was* the only justice I got. 

I was bitter for a while. But it ate me up. I had to let it go. That sergeant did the best he could. Sometimes, that’s all you get. 

It’s Domestic Violence Awareness Month. I survived to tell this tale. Many women don’t survive. 

#domesticviolenceawareness

# Q3 2026 Prediction Markets Surge: Record Volumes, Community Innovation, and Academic Validation Point to Sector Maturity

Prediction markets have entered a new phase of growth and credibility. The third quarter of 2026 delivered an unprecedented $188 billion in trading volume—an all-time high that represents a 70 percent quarter-over-quarter increase and a 21-fold year-over-year expansion. This surge, fueled primarily by Kalshi’s regulatory expansion and Polymarket’s dominance in political event contracts, signals that these platforms are no longer niche experiments but serious tools for price discovery and risk management.

## Volume Explosion: Drivers and Implications

The headline figure of $188 billion did not emerge in isolation. Kalshi’s continued rollout of regulatory-approved event contracts attracted institutional and retail participants seeking compliant venues for election and economic outcomes. Polymarket, meanwhile, retained its edge in high-liquidity political markets, particularly around U.S. midterm and international election cycles. Together, these two platforms accounted for the majority of the reported volume.

This growth carries clear implications for market efficiency. Higher liquidity narrows bid-ask spreads, reduces slippage for large positions, and improves the accuracy of implied probabilities. Early data from the quarter already show tighter calibration between market prices and eventual resolutions in major races. For analysts and traders, the environment now supports more sophisticated strategies, including cross-market arbitrage between Polymarket and Kalshi on overlapping events.

## From Top-Down to Creator-Led: The Rise of Community and AI Models

Alongside volume growth, a structural shift is underway. Traditional platform-curated markets are giving way to creator- and community-driven contracts on niche topics such as crypto protocol disputes, esports tournaments, and entertainment awards. Platforms like XO and https://t.co/OYNoBGwNEs have emerged as early beneficiaries, offering lower barriers for market creation and community governance.

AI tooling is accelerating this transition. Automated settlement oracles, natural-language processing for news verification, and agentic systems that monitor real-world data feeds are reducing resolution disputes and latency. These developments address one of the historical pain points in prediction markets—subjective or delayed outcomes—and are drawing new capital from participants who previously avoided illiquid or ambiguous contracts.

The combination of community creation and AI settlement is not merely additive; it expands the addressable market. Topics once considered too granular for centralized platforms now support meaningful liquidity because AI can handle verification at scale. This evolution mirrors earlier shifts in DeFi, where permissionless innovation outpaced institutional gatekeeping.

## Academic Evidence Reinforces Real-World Value

Research released during the quarter provides independent validation. Studies revisiting the Iowa Electronic Markets continue to demonstrate that prediction markets outperform traditional polling in accuracy, particularly when markets incorporate continuous trading and skin-in-the-game incentives. An NBER paper examining PredictIt’s stake limits further highlights that artificial caps on position size can reduce information aggregation efficiency—an important data point for ongoing regulatory discussions.

These findings carry practical weight. Policymakers evaluating frameworks for event contracts can now reference both historical performance data and recent volume metrics. For traders, the academic literature supplies a stronger theoretical foundation for allocating capital to prediction markets as an asset class rather than a speculative sideshow.

## Regulatory Outlook and Liquidity Considerations

The volume surge and academic scrutiny are occurring against a backdrop of evolving regulation. Kalshi’s expansion under existing CFTC oversight has set a precedent, yet questions remain about stake limits, market access, and cross-border participation. The NBER analysis on PredictIt suggests that overly restrictive position sizing can impair price discovery, a point likely to feature in future comment periods.

Liquidity concentration remains another focal area. While overall volume is high, certain niche or long-tail markets still suffer from thin order books. Community platforms and AI settlement tools may alleviate this over time by lowering creation and resolution costs, but sustained growth will require continued product iteration from both established and emerging venues.

## Strategic Takeaways for Market Participants

For professional traders and analysts, the Q3 data underscore several priorities. First, monitoring Kalshi and Polymarket remains essential for macro and political probabilities, given their liquidity advantages. Second, tracking new community platforms offers early exposure to emerging narratives in crypto, sports, and culture. Third, integrating AI-assisted analysis tools can improve both trade timing and post-resolution review.

The sector’s trajectory now appears self-reinforcing: higher volumes attract more sophisticated participants, which in turn improves accuracy and draws further capital. Academic validation reduces regulatory uncertainty, while AI and community models broaden the product set.

## Looking Ahead

Q3 2026 has established a new baseline. The combination of record trading activity, technological innovation in market creation and settlement, and empirical research confirming superior forecasting performance positions prediction markets as a durable component of the information economy. Participants who adapt to the dual trends of regulatory-compliant scale and permissionless experimentation will be best placed to capture the next phase of growth.

As the fourth quarter unfolds, attention will turn to whether these momentum factors persist through election cycles and macroeconomic events. Early indications suggest the infrastructure and participant base are now robust enough to sustain elevated activity levels well beyond seasonal spikes.

This is for Dr Banks and his team at the Houston VA Hospital 

Subject: BRAVO ZULU – Recognition for Outstanding Neurosurgical and Postoperative Care

To the Leadership and Staff of the Department of Veterans Affairs:

I would like to take the opportunity to offer a sincere and well-deserved BRAVO ZULU to the physicians, nurses, medical technicians, support staff, and everyone involved in my care during my recent neurosurgery and postoperative recovery from September 2028 through October 3, 2028.

I underwent significant lower-spine surgery involving the L4-L5 and L5-S1 region, including a laminectomy. Anyone who has undergone this type of procedure knows that the surgery itself is only part of the experience. The hours and days afterward—when a patient is dealing with pain, limited mobility, uncertainty, and dependence upon others—are when the professionalism and compassion of the medical staff truly become apparent.

During that period, I had the opportunity to see firsthand the dedication of the men and women caring for America’s veterans.

I spent more than 23 years serving in the United States Marine Corps, including combat deployments, and I have spent much of my life around professionals who understand that their mission and the people beside them matter. I recognize professionalism, teamwork, and commitment when I see it.

I saw it in the VA personnel who cared for me.

From the neurosurgical team responsible for my procedure to the nurses and staff who cared for me afterward, I was treated with dignity, respect, patience, and genuine concern for my recovery. They were not simply performing jobs or completing medical tasks. They were taking care of a veteran during a particularly difficult and vulnerable period.

That distinction matters.

Too often, people are quick to write letters when something goes wrong, but we do not take enough time to recognize the people who quietly do their jobs exceptionally well every day. I believe outstanding service deserves to be acknowledged just as strongly.

I therefore ask that this letter be shared with the leadership responsible for the neurosurgery department, nursing staff, and postoperative care teams, and—most importantly—with the individual employees who were involved in my care. I would also appreciate this recognition being placed in their appropriate personnel or employee recognition channels whenever possible.

To everyone who participated in my surgery and recovery: thank you.

Thank you for your professionalism. Thank you for your patience. Thank you for treating me with dignity. And thank you for remembering that behind every hospital room number is a veteran who once served this country and who is now depending upon you.

You represented the Department of Veterans Affairs exceptionally well.

From one old Marine to the professionals who took care of me:

BRAVO ZULU. Mission accomplished, and a job exceptionally well done.

Semper Fidelis,

James E. Baldwin
First Sergeant, USMC (Retired)
United States Marine Corps
1983–2005

text:
A waitress walked outside holding two menus in her hand and placed them on the table between them. “What would you gentlemen like to drink?” She asked them, getting ready her pen and note pad. 

“Oh, I want a glass of red wine.” NuNew answered almost immediately. He felt like wine was the perfect beverage to warm him up in the cold Parisian weather.

“I’ll take a glass of wine too, thank you.” Zee offered the waitress a sweet smile. 

“Okay. I’ll let you decide on the food. I’ll be right back with your drinks.” 

Without saying anything else, she turned around and left. NuNew took the menu and started looking at the items on it, and after discussing it for a while with Zee, they decided on an assortment of charcuterie and cheese as a starter, a Parisienne toast and the Paysan cheese gratin. 

NuNew loved cheese, in fact, he could barely have any money for groceries, and he’d still buy cheese. He felt like he couldn’t live without it, and that was the main reason NuNew chose this restaurant. As soon as he saw their specialty was gratins, he was sold on the idea of eating there. 

But of course, the official version he gave Zee when he was asked was because of the views and the proximity to Notre Dame. He had just met Zee, but he knew it in his heart that if the tour guide found out about his obsession with cheese, he’d nickname him the Cheese Monster and that was the last thing NuNew wanted. 

Once the food was on the table, and after some small talk to break the ice, Zee cleared his throat. 

“I have a very important question to ask you.” 

NuNew got nervous after the shift in Zee's tone and unconsciously straightened his spine as he waited for the question. 

“Why were you on TV? Imagine my shock last night when I turned on DMax and saw your face on my screen. I didn't know I had met someone famous!” 

“Pfft! Famous! You’re exaggerating! The reason I was on that program was because the producers were looking for new faces, people who’d be recognized by the younger audiences, and since I have a good following on Instagram and after seeing my investigation work, they contacted me. That’s really it. I’m not special or anything.” 

“The more I learn about you, the more impressed I am. You really caught my interest with your explanations. I bet you’re very famous among your students.” Zee took a piece of cheese and brought it to his mouth to take a bite. NuNew’s eyes followed the movement, trying not to stare for too long at Zee’s lips before looking up at his eyes. 

“I don't think so. I’m a good teacher, but I am also very strict. I think most of my students hate me.” 

“Not necessarily. Your father was also very strict and yet, most of us loved him. At least I did. He was my favorite professor.” 

NuNew’s fork froze mid way to his mouth as soon as he heard the mention of his father. “You were his student? Didn't you study here in Paris?” 

“I finished my degree in Paris and also got my master’s degree here, but my first two years were in Bangkok. It was actually your father who helped me get a scholarship for the Sorbonne.” 

“Oh! Well, that’s great. How did you know who my father was, though? I am a bit freaked out.” 

“Your full name was on the documentary.” Zee answered with a chuckle, and NuNew immediately went red with embarrassment. 

“Forget I asked.” NuNew mumbled before laughing it off. Zee made him nervous in all the right ways, and he felt dumb around him. He kept wondering what was it about that man to have such an effect on him.

“How is your father doing, by the way?” 

NuNew found it endearing that Zee wanted to know about his former professor and a warm smile appeared on his face as he started updating him.

text:
Iran War Day 221 — Sitrep Watch | How Tehran Hires in London: The Fairford Chain Analysis

October 6, 2026 UTC

Pinned indicators: 

https://t.co/XWhJ9iNv1N

This is a hypothetical. It reconstructs how an Iranian order and Iranian money reach a group of young men in London, built from how documented Iranian operations in Europe have run and fitted to the published Fairford facts. Each link states what is on the record and what is inference.

1. NEWS
Seven men have been arrested in the RAF Fairford investigation. Five British men aged 23 to 25, from Westminster, Camden and Willesden, were arrested beside three vans near the base on September 27. A sixth, a 25-year-old British-Iranian from Westminster, was arrested on October 1. A seventh, a 22-year-old British national, was arrested in Westminster on October 6 on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. The first six are on bail. No one has been charged. Prime Minister Burnham says there are “strong indications that Iran played a part.” Tehran denies it.

2. ANALYSIS — THE CHAIN
a. The tasking. An IRGC element is given the objective: get the bombers out of Britain. The timing follows a fresh bomber rotation, which spotters publish within hours. On the record: Tasnim named Fairford a legitimate target in July. Inference: the tasking.
b. The controller, outside Britain. A handler in Iran or a third country runs the job over an encrypted app and never meets the men. On the record: in the Heaton Park synagogue case, prosecutors allege a third party in Iran “directed and coordinated” the plot. RFE/RL describes the same structure: “a controller, a multilayered system, a cell leader.”
c. The cutout in London. The controller works through one trusted person on the ground with ties to Iran and local standing. The sixth suspect is the kind of person who fills that role. On the record: his arrest, age, nationality and address. Inference: the role. He has not been charged.
d. The recruitment. The cutout does not post an advert. He goes to people he knows. Three of the five live in Westminster, the others in Camden and Willesden, all aged 23 to 25. That is a friend group hired together through one contact, not five strangers answering Telegram separately. On the record: addresses and ages. Inference: the friend group.
e. The cover story. The men are offered a paid job: drive three vans, carry drums, park at a location at 1:30 a.m., wear masks. They are told it is a protest stunt, an arson job or a delivery. They are not told who is paying. On the record: an official called them “unwitting chumps.” Analysts told Al Jazeera they were probably “paid online to do some naughty work.”
f. The money. A few thousand pounds each, plus three vans and petrol. The whole operation costs in the low tens of thousands of pounds. It moves as cash from the cutout or as cryptocurrency, in amounts too small to trip a bank. On the record: the terrorism-law reviewer, Jonathan Hall KC, puts such gigs at “several thousand pounds,” advertised on Telegram as “Do you fancy a gig?” Inference: the total.
g. The trigger. A call reaches police at 12:45 a.m. about three vehicles heading for the base. Three newspapers say it came from one of the men. Police say “a member of the public.” Either he was told to call, which makes the five a decoy, or he realized what he was part of.
h. The second layer. A farmer saw eight to ten masked men. Five were arrested. A week later came the threat President Trump referred to: “We actually know the people who made the threat.” On the record: the witness count and the statement. Not known: what the other men were doing, or who they are.
i. The result. Twelve bombers leave. The hired men are bailed: the vans held mostly empty drums and a quantity of petrol, and no device.

3. ANALYSIS — WHERE THE SEVENTH ARREST FITS
The seventh man is 22, British, and was arrested in Westminster, the same borough as the sixth suspect and three of the five. He fits link c, a second contact on the ground, or link d, a hired hand who was not at Whelford. Not known: which.
The job was hired out of London, from its violence-for-hire ecosystem. Three arrests in ten days in Westminster show it. The village beside the base was the job.

4. ANALYSIS — WHAT CONFIRMS OR BREAKS THE CHAIN
a. The phones. Whether the five were messaging one local contact or an anonymous account.
b. The vans. Who rented or bought them, and how they were paid for. One was branded “Fuel2You” in red, a near-copy of Fuel2U, a real company that delivers fuel to farms and businesses in green livery. The name was not real and neither was the phone number. Fuel2U says it has no link to the vans. One report says two details look Iranian: the number on the van, 0742 418 2599, is spaced in a style more common in Iran than in Britain, and its red logo matches the colour of Iranian petrol pumps. Both are uncorroborated at this point. Why is not known. The sign calls the van out, and a fake number calls it out further to anyone who checks it. In farm country, where fuel theft from tanks is a known crime, a fuel van on a back road at night signals ill intent. Someone ordered that sign, and that order is a trail.
c. The sixth and seventh suspects. Whether either knew the five before September.
d. The missing men. Whether anyone has identified the three to five who ran.
e. The alternative. The five were hired cold online with no local cutout, as in other European cases. The shared neighborhoods argue against it. Nothing published rules it out.

Per grok, Nickelodeon has been a problem since its inception. 
“This is a sensitive topic that mixes documented industry problems with individual struggles, allegations, and later life outcomes. Public reporting focuses on a handful of Nickelodeon child performers whose experiences involved abuse, workplace conditions, mental-health crises, or legal issues—not a general pattern that applies to the cast as a whole.
The most substantiated cases involve both the network’s production environment and the performers’ own later difficulties.
Drake Bell (Drake & Josh, and earlier All That / The Amanda Show) has publicly described being sexually abused as a teenager by Brian Peck, a dialogue coach and actor who worked on Nickelodeon productions. Peck pleaded no contest in 2004 to charges involving a minor and was sentenced to prison; the victim’s identity was sealed for years and Bell later identified himself in the 2024 Investigation Discovery series Quiet on Set. Bell has also had his own legal problems as an adult, including a 2021 guilty plea in Ohio related to attempted child endangerment and disseminating matter harmful to juveniles (stemming from interactions with an underage fan); he received probation.
Amanda Bynes (All That, The Amanda Show) was a major Nickelodeon star in the late 1990s and early 2000s. In her twenties she experienced a widely reported series of mental-health crises, substance issues, arrests (including DUI and hit-and-run incidents), and a conservatorship that lasted from 2013 until 2022. She has spoken about the pressures of early fame; coverage has not established that Nickelodeon production staff abused her, but her trajectory is one of the more public post-child-star collapses.
Jennette McCurdy (iCarly, Sam & Cat) detailed in her 2022 memoir I’m Glad My Mom Died an abusive relationship with her mother, eating disorders, and what she described as uncomfortable on-set experiences and career pressure while working on Nickelodeon shows produced by Dan Schneider. She has said she was offered hush money related to her experiences; Schneider has denied wrongdoing. McCurdy left acting and has described the period as damaging rather than as a criminal case against the network.
Broader context from Quiet on Set and related reporting includes other former child performers describing a high-pressure environment, inappropriate jokes or behavior by adults on sets associated with Schneider, and at least one additional convicted abuser (Jason Handy, a production assistant, who pleaded guilty to lewd acts with a minor and related charges). Schneider left Nickelodeon in 2018 after an internal investigation; he has denied sexual misconduct allegations. Nickelodeon and parent company Paramount have said they take such claims seriously and have pointed to changed practices.
Other former child actors associated with the network have spoken about ordinary difficulties of early fame (typecasting, loss of privacy, uneven adult careers) without documented abuse or criminal outcomes. Many others have had ordinary or successful adult lives. Claims circulating on social media often blend confirmed court records and firsthand accounts with rumor; the clearest primary sources remain court documents, the performers’ own statements, and the investigative reporting around Quiet on Set”

text:
Have you actually never heard of the Bengal Famine? Or the 1960s PL-480 crisis when India was literally surviving "ship-to-mouth" on foreign food aid? The Green Revolution was aggressively pushed in Punjab by the central government specifically because the rest of the country was starving. The FCI doesn’t procure Punjab's rice out of charity because "no state will buy them"; they procure it because it forms the massive backbone of the National Food Security Act, keeping 800 million impoverished citizens alive through the PDS. If Punjab stopped growing it tomorrow, the national food buffer would collapse.

Now let's address your "Farm Laws would bring competitive international prices" fantasy. If an unregulated free market magically makes farmers rich and diversifies crops, explain Bihar. Bihar abolished its APMC mandi system in 2006 to let farmers sell directly on the open market. Did they get "competitive prices"? No. Their agricultural economy collapsed, and today Bihar's farmers are among the poorest in the nation, routinely forced to sell their crops at throwaway prices to middlemen who just smuggle them into Punjab to sell at MSP.

The repealed Farm Laws offered zero legal guarantees or price floors (MSP) for alternative crops like pulses or oilseeds. Expecting a farmer with a few acres to drop a secure crop and gamble his entire livelihood on the unregulated whims of corporate buyers without a guaranteed safety net isn't basic economics; it is economic suicide.

text:
Ottawa Senators vs Detroit Red Wings — momentum against a second night on the road

Preview · NHL · Regular season · Tuesday 6 October 2026

Ottawa come into Little Caesars Arena unbeaten and travelling well. Detroit come in without a point and without many goals. The complication is the calendar: the Senators played in Boston on Monday, while the Red Wings have been home since Sunday. That is the whole tension of this game, and form edges it.

THE MATCHUP

Seven points separated the teams over 2025-26. Ottawa finished on 99 points at 44-27-11, sixth in the Eastern Conference; Detroit finished on 92 at 41-31-10, tenth. That is not a gap worth leaning on.

Up front, Ottawa's current roster is led by Tim Stützle, who had 34 goals and 83 points last season, and Drake Batherson with 33 goals and 71 points. Detroit have Alex DeBrincat (41 goals, 85 points), Lucas Raymond (76 points) and Dylan Larkin (34 goals, 67 points). Brady Tkachuk, who had 59 points for Ottawa last season, is not on the current roster listing; neither is Patrick Kane, who had 57 for Detroit.

FORM & CONTEXT

This is where the teams part ways. Ottawa closed last season 6-3-1 over their last ten games; Detroit closed it 2-6-2. The opening week has carried both trends on. Ottawa won 3-2 in Toronto and 4-1 in Boston, seven goals for and three against. Detroit lost 2-0 at home to the Rangers and 3-2 at home to Winnipeg on Sunday — two goals in two games.

The goaltending tells the same story. Linus Ullmark has a .949 save percentage and a 1.20 goals-against average from two games, both wins. John Gibson has done his part for Detroit, at .915 in two games, but has no win to show for it. Daniil Tarasov is also on Detroit's current roster listing; his 2025-26 numbers (.895 over 33 games) came with Florida.

Last season's meetings went Detroit's way, three wins to one. Detroit won 5-3 in Ottawa in January, 4-3 in overtime at home later that month and 2-1 in overtime in Ottawa in February; Ottawa won the most recent meeting, 3-2 in Detroit in March. Two of Detroit's three wins needed overtime, which softens the edge.

THE DECIDING FACTOR

The schedule. Ottawa are on the second night of a back-to-back, on the road, after Monday's win in Boston. Detroit last played on Sunday and are at home, where they were 21-16-4 last season; Ottawa were 21-15-5 on the road. Everything outside current form points at the Red Wings.

Against that stands a Detroit team that has not scored more than two goals in a game this season and finished last season winning two of its last ten. Ottawa's start, and the goaltending behind it, is the stronger evidence — but not by enough to lean hard.

THE CALL

Ottawa are the better side in form and in goal. Detroit have home ice, rest, and last season's meetings. One strong argument against three that offer the Senators nothing, or worse, makes this a lean rather than a conviction.

Ottawa Senators to win, low confidence.

The forested landscape, which includes ponderosa pine forest, open meadows and Gonzalez Lake, will become a new public open space and outdoor recreation area for residents and visitors alike.

Located adjacent to Interstate 40 and sharing a 1.5-mile boundary with the Kaibab National Forest, Gonzalez Ranch offers significant opportunities for outdoor recreation, preservation and public access. Future uses may include recreational trails connecting to the nearby national forest lands, outdoor education and wildlife and nature viewing.
